# Smart Fleet pilot test cases

**Date:** 2026-10-25 · **Cases:** 566 (P1 266 · P2 275 · P3 25) · **Branch:** `pilot/happy-path`

These cases test the whole Smart Fleet pilot as the docs in this folder describe it, Increments 1 to 3: money and expenses, orders and drivers, the one-holder rule, customer confirmation, refills, day-end, setup, quality and migrations, and the rehearsal day.

## How to use it

### Who runs which cases

| Type | What it is | Who runs it | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUTO-UNIT | A pure function, or a service with mocks | Developers, and CI | `npm test` (see below) |
| AUTO-API | HTTP calls against a real test database | Developers, and CI | `npm run test:e2e` (see below) |
| MAN-SHOP | The shop app on an Android phone | A tester signed in as Ahmed Gas (or Bilal Gas) | Test server |
| MAN-DRIVER | The driver app on an Android phone | A tester signed in as Kashif (or Imran) | Test server |
| MAN-WEB | The office website in Chrome on a laptop | An office user (Owner or Ops) | Test server |
| MAN-PAGE | The customer link page in a phone browser | A tester playing the customer | Test server |
| MAN-OPS | Work outside the apps: the bank app, a command line, the server or the database | Engineering or operations | Test server |

Manual cases are written for people who don't read code: do the steps in order and compare what you see with "Expect". Automated cases are for developers and can be technical.

### Priorities

- **P1**: must pass before every release.
- **P1 + P2**: must pass before the rehearsal day.
- **P3**: polish. Fix it when there is time. A P3 failure never blocks a release.

Run the cases of every increment a release contains: Inc 1 from the first release, Inc 2 once the driver flow ships, and Inc 3 once refills on scans and day-end ship. The earlier increments' cases keep running in every later release.

### What each case says

- **Before**: what must be true before you start: the data, the settings, who is signed in.
- **Steps**: what to do, in order.
- **Expect**: what must happen. "Step 2: …" is the result of step 2. Amounts, words on screen and error codes must match exactly.
- **Spec**: the decisions (ADR-nn in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md)) and the doc sections the case checks.
- **Test file**: for an automated case, the file its test lives in (a suggested path until the test is written).
- **Note**: background for the tester, such as why a step is there or which fixture it needs. Every question the cases raised about the docs has been settled; the decisions are listed at the end, under [Spec questions and how they were settled](#spec-questions-and-how-they-were-settled).

### Recording results in the CSV

[TEST_CASES.csv](TEST_CASES.csv) has one row per case, with the same IDs and text as this page. It is UTF-8 with a BOM, so Excel shows "Rs", "×" and "→" correctly.

1. Make a copy for each test run, for example `2026-10-25-inc1-rc1.csv`, and open it in Excel or Google Sheets.
2. Fill in only the last four columns:
   - **Result**: `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED` (you couldn't run it; say why in Comments) or `N/A` (not in this build).
   - **Tested by**: your name.
   - **Date**: the day you ran it, as YYYY-MM-DD.
   - **Comments**: the app version or build you tested. For a FAIL, add the step number, what you saw and the name of your screenshot. For an automated case, add the CI run link.
3. Don't change the case columns. If a case itself looks wrong, say so in Comments and tell the test lead.
4. A FAIL on a P1 case stops the release until it is fixed and the case passes again.

## How to run the automated tests

The automated tests live in `apps/api/test`, plus the pure-function tests of the shared packages (`packages/*/src/__tests__`), which the API's unit run includes. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the API unit tests and database tests, with PostGIS and Redis services, on pull requests to `main` and on pushes to `main` and `claude/**`.

1. Start the test database (PostgreSQL with PostGIS on port 55432) and Redis (port 56379). Their data lives in memory, so every `down` and `up` starts clean.

   ```sh
   docker compose -f infrastructure/docker-compose.test.yml up -d
   ```

2. Unit tests (`*.spec.ts`, no database), from `apps/api`:

   ```sh
   npm test
   ```

3. Database tests (`*.e2e-spec.ts`), from `apps/api`:

   ```sh
   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://smartfleet:smartfleet_test@localhost:55432/smartfleet_test \
   REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:56379 \
   npm run test:e2e
   ```

   In PowerShell:

   ```powershell
   $env:DATABASE_URL = "postgresql://smartfleet:smartfleet_test@localhost:55432/smartfleet_test"
   $env:REDIS_URL = "redis://localhost:56379"
   npm run test:e2e
   ```

   - The run first brings the database to the current migrations (`prisma migrate deploy`). `E2E_DB_RESET=1` rebuilds it from scratch instead.
   - Every suite empties the tables before it starts, so the tests refuse a database whose name doesn't contain "test". Give each developer a database of their own, for example `docker exec smartfleet-postgres-test psql -U smartfleet -d smartfleet_test -c "CREATE DATABASE sf_mine_test"`.
   - Without `DATABASE_URL`, the database suites are skipped.

4. Run one case, or one file:

   ```sh
   npm run test:e2e -- -t "FEE-009"
   npm run test:e2e -- test/orders/fees.e2e-spec.ts
   ```

5. Also part of these runs:
   - The migration suites in `apps/api/test/migrations` run with the other database suites (`npm run test:e2e -- test/migrations` runs only them). Their helpers build old-style and fresh scratch databases and drop them afterwards.
   - `npm test` in `apps/api` also runs the shared packages' tests (`packages/*/src/__tests__`). The mobile app has no test runner of its own: its rules are checked by API unit tests that load the app's modules (for example UXQ-011 and UXQ-015).
   - The nightly wallet check after all database suites (WAL-020): `test/money/wallet-check.teardown.ts`, the `globalTeardown` of `test/jest-e2e.json`. It fails the run when any wallet's ledger sum differs from its balance.

The "Test file" of an automated case lists the files whose test names start with its ID. A regression case for an Increment 1 review finding (its note names the finding) lists instead the files whose test names start with "REV" and that finding, of its own kind: API cases the database suites, unit cases the others. A case whose note names a describe block ("Its tests are the describe …") lists the files that hold that describe, in the same way. An automated case with no such test yet keeps the path its writer suggested and is marked "Not automated yet." in its note.

**Test names start with the case ID**, so a failing test points straight at its case here and in the CSV:

```ts
it('FEE-009 X3: the distributor cancels before the first load scan and gets Rs 480 back', async () => {
  // …
});
```

Keep IDs stable once tests use them: a new case takes the next free number in its area, and a removed case's number is never reused.

### Worked money examples

| Example | What happens | Delivery cost | Ahmed Gas balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Ahmed Gas orders 2 × 11.8 kg + 1 × 45.4 kg for Sana (North) | Rs 250 + 2 × Rs 40 + Rs 150 = **Rs 480** | Rs 5,000 → Rs 4,520 |
| X2 | Ahmed Gas orders 3 × 15 kg for Usman (South) | Flat **Rs 400** | after X1: Rs 4,520 → Rs 4,120 |
| X3 | X1 is cancelled **before** the first load scan | Rs 480 returned, exactly once | back to Rs 5,000 |
| X3, late | X1 is cancelled **after** the first load scan | Nothing returned | stays Rs 4,520 |
| X4 | The balance is exactly Rs 480 and Ahmed Gas places X1 | Rs 480 | Rs 480 → Rs 0 |
| X4, short | The balance is Rs 479 | Refused: 409 WALLET_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, short by Rs 1; nothing is created or deducted | stays Rs 479 |
| Y1 | Ahmed Gas orders 1 × 11.8 kg for Usman (South) | Flat **Rs 400** | |

Other totals the cases use: X1 + Y1 leaves Rs 4,120; X1 + X2 + Y1 leaves Rs 3,720; five X1 orders leave Rs 2,600; a quote for 10 × 15 kg in North is Rs 250 + 10 × Rs 80 = Rs 1,050. The rehearsal day ends at Rs 5,430, with Rs 1,570 of delivery costs taken.

Money moves only four ways: an approved top-up, the delivery cost taken when an order is placed, its return on a cancel before delivery has started, and an office correction for a genuine mistake. There are no holds, no charge on delivery, no refund once delivery has started, no refill money and no refund for a customer's "Not received". The cases that touch these prove they are off.

## FND · Platform foundations

The public app config, the settings registry, the error envelope and catalogue, the app-version gate, the audit log, files, idempotency, health checks, daily-job time zones and the shared-utils helpers. 41 cases: P1 13 · P2 25 · P3 3.

### FND-001 · GET /app/config works without a token and returns the default public settings

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: PUBLIC (not signed in)

Before: Fresh test database with all migrations applied and no rows in app_settings, so every setting is at its registry default. API started with APP_ENV=test.

Steps:

1. Send GET /api/v1/app/config with no Authorization header and no X-App-\* headers.
2. Send the same request again with the header Authorization: Bearer garbage.
3. Compare the body with the registry defaults in API_CONTRACT §6.

Expect:

- Both requests return 200 with a PublicAppConfig body and an X-Request-Id header. The bad token is ignored on this public route.
- features: autoAssign false, transfers false, fuelRefills false, accessories false, support false, clientApp false, refills true, scanFlow true, confirmations false, dayEnd true, typedCylinderNumber true, languageSwitch false. scanFlow and typedCylinderNumber are true from Inc 2 and dayEnd from Inc 3; an Inc 1 build gives all three false.
- minVersion is { driver: "0.0.0", distributor: "0.0.0" }; orders is { maxCylindersPerOrder: 30, deliveryStartedAt: "FIRST_LOAD_SCAN" }; refill.maxCylinders is 30; day is { timezone: "Asia/Karachi", cutoffLocalTime: "03:00" }.
- Money is sent as digit strings: topup.minPaisa "50000", topup.maxPaisa "5000000", topup.quickAmountsPaisa ["200000", "500000", "1000000"], wallet.lowBalancePaisa "100000". wallet.capPaisa is null. topup.checkingHours is { from: "09:00", to: "21:00" }.
- support is { phone: null, whatsApp: null, hours: "9am–9pm" }; environment is "test"; training is false; links.updateUrl is null.
- The body holds no non-public setting: no lockedRoles, otpLogin, onAmountMismatch, maxPendingPerDistributor, secondApproval, refill deliveryCost or deliveryStrategy, and no company account title or IBAN.

Spec: ADR-03; ADR-04; ADR-12; ADR-21; API_CONTRACT §1.1, §1.2, §5.2, §6, §7.1 · Test file: `apps/api/test/foundation/app-config.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: The docs don't say a bad token on a public route is ignored; assumed, so a phone holding an old token can still read the update gate. topup.account is public only to distributors (served by GET /payments/topup-info, not here). Money fields in PublicAppConfig are assumed to follow §1.1 (digit strings).

### FND-002 · A settings change is audited and used by the very next request

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (SA1)

Before: Standard data. DA balance Rs 5,000. C1 "Sana" has a priced address in North. orders.maxCylindersPerOrder is at its default, 30.

Steps:

1. As SA1, GET /api/v1/settings and read the row for orders.maxCylindersPerOrder.
2. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.maxCylindersPerOrder with { value: 5, reason: "Rehearsal limit test" }. Note the X-Request-Id of the response.
3. Without a token, GET /api/v1/app/config.
4. As DA, POST /api/v1/orders with a new Idempotency-Key for C1 with one line of 6 × 11.8 kg (expectedReturnCount 6).
5. As DA, POST /api/v1/orders/quote for C1 with 5 × 11.8 kg.
6. As SA1, GET /api/v1/audit-logs?action=setting.update.
7. As SA1, PATCH the same key back to 30 with reason "Restore default after test".

Expect:

- Step 1: the row is { key: "orders.maxCylindersPerOrder", value: 30, default: 30, type: int, min: 1, max: 100, editable: true, public: true } with no updatedBy.
- Step 2: 200 with the updated row: value 5, updatedBy SA1 ("Owner"), updatedAt set.
- Step 3: orders.maxCylindersPerOrder is 5.
- Step 4: 400 ORDER_TOO_MANY_CYLINDERS with message "Too many cylinders. An order can have at most 5." No order is created and DA's balance is still Rs 5,000 (GET /wallet balancePaisa "500000").
- Step 5: 200 with quote.totalPaisa "45000" (Rs 250 + 5 × Rs 40 = Rs 450) and wallet.enough true.
- Step 6: one setting.update row with actor { kind: USER, userId: SA1, name: "Owner" }, resourceType setting, reason "Rehearsal limit test", diff { key: "orders.maxCylindersPerOrder", from: 30, to: 5 } (resource_id is a UUID column, so the key is in the diff), and the requestId noted in step 2.
- Step 7: the value is 30 again, and a second setting.update row records the change from 5 to 30.

Spec: ADR-23; API_CONTRACT §2.3 (ORDER_TOO_MANY_CYLINDERS), §5.2, §5.3, §6, §7.5 (POST /orders/quote), §7.6 (rule 3), §7.13; Appendix B (setting.update) · Test file: `apps/api/test/foundation/settings.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: SettingsService.set() clears the 30-second cache when it commits, and the pilot runs one API instance (ADR-23), so step 4 sees the new limit at once (API_CONTRACT §5.2). The details key behind {{max}} is max (§2.3).

### FND-003 · A refused settings change changes nothing and writes no audit row

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (SA1)

Before: All settings at their defaults, except topup.account, which the settings CLI set to the dummy company account (title "Smart Fleet (Pvt) Ltd", IBAN PK00TEST0000000000000000). Count the setting.update audit rows.

Steps:

1. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.maxCylindersPerOrder with value 0, then 101, then "abc", each with reason "Boundary test".
2. PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.deliveryStartedAt with { value: "ON_DELIVERY", reason: "Bad value test" }.
3. PATCH /api/v1/settings/app.minVersion.distributor with { value: "1.0", reason: "Bad version test" }.
4. PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.maxCylindersPerOrder with { value: 20 } and no reason; then with reason "abc" (3 characters).
5. PATCH /api/v1/settings/orders.notARealKey with { value: 1, reason: "Unknown key test" }.
6. PATCH /api/v1/settings/topup.account with another account ({ accountTitle: "Someone Else", bankName: "Other Bank", iban: "PK00OTHR0000000000000001", accountNumber: "1" }) and a reason. Then try pricing.deliveryStrategy, refill.deliveryCost, topup.secondApproval and auth.otpLogin.enabled { value: true } the same way.
7. As SA1, GET /api/v1/settings and GET /api/v1/audit-logs?action=setting.update. As DA, GET /api/v1/payments/topup-info.

Expect:

- Steps 1–3: 400 SETTING_INVALID_VALUE "This value isn't allowed here." for every request.
- Step 4: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields naming reason, for both requests.
- Step 5: 404 SETTING_UNKNOWN "Unknown setting."
- Step 6: 403 SETTING_NOT_EDITABLE "This setting can't be changed here." for all five keys.
- Step 7: every value is unchanged (maxCylindersPerOrder 30, deliveryStartedAt FIRST_LOAD_SCAN, app.minVersion.distributor "0.0.0", auth.otpLogin.enabled false). No new setting.update rows. DA still sees the account "Smart Fleet (Pvt) Ltd" with IBAN PK00TEST0000000000000000.

Spec: ADR-09; ADR-16; API_CONTRACT §2.3 (Settings and legacy), §5.2, §6, §7.9 (GET /payments/topup-info), §7.13 · Test file: `apps/api/test/foundation/settings.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Each request carries one fault only, because the docs don't say which check wins when a body has both a bad value and a missing reason. The reason length 5–300 is from §7.13. The 1–100 range for maxCylindersPerOrder is taken as inclusive.

5. Pass P2002 on orders_distributor_id_client_request_id_key and on ledger_entries_idempotency_key_key.

Expect:

- Step 4: 200 with Idempotent-Replay: true and the same order. Balance still Rs 0.

2. Send that cursor to GET /wallet/statement and /orders?tab=done as DA, and to /orders/board?tab=all, /admin/topups?tab=all and /audit-logs as SA1.
3. As DA, GET /orders?tab=active&limit=1&cursor=\<it>.

Expect:

- Step 2: each 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on cursor (code INVALID_VALUE).
- Step 3: 200 with the other order and nextCursor null.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §1.3 · Test file: `apps/api/test/foundation/rev-foreign-cursor.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding contract-compat-03 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV contract-compat-03 …". The cursor carries a tag of the list that made it: its path and its tab. A cursor issued before the tag existed gets this 400 once after the deploy. Unit tests: apps/api/test/unit/rev-cursor-lists.spec.ts.

### FND-037 · A deploy's shutdown lets a request in flight finish before the database closes

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA)

Before: Standard test data. DA Rs 5,000. Another database session has locked DA's row, as a racing request would.

Steps:

1. As DA, POST /orders (X1) with an Idempotency-Key; it waits on the row lock.
2. Start the shutdown (app.close(), as a deploy's SIGTERM does), then release the lock 1.5 seconds later.

Expect:

- Step 1: the order is still waiting when the shutdown starts.
- Step 2: the order answers 201 and is committed: one order, DA's balance Rs 4,520; the shutdown then completes.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §4 (state changes are atomic; a retry uses the same key) · Test file: `apps/api/test/review/robustness-ops/graceful-shutdown.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding robustness-ops-05 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV robustness-ops-05 …". PrismaService and the rate limiter close their clients in onApplicationShutdown, after the HTTP server has drained, and compose gives each API service 30 seconds to stop (apps/api/test/unit/rev-graceful-shutdown.spec.ts). Before the fix the order answered 503.

### FND-038 · A value Postgres can't store answers 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, never 500

**P2** · AUTO-UNIT · Inc 1 · Role: DEVELOPER

Before: Unit tests of the shared text and date schemas, the cursor decoder and the central error mapping.

Steps:

1. Parse a text and a search value holding a NUL character (U+0000).
2. Parse ISO instants in the year 0000 and with a six-digit year; decode cursors holding such dates.
3. Map data exceptions that still reach the database: P2010 with SQLSTATE 22021, 22P05, 22008, 22003 or 22001; P2000; P2033; "Could not convert argument value"; and 22P02.

Expect:

- Step 1: INVALID_VALUE on the field.
- Step 2: INVALID_DATETIME; each cursor gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on cursor.
- Step 3: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields [], logged as a warning and not sent to Sentry; 22P02 stays 404 NOT_FOUND.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §1.3, §2.2 · Test file: `apps/api/test/unit/rev-bad-input-mapping.spec.ts, apps/api/test/unit/rev-cursor-lists.spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding robustness-ops-06 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV robustness-ops-06 …". The routes are checked over HTTP by apps/api/test/review/robustness-ops/bad-input-500.e2e-spec.ts and fuzz-inc1.e2e-spec.ts: no 5xx anywhere.

### FND-039 · A body the parser refuses answers 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, logged at debug and never sent to Sentry

**P3** · AUTO-UNIT · Inc 1 · Role: DEVELOPER

Before: Unit test of the central error mapping with the http-errors objects the body parser throws.

Steps:

1. Map request.aborted (400), entity.too.large (413), charset.unsupported and encoding.unsupported (415), and a bad gzip body.
2. Map a 5xx http-errors object and a plain Error.

Expect:

- Step 1: each 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields [], at log level debug, with no Sentry capture.
- Step 2: 500 INTERNAL_ERROR at log level error.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §2.2 · Test file: `apps/api/test/unit/rev-bad-input-mapping.spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding robustness-ops-07 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV robustness-ops-07 …". A phone that drops the connection mid-body no longer writes an error line with a stack (apps/api/test/review/robustness-ops/bad-input-500.e2e-spec.ts).

### FND-040 · While Redis is down, queue and worker errors are one warning a minute through the logger

**P3** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DEVELOPER

Before: The API booted as main.ts does, with REDIS_URL pointing at a port where nothing listens.

Steps:

1. Let the dispatch queue and worker try to reconnect for 4 seconds, then read the log; GET /api/v1/health/live.

Expect:

- Step 1: at most one warning per queue and per worker ("queue dispatch: …", "worker dispatch: …") through the Nest logger, no console.error stack dumps, and the API answers 200.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §3.6 · Test file: `apps/api/test/foundation/rev-queue-errors.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding robustness-ops-14 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV robustness-ops-14 …". Before the fix BullMQ printed every reconnect failure as a multi-line stack dump, about 109 lines a minute.

### FND-041 · Every request writes one log line with its route pattern, status, time, request id and user

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA)

Before: Standard test data.

Steps:

1. As DA, GET /api/v1/orders/\<an unknown id>?phone=03001234567 with X-Request-Id rev-log-0000001.
2. Without a token, GET /api/v1/health/live (rev-log-0000002) and GET /api/v1/wallet (rev-log-0000003).

Expect:

- Step 1: one line "GET /api/v1/orders/:id 404 \<n>ms requestId=rev-log-0000001 userId=\<DA's user>".
- Step 2: "GET /api/v1/health/live 200 …" and "GET /api/v1/wallet 401 …", each with its requestId. No line contains the query string or the id from the path.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §2.2 (Logs), §5.3; UX_ADMIN §1.7 (ErrorState Reference) · Test file: `apps/api/test/foundation/rev-request-log.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding robustness-ops-15 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV robustness-ops-15 …". Lines are JSON through pino, with LOG_LEVEL and redaction (apps/api/test/unit/rev-logging.spec.ts).

## SEC · Security and roles

Sign-in, tokens and sessions, locked roles, exact roles, ownership (another shop's data gives 404), the driver socket, secrets that never leave, CORS, boot guards, switched-off modules and user accounts. 36 cases: P1 28 · P2 8 · P3 0.

### SEC-001 · A distributor signs in with the phone typed in any normal form

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA)

Before: DA's user is ACTIVE and has a password. Use DA's sign-in number from the test data sheet.

Steps:

1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with X-App-Variant: distributor and { phone: DA's number in local form with a space ("03xx xxxxxxx"), password }.
2. Decode the access token's claims.
3. Sign in again with the number typed as "+923xxxxxxxxx" and as "03xx-xxxxxxx".
4. GET /api/v1/auth/me and GET /api/v1/users/me with the access token.

Expect:

- Step 1: 200 { accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn, role: "DISTRIBUTOR" }, the same shape as today.
- Step 2: sub is DA's user id, role is DISTRIBUTOR, distributorId is DA's id, driverId is empty, and tv equals users.token_version.
- Step 3: 200 both times.
- Step 4: 200 with DA's profile. Neither body contains passwordHash, cnic, cnicEncrypted, cnicIndex, codeHash or tokenHash at any depth.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §3.3, §3.5, §7.1, §7.2 (GET /auth/me, GET /users/me), Appendix A; UX_MOBILE S1 · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/auth-login.e2e-spec.ts, apps/api/test/security/security-units.spec.ts`

Note: The standard test data doesn't fix the users' sign-in numbers; take them from the test data sheet.

### SEC-002 · An unknown phone or a wrong password is refused the same way, and no account is created

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: PUBLIC (not signed in)

Before: No user has +923009999999. Count the rows in users and refresh_tokens.

Steps:

1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with { phone: "0300 9999999", password: "Anything123" }.
2. POST /api/v1/auth/login with DA's number and the password "WrongPass123".
3. Count users and refresh_tokens again.

Expect:

- Steps 1–2: 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS "Wrong phone number or password.", with the same body apart from requestId and timestamp. No tokens.
- Neither message contains "OTP" or "one-time code".
- Step 3: both counts are unchanged, and no user with +923009999999 exists.

Spec: ADR-03; API_CONTRACT §2.1 (login wording), §2.3 (Auth and users), §7.1, Appendix A · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/auth-login.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: +923009999999 is used only as a number that must not exist. Giving the same answer in both cases stops anyone finding out which numbers have accounts.

### SEC-003 · Accounts that aren't active can't sign in

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (pending), DRIVER (DR2)

Before: SA1 created a test distributor "Pending Gas" (code PG, store in North) and set its password, but didn't approve it, so its user is PENDING. SA1 suspended DR2 with the reason "Inactive sign-in test".

Steps:

1. POST /api/v1/auth/login as Pending Gas with the right password and X-App-Variant: distributor.
2. POST /api/v1/auth/login as DR2 with the right password and X-App-Variant: driver.
3. Sign in as DR2 with a wrong password.
4. As SA1, reactivate DR2 with a reason. DR2 signs in again.

Expect:

- Steps 1–2: 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE "This account isn't active. Call the office." No tokens.
- Step 3: 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS, so the account's status isn't revealed without the right password.
- Step 4: 200 with tokens.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §2.3 (Auth and users), §3.3, §7.1, §7.2 (PATCH /users/:id/status), §7.3 (rule 5, approve); Appendix B (user.status_change) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/auth-login.e2e-spec.ts`

### SEC-004 · Locked roles can't sign in, including the seeded branch admin

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: ADMIN, DISPATCHER, STORE_KEEPER, CLIENT

Before: auth.lockedRoles at its default [ADMIN, DISPATCHER, STORE_KEEPER, CLIENT]. Users with known passwords: the seeded "LPG Branch Admin" (ADMIN), a DISPATCHER, a STORE_KEEPER and a CLIENT.

Steps:

1. POST /api/v1/auth/login for each of the four with the right password and X-App-Variant: admin-web.
2. Repeat for the CLIENT with X-App-Variant: distributor, and for each of the four with no variant header.

Expect:

- Every attempt: 403 AUTH_ROLE_LOCKED "This account can't sign in. Call the office." No tokens. The answer is the same with or without a variant header.
- No message contains "OTP" or "one-time code".

Spec: ADR-02; ADR-03; API_CONTRACT §2.1, §3.1, §6 (auth.lockedRoles), §7.1, §8.6 (Access), Appendix A · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/auth-login.e2e-spec.ts`

### SEC-005 · Changing auth.lockedRoles takes effect for sign-in, refresh and open sessions

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (SA1), STORE_KEEPER

Before: A test user "Store Keeper Test" (STORE_KEEPER, ACTIVE, password set). auth.lockedRoles at its default.

Steps:

1. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/settings/auth.lockedRoles with { value: ["ADMIN", "DISPATCHER", "CLIENT"], reason: "Lock test: allow store keeper" }.
2. Sign in as Store Keeper Test, then call GET /api/v1/auth/me.
3. As SA1, set auth.lockedRoles back to ["ADMIN", "DISPATCHER", "STORE_KEEPER", "CLIENT"] with a reason.
4. With the store keeper's access token, call GET /api/v1/auth/me every 10 seconds for 70 seconds.
5. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with the store keeper's refresh token. Then try to sign in again.
6. As SA1, try to PATCH auth.lockedRoles with a list that includes SUPER_ADMIN; then with ['ADMIN', 'ADMIN'] (a repeated role).

Expect:

- Step 1: 200, and a setting.update audit row with the old and new lists.
- Step 2: 200 with tokens; /auth/me answers 200.
- Step 4: refused with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED no later than 60 seconds after step 3.
- Step 5: the refresh is refused with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED; sign-in answers 403 AUTH_ROLE_LOCKED.
- Step 6: 400 SETTING_INVALID_VALUE for both lists. The setting is unchanged, so the office can't lock itself out.

Spec: ADR-02; API_CONTRACT §3.1, §3.3, §5.2, §6 (auth.lockedRoles), §7.1 (refresh); Appendix B (setting.update) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/security-units.spec.ts, apps/api/test/security/sessions.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Use STORE_KEEPER, not ADMIN: unlocking ADMIN would reopen the ADMIN self-promotion hole (§3.1).

### SEC-006 · Signing in on the wrong app is refused with the name of the right app

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA), DRIVER (DR1), SUPER_ADMIN (SA1)

Before: DA, DR1 and SA1 are ACTIVE with passwords.

Steps:

1. POST /api/v1/auth/login as DA with X-App-Variant: driver, then with admin-web.
2. Sign in as DR1 with X-App-Variant: distributor.
3. Sign in as SA1 with X-App-Variant: distributor, then with driver.
4. Sign in as DA with distributor, DR1 with driver and SA1 with admin-web.
5. Sign in as DA and as DR1 with no variant header.

Expect:

- Step 1: 403 AUTH_WRONG_APP with details { role: "DISTRIBUTOR", app: "Smart Fleet shop app" } and message "This account is for the Smart Fleet shop app." No tokens.
- Step 2: 403 AUTH_WRONG_APP with details { role: "DRIVER", app: "Smart Fleet Driver app" } and "This account is for the Smart Fleet Driver app."
- Step 3: 403 AUTH_WRONG_APP with details { role: "SUPER_ADMIN", app: "Smart Fleet Office website" } and "This account is for the Smart Fleet Office website."
- Step 4: 200 for all three.
- Step 5: 200, because installed 0.1.0 apps send no variant.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §1.2, §2.3 (AUTH_WRONG_APP), §7.1, Appendix A; UX_MOBILE §3.6, S1 (WrongApp); UX_ADMIN §2.10 (role gate) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/auth-login.e2e-spec.ts, apps/api/test/security/security-units.spec.ts`

### SEC-007 · Sign-in and token refresh are rate limited

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: PUBLIC (not signed in)

Before: Redis is up and the rate-limit keys are cleared. All requests come from one IP address.

Steps:

1. Send 5 sign-ins with DA's number and a wrong password within 10 minutes. Then send a 6th with the right password.
2. Move past the 10-minute window (advance the test clock, or clear the window key). Sign in with the right password.
3. From the same IP, send 30 sign-ins with 30 different unknown numbers within 10 minutes. Then sign in as DR1 with the right password.
4. Send 30 POST /api/v1/auth/refresh calls from one IP within a minute, then a 31st.
5. Stop Redis. Sign in as DA with the right password.

Expect:

- Step 1: attempts 1–5 get 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS. The 6th gets 429 RATE_LIMITED "Too many tries. Please wait {{minutes}} min and try again." with a number from 1 to 10 filled in, and no tokens even though the password is right.
- Step 2: 200 with tokens.
- Step 3: the 31st request gets 429 RATE_LIMITED.
- Step 4: the 31st refresh gets 429 RATE_LIMITED.
- Step 5: 200 with tokens: the guard lets requests through while Redis is down.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §2.3 (RATE_LIMITED), §3.6, §7.1 · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/auth-limits.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: details.minutes is the whole minutes until the window resets, rounded up, at least 1 (API_CONTRACT §2.3). Every attempt counts, and a successful sign-in resets nothing (§3.6). With fixed windows the real wait can be shorter than 10 minutes.

### SEC-008 · Code (OTP) sign-in is off, can't be switched on over the API, and never creates users

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: PUBLIC (not signed in), SUPER_ADMIN (SA1)

Before: auth.otpLogin.enabled is false (the default). Count users and outbound messages. Run on the test server only; the SMS provider is the mock.

Steps:

1. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/send for DA's number and for "0300 9999999".
2. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify with { phone: "0300 9999999", code: "123456" }.
3. Count users and outbound messages.
4. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/settings/auth.otpLogin.enabled { value: true, reason: "OTP on-path test" }.
5. As SA1, read auth.otpLogin.enabled from GET /api/v1/settings. Then repeat step 1.

Expect:

- Steps 1–2: 403 AUTH_OTP_DISABLED "Sign in with your password." for every call. No code is sent.
- Step 3: no new user (none with +923009999999) and no SMS.
- Step 4: 403 SETTING_NOT_EDITABLE "This setting can't be changed here."; no setting.update audit row.
- Step 5: auth.otpLogin.enabled is still false, and step 1 again gives 403 AUTH_OTP_DISABLED with no code sent.

Spec: ADR-03; API_CONTRACT §3.1, §6 (auth.otpLogin.enabled), §7.1 (POST /auth/otp/\*), §8.6 (Access), Appendix A · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/auth-limits.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Code sign-in isn't built in the pilot: auth.otpLogin.enabled is reserved and the two routes always refuse (ADR-03; API_CONTRACT §6, §7.1).

### SEC-009 · Bad access tokens are refused, and reusing an old refresh token ends the session

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA)

Before: DA can sign in. The test config gives one token a short access lifetime (for example 2 seconds).

Steps:

1. Call GET /api/v1/auth/me with: no token; "Bearer garbage"; a token signed with another secret; DA's token with the payload changed to role SUPER_ADMIN (old signature); an expired token.
2. Sign in as DA (refresh token R1). POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with R1 and note the new pair (A2, R2).
3. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh again with R1.
4. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with R2.
5. Sign in as DA again.

Expect:

- Step 1: 401 AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID "Please sign in again." for every call. The edited token never reaches an office route.
- Step 2: 200 with a new access token and a refresh token R2 that differs from R1.
- Step 3: 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID.
- Step 4: 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID, because the reuse revoked the whole chain.
- Step 5: 200 with fresh tokens.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §2.3 (Auth and users), §3.3, §7.1 (POST /auth/refresh); UX_MOBILE §3.1 (single-flight refresh); UX_ADMIN §1.7 · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/security-units.spec.ts, apps/api/test/security/sessions.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Reuse detection is today's behaviour (auth.service.ts:177-211), kept by §7.1. Because of it, both apps must refresh single-flight.

### SEC-010 · Suspending a user or changing a password ends that user's other sessions within 60 seconds

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (SA1), DRIVER (DR2), DISTRIBUTOR (DA)

Before: DR2 signed in (tokens A and R). DA signed in twice, as if on two phones (A1/R1 and A2/R2).

Steps:

1. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/\<DR2 user>/status with { value: "SUSPENDED", reason: "Session end test" }.
2. As DR2, call GET /api/v1/trips/mine with A every 10 seconds for 70 seconds. Then POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with R.
3. As DA on phone 1, POST /api/v1/auth/change-password with { currentPassword, newPassword: "NewPass#2026" }.
4. As DA on phone 2, call GET /api/v1/wallet with A2 every 10 seconds for 70 seconds. Then refresh with R2.
5. As DA on phone 1, call GET /api/v1/wallet with the tokens returned in step 3.
6. As DA, change the password again with newPassword "short12" (7 characters).
7. As SA1, reactivate DR2 with a reason.

Expect:

- Step 1: 200. DR2's token_version goes up by 1. A user.status_change audit row holds the reason.
- Step 2: refused with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED "Please sign in again." no later than 60 seconds after step 1. The refresh is refused at once with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED.
- Step 3: 200 with new tokens. DA's token_version goes up by 1.
- Step 4: A2 is refused with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED within 60 seconds, and R2 is refused with 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED.
- Step 5: 200.
- Step 6: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (at least 8 characters).

Spec: API_CONTRACT §3.3, §7.1 (refresh, change-password), §7.2 (PATCH /users/:id/status), §8.6 (Access); Appendix B (user.status_change) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/security-units.spec.ts, apps/api/test/security/sessions.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: The 60-second cache is from §3.3.

### SEC-011 · The super admin is refused on routes only the distributor or the driver may use

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (SA1)

Before: X1 placed by DA (balance Rs 4,520) and assigned to DR1 (trip planned). AG-C0001 is full at Ahmed Gas Store.

Steps:

1. As SA1, call: POST /orders (X2 body for C2), POST /orders/quote, POST /payments/topup-requests, POST /clients, GET /wallet, GET /wallet/statement, GET /ledger/balance, GET /distributor/home, GET /distributors/me and POST /filling-orders.
2. As SA1, call: POST /custody/scan { qrCode: "AG-C0001", eventType: "SCAN_OUT", tripId: DR1's trip }, PATCH /drivers/\<DR1>/location and GET /trips/mine.
3. As SA1, PATCH /orders/\<X1>/status with { status: "DELIVERED" }.

Expect:

- Steps 1–2: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED "Your account can't do this." for every call.
- Step 3: 400 ORDER_USE_MANUAL_DELIVERY, message: Use "Mark delivered by office" for this.
- Nothing changed: DA balance Rs 4,520; no new order, top-up request, customer or refill; AG-C0001 still in the store; X1 still assigned and not delivered; DR1's location unchanged.

Spec: ADR-02; API_CONTRACT §3.1 (@ExactRoles), §7.2, §7.3 (GET /distributor/home), §7.4, §7.6 (status table), §7.7 (POST /custody/scan), §7.8, §7.9, §7.11 · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/roles.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Routes the office may also use (cancel, fail) let SA1 through by design and are tested in the orders area.

Spec: ADR-02; ADR-07; API_CONTRACT §3.2 (canSeeOrder), §7.6 (GET /orders/:id, /tracking, cancel) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/roles.e2e-spec.ts`

### SEC-015 · The /drivers socket accepts only a valid driver or office session, and only the office hears locations

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DRIVER (DR1, DR2), SUPER_ADMIN (SA1), DISTRIBUTOR (DA)

Before: DR1 and DR2 ACTIVE and signed in; SA1 and DA signed in.

Steps:

1. Connect a socket.io client to the /drivers namespace with no auth.token; then with "garbage"; then with an expired token.
2. Connect with DA's access token.
3. Connect DR1, DR2 and SA1 with their own tokens.
4. DR1 emits location:update { lat: 31.5204, lng: 74.3587 }.
5. As SA1, suspend DR1 with a reason. Wait 60 seconds. DR1 reconnects with the old token.

Expect:

- Steps 1–2: the server emits error { code } and disconnects: no token, "garbage" and the expired token get { code: 'AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID' }; DA gets { code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED' }. No drivers:snapshot is sent.
- Step 3: DR1 and DR2 stay connected (room driver:\<id>). SA1 stays connected (room office) and receives drivers:snapshot.
- Step 4: SA1 receives driver:location for DR1. DR2 receives nothing.
- Step 5: the reconnect gets error { code: 'AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED' } and a disconnect.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §3.3, §7.14, §8.6 (Access: a socket without a token is disconnected), Appendix A · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/drivers-socket.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: The event name driver:location is today's (drivers.gateway.ts:51). An open socket whose session ends is dropped with error { code } (API_CONTRACT §7.14): a driver's socket on its next message; the office's socket at once for a change made through the API, within 60 seconds for a change made elsewhere, and when its access token expires. Tests: apps/api/test/security/rev-live-sessions.e2e-spec.ts and apps/api/test/review/security/office-socket-and-tracking.e2e-spec.ts.

### SEC-016 · A driver's location is taken only from that driver's own session

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DRIVER (DR1)

Before: DR1 and DR2 online on the socket. DR2's last location is a known point L2 in Lahore.

Steps:

1. DR1's socket emits location:update { driverId: \<DR2>, lat: 31.5204, lng: 74.3587 }.
2. DR1's socket emits online:set { driverId: \<DR2>, isOnline: false }.
3. DR1 emits three location updates within 5 seconds.
4. As DR1, PATCH /api/v1/drivers/\<DR2>/location with { lat: 31.5, lng: 74.3 }, and PATCH /api/v1/drivers/\<DR2>/online.
5. As SA1, GET /api/v1/drivers/\<DR2> and /drivers/\<DR1>.

Expect:

- Step 1: DR1's location becomes 31.5204, 74.3587. DR2 stays at L2. The office broadcast names DR1.
- Step 2: DR1 goes offline; DR2 stays online.
- Step 3: only one update in those 5 seconds is stored and broadcast.
- Step 4: 404 NOT_FOUND for both. DR2's location and online state don't change.
- Step 5: DR2 is at L2 and online.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §7.2 (PATCH /drivers/:id/location, /online: DRIVER exact, own id), §7.14, §8.6 (Access: a driver can't move another driver's location) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/drivers-socket.e2e-spec.ts, apps/api/test/security/security-units.spec.ts`

Note: An ownership miss answers 404 NOT_FOUND (API_CONTRACT §3.2). What happens to extra updates within 5 seconds (dropped quietly or refused) isn't documented.

### SEC-018 · CORS answers only our own website's origin

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: PUBLIC (not signed in)

Before: API started with CORS_ORIGINS set to the test website's origin only (for example https://office.test.smartfleet.example).

Steps:

1. Send OPTIONS /api/v1/orders with Origin: \<website origin>, Access-Control-Request-Method: POST and Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization, idempotency-key, x-app-variant.
2. Send GET /api/v1/app/config with Origin: \<website origin>.
3. Repeat steps 1–2 with Origin: https://evil.example and with Origin: null.
4. Open a /drivers socket handshake with Origin: https://evil.example.

Expect:

- Step 1: Access-Control-Allow-Origin equals the website origin (never \*), and the allowed headers include Authorization, Idempotency-Key and X-App-Variant.
- Step 2: Access-Control-Expose-Headers lists X-Request-Id, Idempotent-Replay, X-Already-Applied and X-Feature-Disabled.
- Step 3: no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so a browser blocks the answer.
- Step 4: the handshake is refused.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §1.2 (returned headers, exposed through CORS), §3.7 (CORS) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/cors.e2e-spec.ts, apps/api/test/security/security-units.spec.ts`

Note: Phones send no Origin, so CORS doesn't affect the apps; it protects the website. The origin list is environment config, not in the docs.

### SEC-019 · The API refuses to start in production or staging with default secrets or test switches

**P1** · AUTO-UNIT · Inc 1 · Role: DEVELOPER

Before: Unit test of the boot-guard function that main.ts calls before NestFactory.create. process.exit and the logger are mocked. Each variant starts from a fully valid production env.

Steps:

1. With NODE_ENV=production, change one value at a time: JWT_ACCESS_SECRET = "change_me_access_secret_but_long_enough"; JWT_ACCESS_SECRET 31 characters long; JWT_ACCESS_SECRET equal to JWT_REFRESH_SECRET; DATABASE_URL missing; REDIS_URL and REDIS_HOST both missing; BULLMQ_PREFIX "smartfleet"; the S3 keys set to the minio defaults; CORS_ORIGINS "\*"; ENCRYPTION_KEY missing; ENCRYPTION_KEY of 63 hex characters; BLIND_INDEX_KEY missing.
2. With NODE_ENV=production, add one at a time: AUTH_EXPOSE_OTP=true, TEST_PHONES=…, ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true, SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD=…, PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_ENABLED=true.
3. Repeat two of the bad values with NODE_ENV=staging.
4. Run with NODE_ENV=development and the default config; then with the fully valid production env.
5. Start with NODE_ENV=staging and BULLMQ_PREFIX 'sf-stg'. Then with NODE_ENV=production, APP_ENV=training and BULLMQ_PREFIX 'sf-prod'; then with 'sf-train'.

Expect:

- Steps 1–3: exit code 1 before Nest starts (no port is opened), with a one-line reason naming the variable, for example "JWT_ACCESS_SECRET must be at least 32 characters".
- Step 4: development starts with the defaults, and the valid production env starts.
- Step 5: staging with 'sf-stg' starts (stg is an alias); production with APP_ENV=training refuses 'sf-prod' (exit 1 naming BULLMQ_PREFIX) and starts with 'sf-train'.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §3.7 (boot guards); DATA_MODEL §2.6 (separate Redis prefixes) · Test file: `apps/api/test/unit/boot-guards.spec.ts`

Note: The minio default values aren't spelled out in the docs (they are in files.service.ts:31-34). The environment name is APP_ENV when set, else NODE_ENV (API_CONTRACT §3.7). From Inc 2, PUBLIC_LINK_BASE_URL (https) and CONFIRM_LINK_SECRET (at least 32 characters) are also required.

### SEC-023 · Only the super admin changes a role, with a reason and an audit row, and unsafe changes are refused

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (SA1), DISTRIBUTOR (DA)

Before: The seeded "LPG Branch Admin" (ADMIN, no driver or shop profile). DR2 has a driver profile. SA1 and DA are signed in.

2. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/\<SA1>/role with { value: "DISPATCHER", reason: "Self change test" }, and PATCH /api/v1/users/\<SA1>/status with { value: "SUSPENDED", reason: "Self suspend test" }.
3. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/\<Branch Admin>/role with { value: "SUPER_ADMIN", reason: "Promote test" }.
4. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/\<DR2>/role with { value: "DISTRIBUTOR", reason: "Profile mismatch test" }.
5. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/\<Branch Admin>/role with { value: "DISPATCHER" } and no reason.
6. As SA1, PATCH /api/v1/users/\<Branch Admin>/role with { value: "DISPATCHER", reason: "Role change test for audit" }. Read the audit log and the user's token_version. Then change the role back to ADMIN with a reason.

- Steps 1–5 change nothing and write no user.role_change or user.status_change row.
- Step 6: 200. The role is DISPATCHER, token_version goes up by 1, and one user.role_change row holds actor SA1, the reason, and before ADMIN / after DISPATCHER.

Note: Every pilot user has a profile that fixes its role, so a valid change is rare in the pilot; this case uses the seeded ADMIN user, which has no profile. Moving between two locked roles keeps that account unable to sign in.

### SEC-024 · Two super admins suspending each other at the same time can't lock the office out

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (SA1, SA2)

Before: SA1 and SA2 are the only ACTIVE super admins, and both are signed in.

Steps:

1. At the same moment (Promise.all), SA1 sends PATCH /api/v1/users/\<SA2>/status { value: "SUSPENDED", reason: "Race test A" } and SA2 sends PATCH /api/v1/users/\<SA1>/status { value: "SUSPENDED", reason: "Race test B" }.
2. Count the ACTIVE SUPER_ADMIN users and the user.status_change audit rows.
3. Reactivate the suspended one (through the database or the CLI) and repeat 20 times.

Expect:

- In every run exactly one request succeeds (200) and the other gets 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED: both lock the active super-admin rows and re-read the caller, so the second sees that its sender was just suspended.
- After every run at least one super admin is ACTIVE, and that run wrote exactly one user.status_change row.

Spec: ADR-02; API_CONTRACT §2.3 (USER_LAST_SUPER_ADMIN), §3.3, §4 (rule 1), §7.2 (PATCH /users/:id/status) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/users.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: USER_LAST_SUPER_ADMIN stays as the safety net; with the lock it can't happen in this race (API_CONTRACT §7.2).

Expect:

- Step 1: the old DISTRIBUTOR_CREDIT_OVER rule is listed as not active (inc1a backfill 12).
- Step 2: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; no rule is created.
- Step 3: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED for each call.
- Step 4: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; the rule stays not active.

Spec: ADR-06 (balances can't go negative); API_CONTRACT §7.2 (/alerts, /alert-rules: office exact; DISTRIBUTOR_CREDIT_OVER refused; existing ones deactivated); DATA_MODEL §3.4 (backfill 12), §3.7 (alert-rules.service.ts), §3.8 (invariant 13) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/push-alerts.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: The alert-rule body is today's route.

### SEC-030 · The website signs the office out after 30 minutes without activity, with a warning at 28

**P2** · MAN-WEB · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (Owner)

Before: Signed in to the office website as Owner on a laptop. A watch or the laptop clock to time the steps.

Steps:

1. Open Top-ups and leave the laptop untouched for 28 minutes.
2. Move the mouse, then leave the laptop untouched again for 30 minutes.
3. Read the page you land on.
4. Sign in again.

Expect:

- Step 1: at 28 minutes a toast at the top centre says "You'll be signed out in 2 minutes. Keep working to stay signed in."
- Step 2: moving the mouse restarts the timer; after 30 more idle minutes the website signs you out.
- Step 3: the sign-in page says "You were signed out after 30 minutes without activity." It never says "10 minutes".
- Step 4: sign-in works.

Spec: UX_ADMIN §0 (A15), §2.10 (Session)

Note: The server-side tokens last 12 hours (access) and 30 days (refresh) (API_CONTRACT §7.1); this case checks only the website's idle timer.

### SEC-031 · Tracking shows the shop its driver's position only while its order is on the way

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA), SUPER_ADMIN (SA1), DRIVER (DR1, DR2)

Before: Standard test data with cylinders. DR1 and DR2 report positions (PATCH /drivers/:id/location).

Steps:

1. As DA, place X1; as SA1, assign DR1. DR1 reports a position. As DA and as SA1, GET /orders/\<X1>/tracking.
2. DR1 departs the store stop. As DA, GET /orders/\<X1> and /orders/\<X1>/tracking.
3. DR1 taps Delivered, then reports a position at Hina's address (Bilal Gas's customer). As DA, GET the tracking again.
4. Place three more orders: one cancelled before loading, one failed after leaving the store, one reassigned from DR1 to DR2 before loading. As DA, GET each tracking; then DR2 departs the store stop and DA reads the reassigned one again.

Expect:

- Step 1: DA gets the same keys as before (orderId, status, destination, driver, driverLocation, tripId, paymentStatus, deliveryFeePaisa), with driverLocation null while ASSIGNED; SA1 gets the position.
- Step 2: stage ON_THE_WAY with TRACK offered, and DA gets DR1's position.
- Step 3: status DELIVERED and driverLocation null; the driver card and the destination are still sent.
- Step 4: the cancelled and the failed order give driverLocation null; the reassigned one names DR2 with driverLocation null until DR2 departs the store, then DR2's position, never DR1's.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §1.6 (TRACK), §3.2, §7.6 (GET /orders/:id/tracking), Appendix A; UX_MOBILE S11 · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/review-fixes.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding security-01 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV security-01 …". Accepted for the pilot (API_CONTRACT §7.6): while its order is on the way, the shop also sees the driver when he serves another distributor's trip at the same time. Confirming test: apps/api/test/review/security/office-socket-and-tracking.e2e-spec.ts.

### SEC-032 · An open office socket on /drivers ends with its session or its token, and a driver's socket is re-checked on every message

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SUPER_ADMIN (SA1, SA2), DRIVER (DR1)

Before: Standard test data. SA1 and SA2 connected to the /drivers socket and received drivers:snapshot.

Steps:

1. As SA1, change SA2's role (PATCH /users/\<SA2>/role { value: "ADMIN", reason }).
2. SA1 changes its own password (POST /auth/change-password) and opens a socket with the new access token; then its sockets are re-checked.
3. Suspend SA2 outside this API (a database change the session cache isn't told of). Run the office re-check at once, then again 61 seconds later.
4. DR1 connects with a token that expires in 2 seconds; 2.5 seconds later it sends location:update.

Expect:

- Step 1: SA2's socket gets error { code: 'AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED' } and is disconnected at once.
- Step 2: the socket of the old token is dropped with AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED; the one opened with the new token stays connected through the re-check.
- Step 3: the first re-check keeps SA2's socket (the session row is cached for up to 60 seconds, API_CONTRACT §3.3); the one 61 seconds later drops it with AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED. SA1's socket stays.
- Step 4: DR1 gets error { code: 'AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID' } and a disconnect, and his position isn't stored.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §3.3, §7.14 (Refusals and revoked sessions), §8.6 (Access) · Test file: `apps/api/test/security/rev-live-sessions.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding security-02 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV security-02 …". An office socket also gets an expiry timer when it connects: apps/api/test/review/security/office-socket-and-tracking.e2e-spec.ts checks that a suspended office user and an expired office token stop hearing driver positions. The website half (refresh and reconnect) has its own case in the OFF area.

### SEC-033 · A DISTRIBUTOR or DRIVER caller without its profile id is refused at every scoped route, before any read

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA without its distributorId), DRIVER (DR1 without its driverId)

Before: Standard test data with X1 assigned to DR1. Callers carry DA's and DR1's user ids and roles but no profile id, as a legacy user with no distributors or drivers row would.

Steps:

1. As the DISTRIBUTOR caller: list orders, quote and create an order, list and create customers, list and create refills, read the shop profile and home, and quote a location.
2. As the DRIVER caller: GET /trips/mine, GET /trips/next-suggestions and GET /filling-orders/driver/mine.
3. Repeat GET /trips/mine with DR1's driverId.

Expect:

- Step 1: all ten are refused with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED and nothing is created.
- Step 2: all three are refused with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
- Step 3: DR1's own trip only.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §3.2 (scoped queries), §3.3, §7.1, §7.2 (POST /users/:id/password, PATCH /users/:id/status), §8.5 step 3 · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/review-fixes.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Regression case for review finding security-03 (CHANGELOG, "Review fixes, 2026-10-23"); its tests are named "REV security-03 …". Such a user also gets no tokens: sign-in 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE, and refresh and every request with an old token 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED; the office can't give it a password or make it ACTIVE (apps/api/test/review/security/profileless-role-token.e2e-spec.ts). A unit test scans every route and service for an unchecked cast of the caller's id (apps/api/test/orders/review-fixes.spec.ts).

## WAL · Wallet and history

The wallet card and low-balance warning, the history, the office correction tool, the nightly wallet check, races for the last rupee, and money on the wire. 25 cases: P1 13 · P2 11 · P3 1.

### WAL-001 · Wallet summary shows the balance and the money being checked

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: Distributor DA (API)

Before: Standard test data. DA balance Rs 5,000 (one OPENING_BALANCE row), no top-up requests. Settings at defaults (wallet.lowBalancePaisa 100000, wallet.maxBalancePaisa null).

Steps:

1. As DA, GET /api/v1/wallet.
2. As DA, POST /api/v1/payments/topup-requests {amountPaisa: 200000, payerName: 'Ahmed Raza', payerChannel: 'BANK_APP'} and then {amountPaisa: 300000, ...}, each with a new Idempotency-Key.
3. As DA, GET /api/v1/wallet again, then GET /api/v1/distributor/home.

Expect:

- Step 1: 200 {balancePaisa: '500000', pendingTopupPaisa: '0', pendingTopupCount: 0, lowBalance: false, capPaisa: null}. Every \*Paisa value is a JSON string of digits.
- Step 3: balancePaisa is still '500000'; pendingTopupPaisa '500000'; pendingTopupCount 2. Requests being checked never change the balance.
- GET /distributor/home returns the same WalletSummary under 'wallet'.
- No ledger_entries row was written by the two requests.

Spec: ADR-06; ADR-09; API_CONTRACT §1.1, §7.3, §7.8, §7.9; UX_MOBILE S2 · Test file: `apps/api/test/money/wallet-routes.e2e-spec.ts`

### WAL-002 · Home wallet card shows the balance and the 'Being checked' row

**P2** · MAN-SHOP · Inc 1 · Role: Distributor DA (shop app)

Before: DA is signed in to the shop app. Balance Rs 5,000. No top-up requests waiting.

Steps:

1. Open the Home screen and look at the wallet card.
2. Tap 'Add money' and send a top-up request for Rs 2,000 (any name on the account). Go back to Home.
3. Look at the wallet card again. Tap the 'Being checked' row.
4. Go back. Send a second request for Rs 3,000. Go back to Home and tap the 'Being checked' row again.

Expect:

- Step 1: the card shows 'Balance' and 'Rs 5,000' with one button, 'Add money'. 'History' is a tile under the card, not a button on it. There is no 'Being checked' row.
- Step 3: the balance still reads 'Rs 5,000'. A row with a clock icon reads 'Being checked' and 'Rs 2,000'. Tapping it opens the status screen of that top-up.
- Step 4: the row reads 'Being checked' and 'Rs 5,000'. Tapping it opens History with the 'Top-ups' filter chosen.
- No screen shows 'On hold', 'held', 'Rs.' or a code such as PENDING.

Spec: ADR-06; UX_MOBILE §0, S2, S7; API_CONTRACT §7.3

### WAL-003 · Home wallet card loading, error, no-signal and stale states

**P2** · MAN-SHOP · Inc 1 · Role: Distributor DA (shop app)

Before: DA is signed in. Balance Rs 5,000. You can slow the network (weak-signal area or the phone's developer options) and switch airplane mode on and off.

Steps:

1. Close the app. With a slow network, open it and watch the Wallet card while Home loads.
2. Switch on airplane mode. Pull down on Home to refresh.
3. Wait 30 seconds and look at the top of the screen.
4. Close and reopen the app while still in airplane mode.
5. Switch off airplane mode. Tap 'Try again' (or pull down to refresh).

Expect:

- Step 1: grey placeholder bars show inside the card while it loads. It never shows 'Rs 0'.
- Step 2: the balance already shown stays on screen, stamped 'Saved' and a time inside the wallet card (for example 'Saved 4:12 pm'), with the history icon.
- Step 3: one banner at the top, 'No connection' with 'Try again'. The card keeps its 'Saved …' stamp and adds no error of its own.
- Step 4: if no saved balance is available, the card says 'Couldn't load your balance.' with a 'Try again' button. It never shows 'Rs 0'.
- Step 5: the card shows 'Rs 5,000' again and the banner goes away.

Spec: UX_MOBILE §2.2 (OfflineBanner, QueryBoundary), §3.5, S2, §6

Note: Whether a cold start offline shows the last saved balance depends on query persistence, which the docs do not specify; either the stale balance or the error card is acceptable, never 'Rs 0'.

### WAL-004 · The low-balance flag follows wallet.lowBalancePaisa, is true only below it, and the office wallet list carries the same flag

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: Developer (API test) as SA1, DA and DB

Before: Standard test data. DA Rs 5,000, DB Rs 0. wallet.lowBalancePaisa at its default 100000 (Rs 1,000).

Steps:

1. As DB, GET /wallet. As SA1, GET /admin/wallets.
2. As SA1, record a correction on DA: TAKE 400000, reasonCode OTHER, note 'test setup low balance' (DA now Rs 1,000). As DA, GET /wallet; as SA1, GET /admin/wallets.
3. As SA1, TAKE 100 more (DA now Rs 999). As DA, GET /wallet; as SA1, GET /admin/wallets.
4. As SA1, PATCH /settings/wallet.lowBalancePaisa {value: 50000, reason: 'test lower warning'}. Right after it, as DA GET /wallet; as SA1, GET /admin/wallets.
5. GET /app/config without signing in.
6. As SA1, set wallet.lowBalancePaisa to 0 with a reason. As DB, GET /wallet; as SA1, GET /admin/wallets. Then set the setting back to 100000 with a reason.

Expect:

- Step 1: DB lowBalance true (Rs 0 is below Rs 1,000); the office list carries the same flags: Ahmed Gas false, Bilal Gas true.
- Step 2: DA at exactly Rs 1,000: lowBalance false, on GET /wallet and on the office list.
- Step 3: DA at Rs 999: lowBalance true on both.
- Step 4: with the threshold at Rs 500, DA at Rs 999: lowBalance false on both (Bilal Gas still true). An audit row setting.update records {key: 'wallet.lowBalancePaisa', from: 100000, to: 50000} with the reason and actor SA1.
- Step 5: /app/config wallet.lowBalancePaisa shows the new value 50000.
- Step 6: with the threshold at Rs 0, DB at Rs 0 shows lowBalance false on GET /wallet and on the office list: Rs 0 turns the warning off.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §5.2, §6, §7.8 (WalletSummary.lowBalance, AdminWalletRow.lowBalance), Appendix B; UX_ADMIN §2.6, §2.8; UX_MOBILE S2 · Test file: `apps/api/test/money/wallet-routes.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: A balance exactly at the threshold is not low: lowBalance is balance \< wallet.lowBalancePaisa, strictly below, and Rs 0 turns the warning off (API_CONTRACT §7.8, UX_ADMIN §2.8). The office Wallets list (GET /admin/wallets) uses the same rule. The shop app shows the chip "Low balance" on the wallet card whenever lowBalance is true (UX_MOBILE S2), and the website a red "Low" chip on the Wallets list (UX_ADMIN §2.6).

- Step 4: 404 NOT_FOUND.
- Step 5: Ahmed Gas's lastTopupAt equals the approved payment's completedAt (the approval time); checkingCount 0.
- Step 6: lastTopupAt is unchanged (a request being checked doesn't count); checkingPaisa '100000', checkingCount 1.
- Step 7: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields [{ path: 'limit', code: 'TOO_LARGE' }] for limit=101 and code 'TOO_SMALL' for limit=0 (nothing is clamped); 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming cursor for the bad cursor.

Spec: API_CONTRACT §1.3, §7.8; UX_ADMIN §2.6, §2.12 · Test file: `apps/api/test/money/wallet-routes.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: lastTopupAt is when the latest approved top-up was approved (completed_at of its newest SUCCESS payment); requests being checked or rejected don't count (API_CONTRACT §7.8).

- Step 4: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields [{ path: 'Idempotency-Key', code: 'REQUIRED' }]; nothing is written.
- Step 5: 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (the key belongs to a correction for DA); DB's balance is unchanged.
- Step 6: exactly one ledger row with key 'adjust:K3' and one wallet.correction audit row.

## TOP · Manual bank top-ups

Top-up info and limits, telling the app you paid, the office approval against the bank app, bank references used once, amount mismatches, rejects, and the payment webhook switched off. 31 cases: P1 17 · P2 13 · P3 1.

### TOP-001 · Top-up info comes from settings, and top-ups are closed while no company account is set

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: Distributor DA (API); engineer for the settings CLI

Before: Test server. topup.account set by the CLI to {accountTitle: 'Smart Fleet (Pvt) Ltd', bankName: \<test bank>, iban: 'PK00TEST0000000000000000', accountNumber: \<test>}. Other settings at defaults. DA has no pending request.

Steps:

1. As DA, GET /payments/topup-info.
2. As SA1, GET /payments/topup-info.
3. With the settings CLI, set topup.account to null (with a reason). As DA, GET /payments/topup-info again; then POST /payments/topup-requests with a valid body and a new Idempotency-Key, and the legacy POST /payments/topup {amountPaisa: 500000, provider: 'BANK_MANUAL'}. Then restore the account with the CLI.

Expect:

- Step 1: 200 with account {accountTitle 'Smart Fleet (Pvt) Ltd', iban 'PK00TEST0000000000000000', ...}, limits {minPaisa '50000', maxPaisa '5000000', maxNowPaisa null}, quickAmountsPaisa for Rs 2,000, Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000, payerChannels ['EASYPAISA_APP', 'BANK_APP', 'OTHER'], checkingHours {from '09:00', to '21:00'}, support {phone, hours}, pending {count 0, totalPaisa '0'}, training false here (APP_ENV=test, as FND-001 expects; true only with APP_ENV=training).
- Step 2: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.
- Step 3: all three calls give 503 TOPUP_ACCOUNT_NOT_CONFIGURED 'Top-ups aren't open yet. Call the office.', and no payment row is created (the shop app's Add money screen for this is the manual case FND-004).

### TOP-003 · Top-up amount must be whole rupees within the limits set in settings

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: Distributor DA (API); SA1 for settings

- After the change: Rs 500 gives 400 'The minimum top-up is Rs 1,000.' and Rs 25,000 gives 400 'The maximum top-up is Rs 20,000.'; topup-info limits show '100000' and '2000000'.
- Each setting change writes a setting.update audit row with the reason. No refused request is saved.

Before: Standard test data. DA has pending Rs 5,000 requests P1 and P2; DB has pending Rs 1,000 request P3; DA has P4 and P5 for the race step. Seed the requests with the test factories rather than POST /payments/topup-requests: DA's four pending requests are over the default limit of 3 (topup.maxPendingPerDistributor).

Steps:

1. As SA1, approve P1 with 'FT-7781-4402'.
2. As SA1, approve P2 with 'ft 7781 4402'.
3. As SA1, approve P3 (DB) with 'FT77814402'.
4. At the same moment, SA1 approves P4 and SA2 approves P5, both with the new reference 'IBFT-2210-5566'.

Expect:

- Step 1: 200.
- Step 2: 409 TOPUP_BANK_REFERENCE_USED, details {paymentShortCode: P1's AG-T number, distributorName: 'Ahmed Gas', approvedAt}, message 'Already used for AG-T0nn (Ahmed Gas). Check it, or reject as a duplicate.' P2 stays PENDING.
- Step 3: the same 409 for DB's request; DB's balance stays Rs 0.
- Step 4: one approval succeeds and the other gets 409 TOPUP_BANK_REFERENCE_USED; only one CREDIT_TOPUP is written.

Spec: ADR-09; API_CONTRACT §2.3, §7.9 (approve rules 2 and 7), §8.6; DATA_MODEL §1 (exactly once), §3.2 (bankReferenceKey), §3.6, §7 · Test file: `apps/api/test/money/topup-review.e2e-spec.ts`

### TOP-021 · Rejecting a top-up needs a reason code, moves no money and is audited

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: Super admin SA1 (API)

Steps:

3. Reject P2 with {reasonCode: 'OTHER', note: 'Payer name and amount both differ'}.
4. Reject P3.
5. As DA, GET /payments/\<P1 id> and GET /wallet. Read ledger_entries and audit_logs.

Expect:

- Step 1: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED each time (unknown code; OTHER needs a 3-300 character note).
- Step 2: 200; status 'REJECTED', stage 'NOT_ADDED', rejectReasonCode 'NOT_IN_BANK'. The repeat returns 200 with X-Already-Applied: true and the request unchanged: rejectReasonCode is still 'NOT_IN_BANK'.
- Step 3: 200 with rejectNote 'Payer name and amount both differ'.
- Step 4: 409 TOPUP_NOT_PENDING; P3 stays SUCCESS.
- Step 5: DA sees the reason code and note; the balance is the same as before the rejects; no ledger row for P1 or P2; one topup.reject audit row each, with the reason (the repeat writes none).

## FEE · Delivery cost on orders

The delivery cost taken when an order is placed, the balance boundary, retries, cancels with and without a refund, the refund cut-off setting, and proof that nothing else moves money. 29 cases: P1 19 · P2 9 · P3 1.

### FEE-001 · Placing X1 deducts Rs 480 in the same transaction that creates the order

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: Distributor DA (API)

2. As DA, GET /wallet and GET /wallet/statement.
3. Read the orders, order_lines, ledger_entries and audit_logs rows.

Expect:

- Step 1: 201 OrderDto {shortCode like 'AG-0001', status 'PENDING', stage 'NEEDS_DRIVER', fee {totalPaisa '48000', status 'DEDUCTED', breakdown {basePaisa '25000', lines 11.8 kg 2 x '4000' = '8000' and 45.4 kg 1 x '15000' = '15000'}}, cancel {allowed true, refundPaisa '48000', noRefundReason null}, deliveryFeePaisa '48000', paymentStatus 'PAID_VIA_LEDGER', originStore 'Ahmed Gas Store'}.
- Step 2: balance '452000' (Rs 4,520); newest statement item DELIVERY_COST '-48000' with balanceAfterPaisa '452000'.
- Step 3: fee_status DEDUCTED, fee_strategy DISTRIBUTOR_ZONE, fee_base_paisa 25000, fee_details naming zone North; lines store 4000/8000 and 15000/15000; one DEBIT_ORDER -48000 with key 'order:\<id>:debit'; one order.create audit row (actor DA). No dispatch job was queued (auto-assign off).

### FEE-004 · A distributor that isn't active can't place an order, and nothing is deducted

- Step 4: 200; X1 FAILED, stage 'NOT_DELIVERED', failureReasonCode 'CUSTOMER_REFUSED', its stop FAILED, an order.fail audit row; the cancel gets 409 ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE.
- Step 5: no note gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; with the note 200 and X2 FAILED.
- Balance stays Rs 4,120; no CREDIT_ORDER_REVERSAL; both orders keep fee status 'DEDUCTED'.

Spec: ADR-07; API_CONTRACT §1.5 (DeliveryFailureReason), §7.6 (fail), §8.1, §8.6; UX_MOBILE §5 (Could not deliver) · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/fees.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Before the start the right action is a cancel, which refunds (FEE-009).

### FEE-021 · Default refund cut-off (FIRST_LOAD_SCAN): what does and doesn't count as delivery started

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: Distributor DA and driver DR1 (API)

Before: Standard test data. orders.deliveryStartedAt = FIRST_LOAD_SCAN. For each scenario DA places a fresh X1 and SA1 assigns DR1 (trip T).

Steps:

1. Scenario 1: no driver action. DA cancels.
2. Scenario 2: DR1 PATCH /trips/\<T>/status {status: 'IN_PROGRESS'} (the trip starts; X1 stays ASSIGNED), no load. DA cancels.
3. Scenario 3: DR1 arrives at the store stop (PATCH /trips/stops/\<store stop>/arrive), no load. DA cancels.
4. Scenario 4: DR1 load-scans one cylinder. DA cancels.
5. Scenario 5: DR1 departs the store stop with no load scan. DA cancels.
6. Scenario 6: DR1 arrives at Sana's delivery stop with no load scan. DA cancels.

Expect:

- Scenarios 1, 2 and 3: GET shows refundPaisa '48000'; the cancel returns '48000' and writes one CREDIT_ORDER_REVERSAL (a trip start, IN_TRANSIT or arriving at the store never counts).
- Scenarios 4, 5 and 6: GET shows refundPaisa '0' with noRefundReason 'DELIVERY_STARTED'; the cancel returns '0' and writes no reversal.
- Every order.cancel audit row has startedRule 'FIRST_LOAD_SCAN'. The ledger sum equals the balance at the end.

Spec: ADR-07; API_CONTRACT §5.5 (isDeliveryStarted), §7.6, §7.7 (arrive, depart), §8.1; DATA_MODEL §1 (rule 7) · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/fees.e2e-spec.ts`

### FEE-022 · orders.deliveryStartedAt = DRIVER_ASSIGNED or LEFT_STORE moves the refund cut-off

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: SA1, distributor DA and driver DR1 (API)

Before: Standard test data. DA has enough balance. Each scenario uses a fresh X1.

Steps:

1. As SA1, PATCH /settings/orders.deliveryStartedAt {value: 'ON_DELIVERY', reason: 'bad value test'}.
2. Set DRIVER_ASSIGNED (with a reason). A: cancel an unassigned X1. B: cancel an X1 right after assigning DR1.
3. Set LEFT_STORE. C: assign, load-scan, then cancel. D: assign, load-scan, DR1 fails it (CUSTOMER_REFUSED). E: assign, load-scan, depart the store stop, then cancel.
4. Set FIRST_LOAD_SCAN. Assign a fresh X1 to DR1. Switch to DRIVER_ASSIGNED, then cancel it. Restore FIRST_LOAD_SCAN.
5. GET /app/config after each change.

Expect:

- Step 1: 400 SETTING_INVALID_VALUE; the setting is unchanged.
- A: refund Rs 480. B: refund Rs 0 with noRefundReason 'DELIVERY_STARTED'.
- C: refund Rs 480 (loading alone doesn't count under LEFT_STORE). D: 409 ORDER_NOT_STARTED_USE_CANCEL. E: refund Rs 0.
- Step 4: refund Rs 0; the audit row shows startedRule 'DRIVER_ASSIGNED' (the rule is read when cancelling).
- Each change writes setting.update {key, from, to} with the reason; /app/config orders.deliveryStartedAt shows the current value.

Spec: ADR-07; API_CONTRACT §5.2, §5.5, §6, §7.6, §7.13, Appendix B; UX_ADMIN §2.8; UX_MOBILE S9 (refund sentence) · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/fees.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: The shop app's refund sentence must follow the value: orders.new.refundRule.DRIVER_ASSIGNED ('…If you cancel before a driver is assigned, you get it back…') and LEFT_STORE ('…If you cancel before the van leaves your store…'); 'Check and place' reads the app config fresh (FEE-007). The rule isn't stored on the order (DECISIONS ADR-07), so E4 is the documented behaviour.

### FEE-023 · OrdersFeePolicy: delivery-started and cancel-terms rules

**P1** · AUTO-UNIT · Inc 1 · Role: Developer (unit test)

Before: OrdersFeePolicy with OrderForPolicy fixtures; WalletService mocked.

Steps:

1. Run isDeliveryStarted for each rule (FIRST_LOAD_SCAN, DRIVER_ASSIGNED, LEFT_STORE) against: nothing set; assignedAt; IN_TRANSIT with onTheWayAt only; loadStartedAt; store stop departedAt; delivery stop arrivedAt; status DELIVERED; status FAILED.
2. Run cancelTerms for: DEDUCTED and not started; DEDUCTED and started; DEDUCTED with fee_strategy LEGACY_ZONE_PAIR (charged by the old code) and not started; fee status NONE (an order from before the switch-over, or a zero cost) not started; a terminal status; handoverStarted true.
3. Call cancel for a NONE order and for the legacy DEDUCTED order, and check WalletService.reverse.

Expect:

- FIRST_LOAD_SCAN is started by loadStartedAt, departedAt, arrivedAt, DELIVERED or FAILED, never by onTheWayAt alone; DRIVER_ASSIGNED adds assignedAt; LEFT_STORE ignores loadStartedAt.
- cancelTerms: refundPaisa = the fee only for DEDUCTED and not started; 0 with noRefundReason 'DELIVERY_STARTED' once started; 0 for NONE; 0 with noRefundReason null for the legacy DEDUCTED order; allowed false for a terminal status or a started hand-over.
- For the NONE order and the legacy DEDUCTED order no reversal is written: reverse is never called for the legacy order, and it returns null when there is no ledger row keyed order:\<id>:debit.

Spec: ADR-07; API_CONTRACT §5.4 (reverse), §5.5, §8.1 (orders before the switch-over); DATA_MODEL §3.4 (backfill 3) · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/fee-policy.spec.ts`

### FEE-025 · Shop app with a zero delivery cost: 'Place order' without 'pay', and no wallet lines

**P3** · MAN-SHOP · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (Ahmed Gas); SUPER_ADMIN (Owner) for the price

### FEE-026 · After loading, a cancel and a 'could not deliver' at the same moment: one wins and no money moves

**P2** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA), DRIVER (DR1)

Before: Inc 1 build. Standard test data. For each round, a fresh X1 (Rs 480) is assigned to DR1 and AG-C0005 has been load-scanned on its trip, so delivery has started. Run 20 rounds.

Steps:

1. At the same moment, DA sends POST /api/v1/orders/\<id>/cancel { reasonCode: "CUSTOMER_CANCELLED", confirmRefundPaisa: "0" } and DR1 sends POST /api/v1/orders/\<id>/fail { reasonCode: "CUSTOMER_NOT_HOME" }.
2. Read the order, its audit rows and DA's ledger rows.

Expect:

- Exactly one call succeeds. A cancel that loses gets 409 ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE with details.currentStatus 'FAILED'; a fail that loses gets 409 ORDER_INVALID_TRANSITION with details { from: 'CANCELLED', to: 'FAILED', currentStatus: 'CANCELLED' }.
- The order ends CANCELLED (refundedPaisa "0") or FAILED, never both, with exactly one order.cancel or one order.fail audit row.
- No CREDIT_ORDER_REVERSAL row in any round. DA's balance goes down by Rs 480 per round (the placement) and by nothing else.

Spec: ADR-07; API_CONTRACT §4 (rules 1 and 3), §7.6 (cancel, fail), §8.1 · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/fees.e2e-spec.ts`

### FEE-027 · Inc 2: the first LOAD scan ends the refund, and a scanned delivery with a short take-back moves no money

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 2 · Role: Driver DR1 and distributor DA (API, Inc 2 build)

Before: Inc 2 build. DA placed X1 (balance Rs 4,520; take back 2 x 11.8 kg and 1 x 45.4 kg) assigned to DR1 (trip T). confirmation.enabled false. Fixture (seeded, no money): Sana already holds AG-C0011 (11.8 kg) from an earlier finished run.

Steps:

2. As DA, GET /orders/\<X1 id>.
3. As DR1, load AG-C0006 and AG-C0031 and finish the store stop. At Sana's stop, HANDOVER all three (AG-C0005, AG-C0006, AG-C0031), TAKE_BACK AG-C0011 with returnState 'EMPTY', then POST .../finish with no body.
4. POST .../finish with {takeBackShort: {reasonCode: 'CUSTOMER_KEPT'}}.

Expect:

- Step 1: 201 RECORDED; load_started_at is stamped on X1.
- Step 2: cancel {allowed true, refundPaisa '0', noRefundReason 'DELIVERY_STARTED'}.
- Step 3: the finish gets 409 TAKE_BACK_SHORT {expected 3, taken 1}.
- Step 4: X1 is DELIVERED with deliveryMethod 'SCANNED'. Balance stays Rs 4,520; no ledger row besides X1's DEBIT_ORDER; fee status 'DEDUCTED'.

## CUS · Customers and zones

Adding customers with a phone number and a map pin, zone lookup, duplicates, editing (Inc 2) and ownership. 14 cases: P1 4 · P2 10 · P3 0.

### CUS-001 · Add a customer with a North pin: phone saved as +923001234567, with its zone and price

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA)

Before: Standard test data, except that C1 "Sana" does not exist yet. DA token (X-App-Variant: distributor). DA's North price: base Rs 250; per cylinder 6 kg Rs 30, 11.8 kg Rs 40, 15 kg Rs 80, 45.4 kg Rs 150.

Steps:

1. As DA, POST /api/v1/clients with a new Idempotency-Key and body { name: "Sana", phone: "0300 1234567", area: "Model Town", address: { label: "House 14, Street 5", lat/lng of a point well inside North } }.
2. As DA, GET /api/v1/clients.
3. In the test database, read client_addresses.zone_id for the new address.

Expect:

- Step 1 returns 201. client.name is "Sana" and client.phone is "+923001234567".
- address.label is "House 14, Street 5" and address.zone.name is "North".
- price.zone.name is "North" and price.basePaisa is "25000". price.sizes lists every active size as digit strings: 6 kg "3000", 11.8 kg "4000", 15 kg "8000", 45.4 kg "15000".
- Step 2 returns a bare JSON array (not { items }). Sana's row has addresses[0].zone.name "North" and addresses[0].priceStatus "SET".
- client_addresses.zone_id is North's zone id.
- No audit_logs row is written for the new customer or its address.

Spec: ADR-08; API_CONTRACT §7.4, §7.5 (PriceView), §1.1, §1.3; DATA_MODEL §3.2 (ClientAddress.zoneId) · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/customers.e2e-spec.ts`

### CUS-002 · Customer phone rules: an invalid mobile gives 400, a duplicate in the same shop gives 409, and another shop may reuse the number

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA, DB)

Before: Standard test data: Sana (C1) exists for DA with phone +923001234567. DA and DB tokens. DB's South price is Rs 300 flat.

Expect:

- Step 3 returns 409 CLIENT_PHONE_EXISTS with details.clientId = Sana's id and details.name "Sana", and the message "Sana already has this number. Pick them from the list." No new DA customer is made.
- Step 4 returns 201 with client.phone "+923001234567". The response never mentions Sana or Ahmed Gas (no leak across shops).
- Step 5 has exactly one customer with +923001234567 (Sana), and no "Test Landline", "Test Short" or "Sana B".

### CUS-004 · Zone lookup for a pin inside a zone, on a border, and outside every zone

**P1** · AUTO-API · Inc 1 · Role: DISTRIBUTOR (DA), SUPER_ADMIN (SA1)

Before: Standard zones North, South and East are active; the Outside point is in no zone. DA and SA1 tokens. Know which of North and South has the smaller area (ST_Area of the seeded shapes).

Steps:

1. As DA, GET /pricing/quote?lat&lng for a point well inside North, then for a point well inside South.
2. As DA, GET /pricing/quote for a vertex of North that touches no other zone.
3. As DA, GET /pricing/quote five times for a vertex shared by North and South.
4. As DA, GET /pricing/quote for the Outside point.
5. As SA1, GET /zones/locate for the same five points.

Expect:

- Every call in steps 1-4 returns 200 (the quote never errors for coverage).
- Inside North: zone North and blockCode null. Inside South: zone South and blockCode null.
- North's outer vertex: zone North (border points count as inside).
- Shared vertex: the same single zone all five times, namely the one with the smaller area (if the areas are equal, the one created first, then the lower id).
- Outside: serviceable false, zone null, price null, blockCode "PRICING_ZONE_NOT_COVERED".
- GET /zones/locate gives the same zone for each point, and no zone for Outside.

Spec: ADR-08; API_CONTRACT §5.6 (zone lookup), §7.5 (GET /pricing/quote), §7.2 (GET /zones/locate); DATA_MODEL §6 (6) · Test file: `apps/api/test/orders/customers.e2e-spec.ts`

Note: Use exact polygon vertices: points in the middle of an edge suffer floating-point error. The response shape of GET /zones/locate isn't in the docs; compare the zone id only.

- No screen shows 'zone', 'client', 'admin', 'Rs.', a code such as PRICING_PRICE_NOT_SET, or a long ID.

Spec: ADR-08; UX_MOBILE S8, §0 (plain words), §2.2 (Toast, Field); API_CONTRACT §7.5 (GET /pricing/quote), §7.4

Note: The line under the map refreshes about half a second after the pin stops moving.
