- **G03-02.** No maximum delivery price is defined (API_CONTRACT §7.5, §2.3 PRICE_INVALID 'Rs 0 or more'), so 'too large' is undefined; values beyond the BigInt range risk a 500. **Settled:** Each delivery price amount (basePaisa and every perCylinderPaisa) is at most Rs 100,000 (10,000,000 paisa), inclusive; above it is PRICE_INVALID. PRICE_INVALID's English becomes "Enter whole rupees, from Rs 0 to Rs 100,000." (no parameters), in ERROR_MESSAGE_EN and VALIDATION_MESSAGE_EN alike. With orders capped at 100 cylinders this keeps every order total at or below Rs 10,100,000, far inside safe integers and the BigInt column, so no amount can cause a 500 (the built paisaSchema already refuses more than 16 digits). The database CHECKs stay >= 0. The §7.5 PUT sentence is the single replacement given under G03-01.
- **G03-03.** LocationQuote.serviceable is not defined for a zone that is found but has no price, the PRICING_PRICE_NOT_SET case (API_CONTRACT §7.5). **Settled:** LocationQuote.serviceable = (blockCode === null): true only when an active zone covers the pin and this distributor has a price there. A zone found without a price: { serviceable: false, zone: {id, name}, price: null, blockCode: 'PRICING_PRICE_NOT_SET' }. Outside every active zone: { serviceable: false, zone: null, price: null, blockCode: 'PRICING_ZONE_NOT_COVERED' }.
- **G03-04.** The response status and body of PUT and DELETE /pricing/prices are not specified (API_CONTRACT §7.5). **Settled:** PUT /pricing/prices/:distributorId/:zoneId answers 200 (first save or edit) with the zone's grid row, the built PriceGridZone: { zone: { id, name, cityName, isActive }, price: { basePaisa, sizes: [{ cylinderTypeId, perCylinderPaisa }] for every active size (missing '0'), updatedAt, updatedBy: { id, name } } }. A PUT whose base, per-size amounts (missing = 0) and note equal the stored price changes nothing, writes no price.set row, and still answers 200 with the row. DELETE /pricing/prices/:distributorId/:zoneId { reason (5–300) } answers 200 with the same row and price: null, auditing price.remove with the old price as before; with no price set it answers 200 with X-Already-Applied: true, price null and no audit row; it works on archived zones too. An unknown distributor or zone: 404 NOT_FOUND; a size that isn't an active cylinder type: 404 NOT_FOUND {field: 'sizes'}; PUT on an archived zone: 409 ZONE_ARCHIVED.
- **G03-05.** Customer phone uniqueness under concurrency: the unique index clients(distributor_id, phone) only arrives in inc1b (DATA_MODEL §3.5), so in Inc 1 two parallel POST /clients with the same phone can both pass the service check (API_CONTRACT §7.4 rule 2). **Settled:** POST /clients, and from Inc 2 PATCH /clients/:id when the phone changes, check phone uniqueness twice: once before the zone and price lookup (so the rule order 1-2-3-4 holds for the error a caller sees), and again inside the create transaction after locking the distributor row (SELECT id FROM distributors WHERE id = \$d FOR UPDATE). Two adds of one number at the same moment therefore give one 201 and one 409 CLIENT_PHONE_EXISTS {clientId, name} even in Inc 1, before the inc1b unique index. From inc1b, clients_distributor_id_phone_key is the safety net: the service maps its P2002 to the same 409 with the existing customer's id and name. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key is answered by the key lookup first (G15-01) and never reaches these checks. Adding an address needs no lock.
- **G03-06.** What the office gets from GET /clients without ?distributorId is not defined (API_CONTRACT §7.4). **Settled:** GET /clients for the office (SUPER_ADMIN) requires ?distributorId=: without it, 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields [{path: 'distributorId', code: 'REQUIRED'}]; a malformed id is VALIDATION_FAILED (INVALID_ID); an id of no distributor gives 200 []. A distributor always gets its own customers and any distributorId it sends is ignored (the token decides). The response stays a bare array. No office screen lists customers in the pilot, so this only closes today's unfiltered leak.
- **G03-07.** API_CONTRACT Appendix B has no audit action for creating a customer or adding an address (only client.update, Inc 2), so customer creation is not audited. **Settled:** No audit row for adding a customer or an address, by design: it is the distributor's own data, recorded on the rows themselves (clients.created_at, client_addresses.created_at, distributor_id; a distributor has exactly one user). Customer edits are audited from Inc 2 (client.update). Appendix B says so explicitly.
- **G03-08.** Editing a customer (API_CONTRACT §9.4, Inc 2) can't change the address, and editing or removing an address isn't specified, so the only way to change zone is to add an address (§7.4). Archiving a zone (§7.2) doesn't say what happens to a store or saved addresses inside it. **Settled:** Addresses are add-only in the pilot: no edit or delete route, and PATCH /clients/:id (Inc 2) changes name, phone and notes only; to change where a customer gets deliveries, add an address (POST /clients/:id/addresses, same coverage check) and pick it on the order. GET /clients and GET /clients/:id/addresses report each address's zone and priceStatus from a live check of the pin (active zones only, the §5.6 rule, then this distributor's price there); client_addresses.zone_id keeps the zone at save time for the record only. Archiving a zone takes it out of every lookup at once: pins inside it quote as the next active zone covering them, else PRICING_ZONE_NOT_COVERED (saved addresses then show zone null and OUTSIDE; adding customers or addresses there is refused). The distributors' price rows for it are kept (not counted in coverage; PUT gives ZONE_ARCHIVED; DELETE still works) and apply again if it is reactivated. A store inside it is untouched: trips still start there, and its zone is recomputed only when the store is edited (STORE_OUTSIDE_ZONES then). Placed orders keep their stored cost and destination zone. The zone-archive sentences are part of the single §7.2 zones-row replacement given under G03-10.
- **G03-09.** Legacy pricing routes: 'frozen' for pricing_rules (API_CONTRACT §5.1, §7.2) isn't defined. Writes could be refused, or kept but unused. **Settled:** 'Frozen' means kept as it is for old data, office only, and never read on the money path: GET /pricing/city/:cityId and POST /pricing/rules keep today's shapes and still read and write pricing_rules for the office, but no quote, order or fee reads that table (DISTRIBUTOR_ZONE uses only distributor_zone_prices), no new screen calls them, and the table is dropped after the pilot. Old orders keep their stored cost (fee_strategy LEGACY_ZONE_PAIR).
- **G03-10.** Zones (API_CONTRACT §7.2): the POST /zones body (GeoJSON shape), its success status and any audit row are undocumented. Appendix B has no zone action, although zones decide delivery prices. **Settled:** Zones keep today's legacy shapes, office only: POST /zones { cityId (uuid), name (2–60, trimmed), polygonGeoJson (GeoJSON MultiPolygon) } answers 201 { id }; PATCH /zones/:id { name?, polygonGeoJson? } answers 200 { ok: true } (an isActive in the body is ignored, so archive and reactivate are always audited); DELETE /zones/:id (archive) and PATCH /zones/:id/reactivate answer 200 { ok: true }, and repeating either answers 200 with X-Already-Applied: true. A shape must be a non-empty MultiPolygon passing ST_IsValid with area > 0, else 400 ZONE_INVALID_SHAPE; an unknown cityId is 404 NOT_FOUND {field: 'cityId'}; overlaps aren't checked over the API (the deterministic lookup decides; the setup file refuses them). Every change writes an audit row in the same transaction (new actions zone.create, zone.update, zone.archive, zone.reactivate; no reason required) with diff { before, after } of { name, isActive, areaKm2 }, because zones decide delivery prices. The same zones-row replacement carries the archive consequences decided in G03-08.

### Orders and cancels

- **G04-01.** Cancel note length: API_CONTRACT §1.5 says a cancel with reason OTHER needs a 3-300 character note, while §7.6 (POST /orders/:id/cancel) says 5-300, and that the office always needs one. The minimum for an office cancel with OTHER is ambiguous. **Settled:** As built in shared-validation (cancelOrderSchema, officeCancelOrderSchema): from the owning distributor the cancel note is optional, required for OTHER, and 3–300 characters when sent (API_CONTRACT §1.5); from the office it is always required and 5–300 characters, whatever the reason, so an office OTHER also needs 5–300. /fail follows the same split (failOrderSchema, officeFailOrderSchema): the trip's driver needs a 3–300 note for OTHER only, the office always needs 5–300. A missing or short note is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on 'note' (NOTE_REQUIRED or TOO_SHORT).
- **G04-02.** orders.deliveryStartedAt is read at cancel time (API_CONTRACT §5.5: the rule used is saved in the audit row), but the refund sentence shown at placement (UX_MOBILE S9) comes from /app/config, cached 5 minutes (UX_MOBILE §3.6). A setting change can contradict what the distributor was told. Decide whether the rule should be stored on the order. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** The rule is not stored on the order (already written in ADR-07). OrdersFeePolicy reads orders.deliveryStartedAt from SettingsService each time the terms are computed (GET, cancel), so a change applies at once to every open order that hasn't started, including orders placed before the change; the order.cancel audit row records the rule used (startedRule). OrderDto.cancel (computed live) and confirmRefundPaisa are what the distributor relies on at cancel time, and ORDER_CANCEL_TERMS_CHANGED catches a change between viewing and confirming. To keep the placement sentence true, the shop app refetches GET /app/config when 'Check and place' opens instead of using its 5-minute copy (already in UX_MOBILE), and the office Settings row says a change applies to orders already placed. This is the reading closest to the owner's words: a cancel refunds only if delivery has not started when the cancel happens.
- **G04-03.** Legacy orders: API_CONTRACT §8.1 says orders from before the switch-over never move money, but §5.5 cancelTerms refunds any DEDUCTED order not yet started, including orders backfilled to DEDUCTED (DATA_MODEL §3.4 backfill 3). **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** Only a cost this platform deducted at placement can come back (already written in ADR-07). cancelTerms.refundPaisa = the fee when the fee status is DEDUCTED, fee_strategy is not LEGACY_ZONE_PAIR, and delivery has not started; otherwise 0. noRefundReason is DELIVERY_STARTED only when such an order has started; a legacy order (backfilled DEDUCTED with LEGACY_ZONE_PAIR, or NONE) or a zero-cost order has refundPaisa '0' and noRefundReason null. A legacy order can still be cancelled while open, but the cancel never calls WalletService.reverse; reverse itself returns null when there is no ledger row keyed order:\<id>:debit, which legacy orders never have (their old debits carry legacy:\<id> keys). This makes §5.5 agree with §8.1 (old orders never move money), the reading closest to the owner's 'the delivery cost is deducted when the order is placed ... refunded only if the delivery has not started'.
- **G04-04.** Order line validation overlap: the body schema in API_CONTRACT §7.6 (1-6 lines, fullCount 1-30, unique sizes) overlaps rule 3 (ORDER_LINES_INVALID / ORDER_TOO_MANY_CYLINDERS); which code an empty list, a 0 count or a duplicate size gets is not stated. The per-line cap of 30 also stays when orders.maxCylindersPerOrder (§6, 1-100) is raised above 30. **Settled:** The body schema checks the lines before rules 1–7, for POST /orders and POST /orders/quote: 1–6 lines, distinct cylinderTypeId, fullCount an integer 1–100, expectedReturnCount an integer 0–100. No lines, more than 6 lines, a repeated size, or a fullCount below 1 give 400 ORDER_LINES_INVALID when the body has no other problem (the promoted code, §2.2), else VALIDATION_FAILED with those fields coded ORDER_LINES_INVALID; a count above 100 or not an integer is VALIDATION_FAILED. Rule 3 in the service then refuses Σ fullCount > orders.maxCylindersPerOrder with 400 ORDER_TOO_MANY_CYLINDERS {max}. The per-line bound is the setting's own ceiling (100), so the setting (1–100, default 30) is the only cap that bites, a single line included: the built ORDER_LINE_MAX_COUNT changes from 30 to 100. The quote's error list is the single edit given under G04-08.
- **G04-05.** allowedActions (API_CONTRACT §1.6, §7 OrderDto) has no table by role and state, and when TRACK is offered isn't defined. **Settled:** OrderDto.allowedActions is computed per request for the caller, listed in ORDER_ACTIONS order, and is [] for DELIVERED, CANCELLED and FAILED orders. CANCEL: owning distributor and office, when cancel.allowed (status PENDING, CONFIRMED, ASSIGNED or IN_TRANSIT and no hand-over started). ASSIGN: office, status PENDING or CONFIRMED. REASSIGN: office, status ASSIGNED and loadStartedAt null (nothing loaded on its trip). MARK_FAILED: office and the trip's driver, status ASSIGNED or IN_TRANSIT, delivery started under the current orders.deliveryStartedAt, and no hand-over started. MANUAL_DELIVERY: office, status ASSIGNED or IN_TRANSIT. TRACK: owning distributor and office, when the stage is ON_THE_WAY. A driver never gets CANCEL, ASSIGN, REASSIGN, MANUAL_DELIVERY or TRACK; a distributor never gets ASSIGN, REASSIGN, MARK_FAILED or MANUAL_DELIVERY.
- **G04-06.** GET /orders?tab=active|done and the board's in-progress tab (API_CONTRACT §7.6) don't define which statuses belong to each. **Settled:** Distributor GET /orders?tab=active: status PENDING, CONFIRMED, ASSIGNED or IN_TRANSIT; tab=done: DELIVERED, CANCELLED or FAILED, from any date; both newest first by createdAt, then id. Office board: needs-driver = PENDING or CONFIRMED, oldest first; in-progress = ASSIGNED or IN_TRANSIT, any day; done-today = DELIVERED with deliveredAt in the current business day; cancelled-failed = CANCELLED or FAILED with cancelledAt or failedAt in the current business day or the 6 before it; all = every order; every tab but needs-driver is newest first by createdAt, then id. counts give the sizes of the four tabs, with the distributorId filter applied and q ignored. GET /admin/summary (needsDriver, inProgress) and GET /distributor/home (orders.active = the size of the active tab, onTheWay = stage ON_THE_WAY, deliveredToday = DELIVERED in the business day) use the same sets.
- **G04-07.** Two races aren't specified (API_CONTRACT §4.3, §7.6): an office manual delivery racing the driver's Delivered tap (§4.3 gives X-Already-Applied only for 'the same kind of action', and the loser's code isn't named); and a cancel racing could-not-deliver after loading (which row lock decides, and what /fail returns on an already-CANCELLED order, aren't stated). **Settled:** Every order transition (cancel, fail, the driver's Delivered tap, the office manual delivery, the first-load stamp) first locks the order row (SELECT … FOR UPDATE) in its transaction; whoever gets the lock first wins, and the other then reads the new state. 'The same kind of action' (§4 rule 3) means the same route's action, whoever calls it: any two cancels (distributor or office, /cancel or PATCH status CANCELLED) and any two fails (/fail or PATCH status FAILED) are the same kind, and a repeated cancel answers with what the first cancel returned; the driver's tap (Inc 2: the visit finish) and the office manual delivery are different kinds. Losers: a tap after a manual delivery, or the reverse → 409 ORDER_INVALID_TRANSITION {from: 'DELIVERED', to: 'DELIVERED', currentStatus: 'DELIVERED'}; a cancel after a fail → 409 ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE {currentStatus: 'FAILED'}; a fail after a cancel → 409 ORDER_INVALID_TRANSITION {from: 'CANCELLED', to: 'FAILED', currentStatus: 'CANCELLED'}. /fail checks, after the role and ownership checks (G11-02) and under the lock: FAILED → 200 X-Already-Applied; DELIVERED or CANCELLED → 409 ORDER_INVALID_TRANSITION; a hand-over started → 409 ORDER_HANDOVER_STARTED; PENDING or CONFIRMED, or delivery not started → 409 ORDER_NOT_STARTED_USE_CANCEL; else FAILED. The manual-delivery repeat and wrong-status rules are G06-09's edit (same rule: DELIVERED by MANUAL → 200 X-Already-Applied; any other status → 409 ORDER_INVALID_TRANSITION).
- **G04-08.** DISTRIBUTOR_NO_STORE (API_CONTRACT §7.6 rule 1) can only happen for legacy distributors before inc1b. It isn't stated whether POST /orders/quote checks the store, even though DeliveryFeeStrategy.quote needs originStore (§5.6). **Settled:** POST /orders/quote runs the body schema and rules 1–4 of POST /orders, writing nothing and ignoring quotedTotalPaisa, so a distributor with no home store gets 409 DISTRIBUTOR_NO_STORE from the quote too (after DISTRIBUTOR_NOT_ACTIVE). DeliveryFeeStrategy.quote takes originStore from the distributor's home store, never from the body. GET /pricing/quote stays 200 always and doesn't need the store, because the DISTRIBUTOR_ZONE price depends only on the customer's zone; POST /clients doesn't check the store either. DISTRIBUTOR_NO_STORE can only occur for a legacy distributor before inc1b makes home_store_id NOT NULL; the code stays in the catalogue. This edit also carries the quote's error list for G04-04.

### Assignment, trips and driver scans

- **G05-01.** Trip auto-start vs the LOADING stage: API_CONTRACT §8.3 says the first load scan starts the trip, and §8.1 says ASSIGNED -> IN_TRANSIT on 'trip start'. If a start triggered by a load scan counts, orders jump to ON_THE_WAY and the LOADING stage (§1.4) never shows in Inc 1. **Settled:** Starting a trip (the driver's PATCH /trips/:id/status IN_PROGRESS, the first arrive, the first load scan, or the auto-start of a PLANNED trip on the Delivered tap) only sets the trip IN_PROGRESS with startedAt; it never changes the trip's orders. An order moves ASSIGNED → IN_TRANSIT (setting onTheWayAt) only when its trip's STORE_PICKUP stop departs (Inc 1: PATCH /trips/stops/:id/depart, which the installed DeliveryStepsScreen calls when loading is done; Inc 2: the "Done loading" finish) or by the driver's legacy PATCH /orders/:id/status IN_TRANSIT on their own trip. So Inc 1 shows the same stages as Inc 2: DRIVER_ASSIGNED → LOADING (first load scan) → ON_THE_WAY (left the store) → DELIVERED.
- **G05-02.** An office abort of a trip (API_CONTRACT §7.7, §8.3) doesn't say what happens to its orders (back to PENDING / Needs a driver, or left ASSIGNED on an aborted trip). **Settled:** The office may abort a trip (PATCH /trips/:id/status { status: 'ABORTED', reason 5–300 }) only while nothing has happened on it: no cylinder event with its trip_id, no stop with arrivedAt or departedAt, and every order on it ASSIGNED with loadStartedAt null (or CANCELLED); otherwise 409 TRIP_INVALID_TRANSITION {currentStatus}. One transaction locks the trip's orders, then the trip, sets the trip ABORTED and every open stop CANCELLED, and sends each ASSIGNED order back to PENDING with trip_id and assigned_at cleared (stage NEEDS_DRIVER, listed under "Needs a driver" again), so the order is exactly as it was before assignment under every orders.deliveryStartedAt value; no money moves. It writes one audit row trip.abort\* {orderIds}; a repeat on an ABORTED trip answers 200 with X-Already-Applied, and the system's own abort (the trip's last open order cancelled or reassigned) writes no trip.abort row, because the order.cancel or order.reassign row covers it.
- **G05-03.** assign-driver (API_CONTRACT §7.6) has no Idempotency-Key and no rule that repeating the same driver does nothing, so a double submit is treated as a reassign (the trip just made is aborted and a new one created), although UX_ADMIN §1.7 sends a key with every mutation. **Settled:** assign-driver locks the order row FOR UPDATE before anything else. After the status rule, if the order is already ASSIGNED on a PLANNED or IN_PROGRESS trip of the same driver, nothing changes and the answer is 200 with X-Already-Applied and the current { tripId, driverId, originStoreId }, with no audit row; a different driver is a reassign under rule 4. An Idempotency-Key header, if sent, is not read: the repeat is detected from the order's state (§4 pattern 3).
- **G05-04.** The ASSIGN_ORDER_LOADED message (API_CONTRACT §2.3) says 'Ask the store to scan them back in first'. But §7.6 assign-driver rule 4 refuses whenever any load scan or loadStartedAt exists, so a store scan-in can never allow the reassignment (DRV-041). **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** ADR-12, as it now reads, is permanent: once the order's trip has any load scan, or the order has loadStartedAt, assign-driver answers 409 ASSIGN_ORDER_LOADED {plateNo}, even after the store has scanned every cylinder back in. The message stops suggesting a store scan-in and becomes "Cylinders are already loaded on {{plateNo}}, so this order can't change driver."
- **G05-05.** Double scan with a NEW scanId: API_CONTRACT §9.2 step 4 defines a replay only by scanId. §7.7 (legacy) says a repeat of the same move returns alreadyRecorded, and STORE_RECEIVE gives a soft ALREADY_RECORDED, but LOAD, HANDOVER and TAKE_BACK say nothing. A re-scan would therefore hit SCAN_NOT_AT_STORE or SCAN_NOT_ON_YOUR_VAN, while UX_MOBILE §7.1 expects 'Already scanned'. HLD-008 and DRV-017 assume ALREADY_RECORDED. **Settled:** A scan that repeats a move already recorded, sent with a new scanId, answers 200 with result ALREADY_RECORDED and X-Already-Applied: true and writes nothing (no event, no stop row, no typed-entry audit); a resend with the same scanId answers 200 ALREADY_RECORDED with Idempotent-Replay: true, even if the rules would now refuse it. A move counts as already recorded when: LOAD — the cylinder's last move is a LOAD on this trip and it is still on the trip's van; HANDOVER — it has a GIVEN row on this stop; TAKE_BACK — it has a TAKEN_BACK row on this stop (the first returnState stays); STORE_RECEIVE — it is already in the caller's store; refill PICKUP — it has an open line on this refill; refill FILL — its line already has filled_at. The legacy POST /custody/scan applies the same test (the cylinder's last event is the same event type on the same trip, and the same order, and the cylinder is still at that event's destination) and answers 200 with X-Already-Applied and its usual body plus alreadyRecorded: true.
- **G05-06.** The order of checks when several scan rules fail is not given (API_CONTRACT §9.2). Examples: a DB cylinder recorded at Bilal Gas's store (SCAN_NOT_AT_STORE or SCAN_WRONG_OWNER?), and a load at a finished store stop (SCAN_STOP_CLOSED or SCAN_LOAD_NOT_NEEDED?). SCAN_STOP_CLOSED appears only in the LOAD row, yet it should cover every driver scan. **Settled:** Every scan (driver, store, refill and the legacy route) runs its checks in one fixed order and stops at the first failure: body (400) → context and ownership (404) → resend by scanId (200 Idempotent-Replay, or 409 SCAN_ID_REUSED) → trip, stop and action fit (SCAN_TRIP_CLOSED; SCAN_STOP_CLOSED for every driver scan; SCAN_EVENT_NOT_ALLOWED; refills REFILL_WRONG_STEP) → typed-entry switch (FEATURE_DISABLED) → resolve the code (SCAN_CYLINDER_UNKNOWN) → lock the cylinder → owner (SCAN_WRONG_OWNER) → the same move again (200 ALREADY_RECORDED) → FAULTY or LOST (SCAN_CYLINDER_BLOCKED) → the action's own rules in the order its table row lists them. A LOAD (and a legacy SCAN_OUT) locks the trip's orders before it reads the trip, and every path locks orders first, then the trip, then the cylinder, so a cancel or a reassign racing a load always gives one winner. So another distributor's cylinder gives SCAN_WRONG_OWNER wherever it is, any scan at a finished stop gives SCAN_STOP_CLOSED, and a legacy SCAN_OUT after "Done loading" (Inc 2) gives SCAN_STOP_CLOSED.
- **G05-07.** No error code exists for a scan whose action doesn't fit the stop type, such as LOAD at a DELIVERY stop or HANDOVER/TAKE_BACK at the STORE_PICKUP stop (API_CONTRACT §9.2, §9.3). **Settled:** A scan whose action doesn't fit the stop — LOAD with a DELIVERY stopId, HANDOVER or TAKE_BACK with the STORE_PICKUP stopId — and a PUT of unlabelled returns on the STORE_PICKUP stop answer 403 SCAN_EVENT_NOT_ALLOWED ("This scan isn't allowed.") and change nothing. It is checked with the trip-open and stop-open checks (§9.2 step 3, after the resend lookup); no new code is needed, because the apps only send the action of the screen they are on.
- **G05-08.** With custody.typedEntry.enabled=false, the server's answer to a TYPED scan is not specified (API_CONTRACT §6, §9.2); FEATURE_DISABLED is assumed (DRV-033). The accepted typed formats are not stated either: §1.1 shows only '0042', not '42' or 'AG-0042'. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** A TYPED scan (driver, store or refill) while custody.typedEntry.enabled is false answers 403 FEATURE_DISABLED before any lookup; QR scans keep working, and the office's manual delivery and Find cylinder are not governed by the switch. Typed entry accepts a cylinder number as 42, 0042, C0042 or AG-C0042 in any letter case (parseCylinderNo in shared-utils, as in G16-02), resolved within the run's distributor (driver, refill) or the caller's (store); another distributor's code part, the order-style AG-0042, or no match answers 404 SCAN_CYLINDER_UNKNOWN. The AG-C0042 form is the fixed choice of principle 8, and the owner can veto it before labels are printed.
- **G05-09.** trip.allowFinishWithLeftovers on but no leftoverReason: §9.3 gives no error code and no reason length. The day-cutoff-van-check (§9.9) 'after a finished run' can only happen with this setting on, and that finish already raised VAN_NOT_EMPTY. Deduplication is not stated (DRV-039, DRV-043). **Settled:** POST /trips/:tripId/finish takes leftoverReason as 5–300 characters after trimming (else 400 VALIDATION_FAILED). With the van not empty: trip.allowFinishWithLeftovers off → 409 TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY with details.leftoversAllowed false whatever the body; on without a reason → the same 409 with leftoversAllowed true, so the app asks for one; on with a reason → 200, the trip COMPLETED with leftover_reason, the cylinders stay on the van, and a VAN_NOT_EMPTY alert. VAN_NOT_EMPTY (WARNING) is kept to one unresolved (OPEN or ACKNOWLEDGED) alert per van: a new raise by a finish or by the 03:00 day-cutoff-van-check only updates its context {vehicleId, plateNo, count, tripId, leftoverReason}, and it stays until the office resolves it. The job raises it for every van that holds at least one cylinder not on an open refill line, whatever its trips (a run still in progress at 03:00 is worth seeing too).
- **G05-10.** Strict body validation of unknown fields (e.g. toCustodyId) is stated only for the legacy route (API_CONTRACT §7.7). §5.9 says clients can never pass a destination, but §9.3 and §9.4 don't say whether POST /trips/:id/scans and POST /store/scans reject such fields or strip them. **Settled:** Every scan body — the legacy POST /custody/scan, POST /trips/:tripId/scans, POST /store/scans and POST /filling-orders/:id/scans — refuses toCustodyType and toCustodyId with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (field code NOT_ALLOWED), as the built custodyScanSchema already does, and drops any other unknown field rather than refusing it. The holder a scan moves to is always derived on the server.
- **G05-11.** Repeat semantics for stop finish, trip finish and manual delivery v2 are not restated (API_CONTRACT §9.3, §9.5); the general §4 pattern 3 (200 X-Already-Applied) is assumed. **Settled:** Repeats follow §4 pattern 3. A stop finish on a stop already DONE returns 200 with X-Already-Applied and the same body whatever the new body ({ order: null, nextStopId } for the STORE_PICKUP stop), and a CANCELLED or FAILED stop gives 409 SCAN_STOP_CLOSED {currentStatus}. A trip finish, or a legacy PATCH /trips/:id/status that repeats the status the trip already has by a caller who may make that change (the driver: IN_PROGRESS or COMPLETED; the office: ABORTED), returns 200 with X-Already-Applied, while an ABORTED trip gives 409 TRIP_INVALID_TRANSITION {currentStatus}; Inc 1 stop arrive and depart repeats return 200 with X-Already-Applied. The legacy PATCH COMPLETED maps to the Inc 2 finish with its reason used as leftoverReason, and manual delivery repeats follow G06-09.
- **G05-12.** The bulk-register body shape is not given (API_CONTRACT §7.2, §9.5). Whether a driver on an IN_PROGRESS trip counts as AVAILABLE for assign-driver v2 is not stated (§7.6 rule 2 vs the 'On another run' label in UX_ADMIN §2.5). **Settled:** POST /cylinders/bulk-register (office) takes { distributorId, cylinderTypeId, quantity (1–500) or serials (1–500 distinct values of 3–128 characters, each used as serial and QR value), state?: 'FULL' | 'EMPTY' (default FULL), initialCustodyType?: 'STORE', initialCustodyId? } with exactly one of quantity or serials; the first holder is always the distributor's home store, so naming a van or another store gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (field code NOT_ALLOWED) and creates nothing. It answers 201 with the created cylinders (Inc 2 returns [{ id, code, shortNo, shortCode, sizeLabel }] for labels), 404 NOT_FOUND {field} for an unknown distributor or size, 409 DISTRIBUTOR_NO_STORE, 409 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE for a serial already used (nothing created), and writes one cylinders.bulk_register audit row from Inc 1. For assign-driver, a driver qualifies when the user is ACTIVE, drivers.availability is AVAILABLE (not ON_LEAVE or OFF_DUTY) and a van is set; being on another PLANNED or IN_PROGRESS trip, or offline, never blocks ("On another run" is information only).

### Holder rules, store receive and manual delivery

- **G06-01.** Unlabelled returns (API_CONTRACT §9.3; DATA_MODEL §4.3, §4.4): (a) do they count toward 'taken' for TAKE_BACK_SHORT, StopProgress.takeBack.count and 'Took back N' (UX_MOBILE R5)? (b) does a count of 0 in the PUT delete the row or get refused (CHECK count > 0)? (c) how do they reach the store? README Inc 2 says the store scans IN what comes back, but there is no store-side count, and TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY covers only labelled cylinders. The automated confirmation cases expect no returns to stay clear of (a); RHS-011 and MSG-022 still finish visits with only unlabelled returns against an expected take-back. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** As ADR-13 now reads, unlabelled and other-brand returns count as taken back: StopProgress.takeBack.count is the labelled TAKEN_BACK rows plus the stop's unlabelled counts, byState includes both, and TAKE_BACK_SHORT and "Took back N" compare that total with the order's Σ expectedReturnCount (more than expected is fine). PUT …/unlabelled-returns replaces the stop's whole list — at most 20 items { cylinderTypeId, state EMPTY | PART_FILLED | FULL, count 0–30 }, one per size and state (else 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, DUPLICATE_ITEM) — where a count of 0 or a pair left out means none and no row is kept (so CHECK count > 0 holds); it works only at an open DELIVERY stop of the caller's open trip (403 SCAN_EVENT_NOT_ALLOWED at the store stop, 409 SCAN_STOP_CLOSED or SCAN_TRIP_CLOSED once closed), an unknown size gives 404 NOT_FOUND {field}, and the first PUT at a PENDING stop sets arrivedAt like a first scan. Unlabelled returns never get a holder: they aren't on the van, in GET /store/incoming, in TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY or on the day-end sheet; the driver hands them over by hand, and the shop and the office see their counts on the order.
- **G06-02.** Responsible driver after the cylinder leaves the van: API_CONTRACT §9.2 says 'the actor of the last event that moved it onto a van'. DATA_MODEL §4.2 says 'its actor, when the move was onto a van'. The owner's notes say 'whoever last scanned it IN', which after the store's SCAN_IN would be the store user. So holder.responsible (§9.4) is undefined for a cylinder with a customer or in the store, yet UX_ADMIN §3.5 shows it for a customer-held cylinder. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** As ADR-13 now reads, holder.responsible is the driver of the trip or refill of the latest event that moved the cylinder onto a van (LOAD, TAKE_BACK, refill PICKUP, or an office manual take-back onto the trip's van) since the cylinder last entered a store, sent as { userId, name, role: 'DRIVER' }. It is null while the cylinder is in a store (the store's scan IN ends it) and when no such event exists (registered and never loaded, or handed straight from the store by an office manual delivery); so a cylinder on a van or with a customer names the driver who last scanned it IN. It is read from cylinder_events (the newest onto-van event newer than the newest into-store event), not from last_event_id alone.
- **G06-03.** Hand-over of a cylinder still on the van from an earlier run (possible with trip.allowFinishWithLeftovers): ADR-13 forbids it, but the HANDOVER row in API_CONTRACT §9.2 names no error code for 'loaded on another trip'. HLD-011 assumes SCAN_NOT_ON_YOUR_VAN. **Settled:** A HANDOVER of a cylinder that is on this trip's van but whose last move onto the van was a LOAD on another trip (a leftover from an earlier run, possible with trip.allowFinishWithLeftovers) answers 409 SCAN_NOT_ON_YOUR_VAN, as ADR-13's "on this run" requires; the same code refuses a cylinder picked up for a refill. The leftover can't be loaded again either (SCAN_NOT_AT_STORE): the store must receive it first, and until then a trip finish lists it as came SPARE.
- **G06-04.** Load progress after the store scans a just-loaded cylinder back in: §9.3 doesn't say whether 'loaded' counts LOAD events or this trip's cylinders still on the van. LOAD_INCOMPLETE and SCAN_LOAD_NOT_NEEDED depend on it (STR-009). **Settled:** For the STORE_PICKUP stop, per size: needed = Σ fullCount of the trip's orders that aren't CANCELLED or FAILED, and loaded (StopProgress lines[].done) = the cylinders whose latest LOAD is on this trip and that haven't gone back into a store since (still on the van, or handed over on this trip); LOAD events are not counted, so a cylinder the store has taken back off no longer counts. LOAD gives SCAN_LOAD_NOT_NEEDED when loaded ≥ needed for its size, and "Done loading" needs loaded ≥ needed for every size, else 409 LOAD_INCOMPLETE { total: Σ needed, done: Σ min(loaded, needed), lines }, so spares from an order cancelled after loading never block it. load_started_at, once stamped, is never cleared.
- **G06-05.** Which store returns go to: the owner's notes say 'the driver chooses the store', but ADR-13 and API_CONTRACT §9.2 STORE_RECEIVE always use the caller's home store with owner = caller. With one store per distributor there is no choice; the docs should drop the notes' wording or define cross-store returns. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** Returns always go into the cylinder owner's one store: STORE_RECEIVE puts the cylinder into the caller's home store, needs the caller to own it (SCAN_WRONG_OWNER otherwise), and no body field can name another store. The owner's "the driver chooses the store" needs no choice while each distributor has exactly one store (owner decision of 2026-10-20, ADR-01), and it matches "a returned empty should go to its owner's store"; a second store per distributor would later add the choice as the receiving store's own scan, still with owner = caller.
- **G06-06.** Cylinder history words (UX_ADMIN §3.5) cover only SCAN_OUT, DELIVERED, PICKED_UP_EMPTY, SCAN_IN and ADJUSTED. REGISTERED, FILLED, TYPED and MANUAL (office) events have no words, and a refill pickup (SCAN_OUT with filling_order_id) would read 'Loaded onto van … at … store'. Plain-word history exists only on the website: the shop app has no cylinder-history screen (UX_MOBILE §7.3), although GET /cylinders/:code/history allows the owning distributor (API_CONTRACT §9.4). **Settled:** The office's cylinder history (UX_ADMIN §3.5) has a sentence for every event the pilot writes — REGISTERED, SCAN_OUT on a trip, SCAN_OUT for a refill, DELIVERED, PICKED_UP_EMPTY, FILLED, SCAN_IN, SCAN_IN that closes a refill line, ADJUSTED — one line for older event types, and suffixes for source TYPED (" · number typed in"), MANUAL (" · recorded by the office: {{reason}}") and a day-end REGISTERED. GET /cylinders/:code/history sends action (the event type) and refill { shortCode } | null, so a refill pickup never reads as a trip load. As UX_MOBILE §7.3 already says, the shop app has no cylinder-history screen in the pilot; the route stays open to the owning distributor for later and for support.
- **G06-07.** Before Inc 3 day-end, no pilot route marks a cylinder FAULTY or LOST, so test fixtures must set these states. A LOST cylinder on TAKE_BACK is not covered: §9.2 says only 'FAULTY stays FAULTY'. The success status of the legacy POST /custody/scan is not stated (§7.7). **Settled:** No pilot route marks a cylinder FAULTY or LOST before the Inc 3 day-end fixes, so tests set these states in fixtures; only an approved day-end fix changes them. For a FAULTY or LOST cylinder, LOAD, HANDOVER and refill PICKUP answer 409 SCAN_CYLINDER_BLOCKED, while TAKE_BACK and STORE_RECEIVE move it and keep its state (the tapped returnState is kept on the TAKEN_BACK row and shown in the take-back lists). The legacy POST /custody/scan follows the same rule (SCAN_OUT and DELIVERED blocked; PICKED_UP_EMPTY and SCAN_IN allowed, state kept), answers 201 with its existing body { event, cylinderId, newState, toType, toId } for a recorded move (the installed ScanScreen.tsx reads newState and toType), and 200 with X-Already-Applied and alreadyRecorded: true for a repeat (G05-05).
- **G06-08.** Manual delivery v2 (API_CONTRACT §9.5, UX_ADMIN §3.4): (a) no destination is given for the optional takenBack cylinders (the van or the store); (b) there is no error code for a named cylinder held by someone else (the UX chip says 'with another customer'; HLD-005 assumes MANUAL_DELIVERY_CYLINDERS_MISMATCH); (c) Appendix B lists both order.manual_delivery and custody.manual_event without saying per cylinder or per delivery. **Settled:** Manual delivery v2 checks, in order: the body (reason 10–300, cylinders 1–100 codes, takenBack 0–100 { code, returnState }), the status (G06-09), every code resolving within the order's distributor (404 SCAN_CYLINDER_UNKNOWN {code}); it then locks the cylinders in id order and refuses the whole request with 409 MANUAL_DELIVERY_CYLINDERS_MISMATCH { problems: [{ code, reason, holderType? }], sizes: [{ cylinderTypeId, sizeLabel, needed, named }] } if anything is wrong, moving nothing. The reasons are WRONG_OWNER, NOT_FULL, BLOCKED, WRONG_SIZE and NOT_AVAILABLE (not in the home store, and not on the order's trip van as a LOAD of that trip; holderType says where it is) for delivered cylinders, WRONG_OWNER and NOT_WITH_THIS_CUSTOMER for taken-back ones, and LISTED_TWICE across both lists; the counts per size must equal the order lines. On success the delivered cylinders move to the customer (DELIVERED, source MANUAL, GIVEN rows) and each taken-back cylinder moves CLIENT → the order's trip van (PICKED_UP_EMPTY, source MANUAL, trip_id set, state = returnState with FAULTY and LOST kept, TAKEN_BACK row), so it reaches the store by the normal receive scan; the DELIVERY stop becomes DONE and the order DELIVERED (MANUAL), with no money. Audit: one order.manual_delivery\* row per delivery (reason and both code lists) and one custody.manual_event\* row per cylinder moved (resourceType cylinder, {eventId, from, to, orderId}).
- **G06-09.** Manual delivery from the wrong status (PENDING, or already DELIVERED by the driver's tap) has no named error code in API_CONTRACT §7.6; UX_ADMIN §3.4 lists ORDER_INVALID_TRANSITION, but only for Inc 2. **Settled:** Manual delivery (v1 in Inc 1, v2 in Inc 2) locks the order row and is allowed only from ASSIGNED or IN_TRANSIT; a repeat after the office's own manual delivery (DELIVERED with delivery_method MANUAL) returns 200 with X-Already-Applied and the order, writing nothing. Every other status — PENDING or CONFIRMED (no driver yet), CANCELLED, FAILED, or DELIVERED by the driver (DRIVER_TAP or SCANNED) — answers 409 ORDER_INVALID_TRANSITION {from: \<status>, to: 'DELIVERED', currentStatus} and changes nothing, as G04-07 also states. v1 also sets the order's DELIVERY stop DONE.

### Customer confirmation, cases and messaging

- **G07-01.** Second-answer status conflict: CUSTOMER_PAGE §4 says an ANSWERED link returns 200 ('You already answered') for both GET and POST. API_CONTRACT §2.3 (CONFIRM_ALREADY_ANSWERED 409) and §9.11 ('A second answer gives 409') say 409. The README precedence rule doesn't rank CUSTOMER_PAGE.md against API_CONTRACT (and §9.7 calls CUSTOMER_PAGE 'the full spec'), so nothing breaks the tie. CNF-017 assumes 409 for the POST. **Settled:** API_CONTRACT decides routes, statuses and codes; CUSTOMER_PAGE decides page content and copy. On an ANSWERED link: GET and HEAD answer 200 ("Thank you" with ?done=1, else "You already answered"); a POST of the stored answer answers 303 to /c/:token?done=1 and records nothing (its comment is ignored); a POST of any other answer answers 409 with the "You already answered" page (CONFIRM_ALREADY_ANSWERED) and records nothing. In a race the guarded UPDATE … WHERE status = 'PENDING' picks one winner and every loser takes the same two branches. CUSTOMER_PAGE §4 and §7 already say this; API_CONTRACT §9.11, the README tie-break and CUSTOMER_PAGE §13 are left (the §9.7 heading is in the G07-07 replacement).
- **G07-02.** Repeated resolve: API_CONTRACT §4 rule 3 (a repeated finished action returns 200 with X-Already-Applied) contradicts §9.6 (a second resolve gives 409 CASE_ALREADY_RESOLVED) when the same admin double-clicks or retries. CAS-007 follows §9.6. **Settled:** POST /alerts/:id/resolve {note} (office): the note is trimmed and must be 5-300 characters, else 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (field note); an id that isn't a CUSTOMER_PROBLEM alert is 404 NOT_FOUND. One transaction locks the alert, moves it OPEN -> RESOLVED with resolved_at, resolved_by_user_id and resolution_note (new inc2 columns) and writes audit case.resolve (resourceType Alert, the note as reason); it answers 200 with a CaseDto (G07-21). A repeat on a case already RESOLVED by the same caller is the §4 rule 3 repeat: 200 with X-Already-Applied and the case unchanged (the first note stays), like a repeated approve. A case resolved by someone else answers 409 CASE_ALREADY_RESOLVED {by: their name, currentStatus: 'RESOLVED'}. The legacy PATCH /alerts/:id/acknowledge and PATCH /alerts/:id/resolve answer 404 NOT_FOUND for a CUSTOMER_PROBLEM alert, so a case only ever closes with a note and an audit row, and a case is only ever OPEN or RESOLVED.
- **G07-03.** Audit IP and user agent: API_CONTRACT §5.3 says AuditLogService fills IP, user agent and requestId from the request context. CUSTOMER_PAGE §12 says no IP or user agent is stored for answers, so the confirmation.answer (actor CUSTOMER) row needs an explicit exception. Its resourceType is also not specified (CUSTOMER_PAGE §7 step 5). **Settled:** AuditLogService.record fills ip, user_agent and request_id from the request context for USER and SYSTEM actors; for a CUSTOMER actor it always stores ip and user_agent as NULL and keeps request_id. The confirmation.answer row has actor {kind CUSTOMER, label 'link:\<orderShortCode>'}, resourceType 'Order', resourceId the order id, distributorId the order's distributor and diff {response}; confirmation.new_link also uses resourceType 'Order', so both show in the order's activity list. CUSTOMER_PAGE §7 step 5 and §12 already say this; API_CONTRACT §5.3 and Appendix B are left.
- **G07-04.** Unreachable CANCELLED state: API_CONTRACT §9.8 says PENDING → CANCELLED happens when 'the order is reversed after issue'. But §7.6 and §8.1 allow no cancel or reversal of a DELIVERED order. So the 410 'This link is no longer active' page (CUSTOMER_PAGE §4, §6) and the card's 'Not needed' pill (§10) can never be reached. **Settled:** ConfirmationStatus CANCELLED is reserved: no pilot route writes it, because a DELIVERED order can't be cancelled or reversed. Its 410 page "This link is closed" and the card's "Not needed" pill stay so a reserved value renders safely, and share and new-link treat it as closed (CONFIRM_CLOSED). The same 410 page is what a known link shows while confirmation.enabled is off (G07-07). CUSTOMER_PAGE §10 already marks it reserved; API_CONTRACT §9.8 and DATA_MODEL §4.1 are left. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-05.** Mock provider vs test mode: CUSTOMER_PAGE §1 and §8 don't say which check runs first under the pilot defaults (MESSAGING_PROVIDER=mock, messaging.testMode=true, empty allowlist). The row's errorCode could be MOCK_PROVIDER or NOT_A_TEST_PHONE. **Settled (the docs already said so):** The test-mode check runs before the provider: with messaging.testMode on and the number not in messaging.allowlist, the row ends SKIPPED with NOT_A_TEST_PHONE and the provider isn't called; otherwise the provider runs and the mock answers SKIPPED MOCK_PROVIDER. Under the pilot defaults (MESSAGING_PROVIDER=mock, test mode on, empty allowlist) every SMS row is therefore SKIPPED NOT_A_TEST_PHONE. CUSTOMER_PAGE §1 and §8 already say this; no doc edit is left.
- **G07-06.** Manual delivery issuing a link: CUSTOMER_PAGE §1 implies office manual deliveries issue a confirmation ('delivery_method SCANNED or MANUAL'). API_CONTRACT §9.5 and DATA_MODEL §4.5 (which mentions only 'Stop finish') don't say so. **Settled:** From Inc 2 every write that sets an order DELIVERED issues the confirmation in its own transaction when confirmation.enabled is on: the DELIVERY stop finish (and the legacy PATCH /orders/:id/status DELIVERED, which maps to it) and the office manual delivery v2. For a manual delivery the snapshot lists the named cylinders as delivered and its takenBack list as taken back (grouped by size and state, with no unlabelled counts); the SMS row and the after-commit send are the same as for a finish. CUSTOMER_PAGE §1 and §8 already say this; API_CONTRACT §9.5 and DATA_MODEL §4.5 are left.
- **G07-07.** Turning the setting on or off while links exist: the docs don't say what /c/:token does for links already sent once confirmation.enabled is switched off (API_CONTRACT §9.7 lists the public routes under 'only when confirmation.enabled'). They also don't say whether the expiry job keeps running, or what GET /orders/:id/confirmation returns for orders delivered while the setting was off. CONFIRM_NOT_READY says 'isn't delivered yet', and there is no back-fill. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** confirmation.enabled is one switch, and turning it off deletes nothing. While it is false: no delivery issues a confirmation; GET /orders/:id/confirmation, share and new-link answer 403 FEATURE_DISABLED with X-Feature-Disabled: confirmations for every caller and method (a setting switch, §3.4, checked right after sign-in); the public page answers a known, well-formed token with 410 and the page "This link is closed" (CONFIRM_LINK_INACTIVE) and records nothing, while bad or unknown tokens stay 404; the confirmation-expiry job keeps running. Switching it on never back-fills: an order delivered while it was off has confirmation null, its card stays hidden, and GET /orders/:id/confirmation answers 404 NOT_FOUND. Check order for the three routes: the switch 403; a driver or another distributor 404; not DELIVERED 409 CONFIRM_NOT_READY; no row 404 NOT_FOUND; then the route's own rules. This follows ADR-15 (Default) and CUSTOMER_PAGE's intro, which already state the behaviour; the owner can still change it. The full §9.7 replacement below also carries G07-01's heading, G07-08, G07-09 and G07-10. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-08.** Missing new-link rules (CUSTOMER_PAGE §2, §10; API_CONTRACT §9.7): (1) is it refused once the link is answered or expired? CONFIRM_CLOSED is stated only for share. (2) Does it honour Idempotency-Key? A retried new-link {send:'SMS'} rotates again and kills the link it just texted. (3) Does it copy an edited customer phone into delivery_confirmations.phone_e164? (4) Does the CLIENT_PHONE_INVALID check run before the rotation? **Settled:** POST /orders/:id/confirmation/new-link {send?: 'SMS'} takes an Idempotency-Key. After the common checks (G07-07), in order: the same key as the last rotation (new column delivery_confirmations.last_new_link_key) answers 200 with the current ConfirmationView and Idempotent-Replay: true, changing and sending nothing (the body isn't compared); a status other than PENDING, or now >= expiresAt, answers 409 CONFIRM_CLOSED; send 'SMS' while the customer's current phone isn't a Pakistani mobile answers 400 CLIENT_PHONE_INVALID before any change. Then one transaction: lock the row FOR UPDATE and re-check PENDING; tokenVersion + 1 and a new token_hash (the old link shows "We can't find this link"); phone_e164 refreshed from the customer's current phone (NULL if it isn't a mobile); last_new_link_key = the key (NULL without one, so every keyless call rotates); audit confirmation.new_link (resourceType Order); with SMS a QUEUED row confirm:\<orderId>:v\<n>:sms, sent after commit. It answers 200 with the ConfirmationView, and expiresAt never changes. CUSTOMER_PAGE §10 already says this; the API_CONTRACT §9.7 text is in the G07-07 replacement; §5.9 and DATA_MODEL §4.3 are left.
- **G07-09.** Share idempotency: DATA_MODEL §4.3 sets outbound_messages.idempotency_key to 'share:\<uuid>' but doesn't say whether the uuid is the request's Idempotency-Key (API_CONTRACT §1.2, §4). If it isn't, a retried share writes a second row. **Settled:** share uses the request's Idempotency-Key: the share row's idempotency_key is share:\<orderId>:\<Idempotency-Key>, or share:\<orderId>:\<new uuid> when none is sent. A repeat with the same key finds the row and answers 200 with the same body (re-derived, no rotation) and Idempotent-Replay: true, writing nothing; the same key with another via answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. After the common checks, in order: the replay; answered, expired or cancelled 409 CONFIRM_CLOSED; 20 share rows for the order created in the last 60 minutes 429 RATE_LIMITED {minutes: until the oldest of them is an hour old, rounded up, at least 1}; then the row is written. A replay is never limited. A concurrent duplicate fails on outbound_messages_idempotency_key_key and is answered as the replay. The API_CONTRACT §9.7 text is in the G07-07 replacement; DATA_MODEL §4.3 and the via conflict in CUSTOMER_PAGE §10 are left.
- **G07-10.** Messaging webhook: API_CONTRACT §9.7 says POST /webhooks/messaging/:provider returns 410, but §2.3 defines no error code for it (PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_DISABLED is for payments only). **Settled:** There is no messaging webhook in the pilot: no provider sends delivery reports, so POST /api/v1/webhooks/messaging/:provider is not registered and answers like any unknown path (404 NOT_FOUND, JSON), changing nothing. No new error code is needed. The route arrives with a provider that sends delivery reports (after the pilot), behind that provider's own signature check; PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_DISABLED stays payments-only. The API_CONTRACT §9.7 text (its last bullet) is in the G07-07 replacement.
- **G07-11.** CONFIRM_LINK_INVALID, CONFIRM_LINK_EXPIRED and CONFIRM_NOTE_REQUIRED are in the API_CONTRACT §2.3 catalogue, but the public page never returns JSON (CUSTOMER_PAGE §4-§5). Where these codes surface (perhaps only as page selectors in PublicPageExceptionFilter) isn't stated. **Settled:** The public-page codes are page selectors, never JSON. The service and controller throw AppError, and PublicPageExceptionFilter renders the page with the code's status: CONFIRM_LINK_INVALID 404 "We can't find this link"; CONFIRM_LINK_INACTIVE (new code: HTTP 410, English 'This link is no longer active.', no params) "This link is closed"; CONFIRM_LINK_EXPIRED 410 "This link has expired"; CONFIRM_ALREADY_ANSWERED 409 "You already answered"; CONFIRM_NOTE_REQUIRED 400, the Other page with its error; VALIDATION_FAILED 400, the main page with "Please tap one answer below."; RATE_LIMITED 429 "Too many tries"; anything else 500. A GET of an ANSWERED or PENDING link renders its 200 page directly. The JSON routes use only CONFIRM_NOT_READY and CONFIRM_CLOSED. CUSTOMER_PAGE §5 already has this mapping; API_CONTRACT §2.3 is left. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-12.** Failed-message words: UX_ADMIN §3.2's link status list (Not sent · Message sent · Shared · Answered · Expired) has no failed state, yet CUSTOMER_PAGE §8 defines 'Didn't send — {reason}' for 'shop app and web'. The CUSTOMER_PAGE §10 card table has no failed row either: not sent, SMS failed and skipped all use confirm.ask.smsOff ('Text messages are not switched on yet'). That text becomes wrong once SMS is live. **Settled:** One set of status words, built from reach and lastMessage of the current link version (G07-15). Shop card while PENDING: NOT_SENT, whatever the reason (no SMS row, a lost send, text messages off), reads "Link not sent yet · {{name}}, {{phone}}"; SMS_FAILED reads "Text didn't send: {{reason}}." with the §8 reasons; both keep "Send on WhatsApp" as the one main button. The website drawer uses the CUSTOMER_PAGE §8 words: 'Sending text…', 'Not sent', 'Not sent · text messages are off', 'Text sent {time}', 'Text delivered {time}' (later), 'Text didn't send · {reason}', 'Shared {time} by {byName} ({via})'; once closed, 'Answered {time}' or 'Expired'. CUSTOMER_PAGE §8 and §10 and UX_ADMIN §3.2 have these. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-13.** QUEUED display: CUSTOMER_PAGE §8 maps QUEUED to 'Waiting to send', but also says a row left QUEUED after a crash 'shows as Not sent'. Nothing says how to tell the two apart. ConfirmationView.reach (§10) has no value for SKIPPED or QUEUED; NOT_SENT is assumed. **Settled (the docs already said so):** reach comes from the newest message row of the current link version: none, SKIPPED, or an SMS still QUEUED 2 minutes or more after it was written gives NOT_SENT; QUEUED under 2 minutes gives SMS_SENDING (the card reads 'Sending text…' with 'Send again'); SENT or DELIVERED gives SMS_SENT; FAILED gives SMS_FAILED; a share gives SHARED. sendQueued gives the provider 15 seconds: no answer is FAILED TIMEOUT, a thrown error FAILED UNKNOWN (the detail only in the log). CUSTOMER_PAGE §8 and §10 already say this; no doc edit is left. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-14.** Missing copy keys: the {{via}} words in confirm.shared ('Link given at {{time}} ({{via}})') and {name} in 'Given to {name} to send' (CUSTOMER_PAGE §8, §10). UX_MOBILE §7.3 S15 doesn't say what the '{{n}} customer problems' line opens when tapped. **Settled (the docs already said so):** The {{via}} words come from confirm.via.\*: WHATSAPP 'WhatsApp', SMS 'text message', SHARE_SHEET 'other app', COPY 'copied' (the website uses the same words). The sharer is lastMessage.byName ('Shared {time} by {byName} ({via})'), which replaces 'Given to {name} to send'. The shop Home line is home.problems / home.problems_plural ('{{count}} customer problem' / '{{count}} customer problems') while GET /alerts/mine has open cases; tapping it opens the order when there is one case, else the Customer problems list (UX_MOBILE S15: the customer's name, '{{shortCode}} · “{{comment}}”', the time on the right and the answer chip), each row opening its order. The shop card says 'Shared {{time}} · {{via}}. Check it was sent.'. No new API. CUSTOMER_PAGE §10 and UX_MOBILE §7.3 S15 already say this; no doc edit is left. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-15.** Stale card after a new link: CUSTOMER_PAGE §10 builds reach and lastMessage from the last message. After 'Make a new link' the card can still say 'Link given at …' about the old link, which no longer works. **Settled:** Every outbound_messages row records the link version it carried (new column token_version, set on SMS and share rows). reach and lastMessage read only rows of the confirmation's current token_version, so right after a new link without SMS the view has reach NOT_SENT and lastMessage null, and the card is back to 'Link not sent yet · {{name}}, {{phone}}' (confirm.notSent). CUSTOMER_PAGE §10 already says this; DATA_MODEL §4.3 is left. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-16.** Wrong date examples: CUSTOMER_PAGE §3 has deliveredAt 2026-10-21T11:12Z, which is Wed 21 Oct, 4:12 pm PKT, but §6 shows 'Tue 21 Oct, 4:12 pm' (21 Oct was a Tuesday in 2025, not 2026). The skeleton's 'You can answer until Thu 24 Oct, 4:12 pm' is not 72 h after either reading (that would be Fri 24 Oct 2025 or Sat 24 Oct 2026). Snapshot tests copied from the skeleton would encode wrong weekdays. **Settled:** Date examples are 2026 dates and equal formatPkDateTime output (built in shared-utils): 2026-10-21T11:12Z is 'Wed 21 Oct, 4:12 pm', 72 hours later is 'Sat 24 Oct, 4:12 pm', and 19 Oct 2026 is a Monday. Snapshot tests are built from formatPkDateTime output, never copied from doc examples. CUSTOMER_PAGE and UX_ADMIN §1.6, §2.1 and §2.2 are already fixed; UX_ADMIN §4.3 still says 'Tue 21 Oct' twice.
- **G07-17.** Expiry wording: CUSTOMER_PAGE §6 doesn't say how '{3 days}' is written for linkTtlHours values that aren't whole days (24–168 is allowed, so 36 is possible). §2 and §11 also don't say whether a lifetime change affects links already issued. CNF-021 assumes it doesn't, since expiresAt is stored at issue. **Settled (the docs already said so):** expiresAt = deliveredAt + confirmation.linkTtlHours, read when the link is issued and stored; a setting change affects only links issued after it, and a new link never extends it. The expired page states the link's own lifetime (expires_at - snapshot.deliveredAt, in whole hours): a multiple of 24 reads '1 day' or '{n} days' (72 -> '3 days'), anything else '{n} hours' (36 -> '36 hours'). CUSTOMER_PAGE §2 and §6 already say this; no doc edit is left.
- **G07-18.** support.phone unset: the 404 page needs support.phone (CUSTOMER_PAGE §6), whose default is null (API_CONTRACT §6). The page text with no number isn't defined, and neither is whether the number is a tel: link. **Settled:** With support.phone null the 404 page shows only 'Please open the full link from your newest message.': the 'Need help? Call Smart Fleet support: …' sentence is left out, with no placeholder. When set, the number is a tel: link: the href is the E.164 form when normalizePkPhone accepts it (shown with formatPkPhone 'local'), else the stored value with spaces, dashes and brackets removed, keeping a leading + (shown as stored). Ops sets support.phone before switching confirmation on. CUSTOMER_PAGE §6 already has the page rule; API_CONTRACT §9.1 gains the ops line.
- **G07-19.** Input rules: CUSTOMER_PAGE §4 strips control characters from the comment, which also removes line breaks typed in the textarea and joins words. No page or status is defined for an invalid or missing 'answer' value; only OTHER without a note has a defined 400. **Settled (the docs already said so):** The comment is cleaned in this order: each CRLF, CR, LF and tab becomes one space; other control characters (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F) are removed; runs of spaces become one; the text is trimmed and cut to 300 code points (never splitting one); empty is stored NULL. OTHER's 3-character minimum applies to the cleaned text. The answer must be exactly YES, PARTLY, NO or OTHER (case-sensitive); a missing or other value on a PENDING link gets the main page again with 400 and 'Please tap one answer below.' (role='alert'), recording nothing; the hidden v is ignored; the state order runs before body checks. CUSTOMER_PAGE §4 already says this; no doc edit is left. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-20.** Best-effort case: CUSTOMER_PAGE §7 raises the case after commit with no retry or sweeper. If that fails, a 'Not received' answer ends with no case while the shop card still says 'The office will look into it.' **Settled:** The CUSTOMER_PROBLEM case is written in the answer's own transaction: AlertsService.raise gains an optional tx and ConfirmationsService.record passes it; confirmation.caseOnAnswers is read at answer time. If raising fails, the whole answer rolls back: the row stays PENDING, no audit row is written, the customer gets the 500 page ('Your answer was not saved. Please try again.') and its 'Try again' records answer and case together. So an answer that needs a case never ends without one, and the shop card's 'The office will look into it.' is always true. No sweeper; the dedupe (resource Order + order id + CUSTOMER_PROBLEM) is unchanged. CUSTOMER_PAGE §1 and §7 already say this; DATA_MODEL §4.5 is left.
- **G07-21.** Problems list scope: UX_ADMIN §3.3 queries GET /alerts?type=CUSTOMER_PROBLEM with no status, while API_CONTRACT §9.6 adds status=OPEN, so it's unclear whether resolved cases are listed. The empty-state text names only 'Not received' and 'Other', even when PARTLY is in caseOnAnswers. **Settled:** The Problems page lists open cases only. GET /alerts?type=CUSTOMER_PROBLEM&status=OPEN|RESOLVED&cursor (office) answers {items: CaseDto[], nextCursor}; status defaults to OPEN; OPEN lists oldest first, RESOLVED newest-resolved first. Any other type, or none, keeps the legacy array, which leaves CUSTOMER_PROBLEM alerts out (they live on the Problems page). GET /alerts/mine (DISTRIBUTOR exact, the one non-office /alerts route) answers {items: CaseDto[], nextCursor} with the caller's OPEN cases, oldest first. CaseDto = {id, status, order {id, shortCode}, answer, comment, customerName, distributor {id, businessName}, openedAt, resolvedAt, resolvedBy {id, name} | null, resolutionNote, allowedActions ('RESOLVE')[]}. The empty state no longer names answers, since caseOnAnswers can add Partly: one line, 'No customer problems'. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G07-22.** Missing office copy: UX_ADMIN §2.9 has no Activity sentence for confirmation.answer, confirmation.new_link or case.resolve, and no display rule for actor kind CUSTOMER (only 'System'). §2.1 Today has no customer-problems card, though its all-clear text mentions problems. §1.3 'Orders (badge … Inc 2 adds problems)' doesn't make clear which badge counts cases. No toast text is given for 'Mark as sorted'. **Settled:** Office copy. Activity sentences: confirmation.answer 'Customer answered “{{answer}}” for {{no}}' (the answer label words), confirmation.new_link 'Made a new customer link for {{no}}', case.resolve 'Marked the problem on {{no}} as sorted'. The Who column shows CUSTOMER actors as 'Customer' (the link label is never shown) and SYSTEM actors as 'System'. The 'Mark as sorted' toast is 'Problem on {{no}} marked as sorted.' From Inc 2, GET /admin/summary adds problems {open, oldestOpenAt}, which feeds the Today card 'Customer problems', the Problems badge (open cases) and the Today badge (top-ups to check + orders needing a driver + open cases); UX_ADMIN §1.3 and §2.1 already describe the badges, the card and the all-clear text by increment.
- **G07-23.** Partly tone differs: neutral on the web board (UX_ADMIN §3.1), warning in the shop app (UX_MOBILE §3.4, CUSTOMER_PAGE §10). **Settled:** Partly received is a warning everywhere: the website chip becomes warning, like the shop app (UX_MOBILE §3.4) and the shop card (CUSTOMER_PAGE §10). Tones: Yes success, Partly warning, No danger, Other warning, Pending warning (the amber clock), Expired neutral. The lead kept this point on 2026-10-23, when the UX specs proposed Partly and Other red; Partly and Other take the warning icon, never the clock, and Pending moved from neutral to the amber clock (UX_PRINCIPLES §4.1, §4.2).
- **G07-24.** SMS-safe names: CUSTOMER_PAGE §9 doesn't define how a business name is 'made GSM-safe', or what an Urdu-only name becomes. **Settled (the docs already said so):** smsShopName(name): decompose accents and drop the marks; ’ ‘ become ', – — become -, … becomes ...; other spaces become a space; “ ” are removed; keep only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, space and . , - & ' ( ) ! ? /; collapse spaces, trim, cut to 20, trim; if nothing is left (an Urdu-only name) use 'Smart Fleet'. renderSms may shorten it further from the end. Only the SMS and share text use it; the page shows the full, escaped business name. CUSTOMER_PAGE §9 already says this; no doc edit is left.
- **G07-25.** Rate-limit details (CUSTOMER_PAGE §5): the 429 page always says 'wait 10 minutes', even for the 1-minute GET window. It isn't stated whether bad-format tokens count toward the unknown-token limit, or whether an IP over that limit can still open a valid link. **Settled (the docs already said so):** Checks, in order: (1) the per-IP limit on every /c/ request (GET and HEAD 60 per minute, POST 20 per minute); (2) an IP with 30 unknown-token misses in its current 10-minute window gets 429 on every /c/ request, valid links included, without a lookup (a lookup would still tell valid from unknown, so the limit only slows guessing if it skips the lookup); (3) the format check: a bad format is 404 with no lookup and is not a miss; (4) for POST, 6 per 10 minutes per normalised token, counted before the lookup (refused 400s count); (5) the lookup, where a well-formed unknown token adds a miss. The 429 page reads 'Please wait {minutes} minutes, then try again.' ('Please wait 1 minute, then try again.' for 1), from Retry-After rounded up. Limits fail open when Redis is down. CUSTOMER_PAGE §5 and §6 already say this; no doc edit is left.
- **G07-26.** Page coverage details (CUSTOMER_PAGE §4, §6), not stated: (1) whether the second-step GETs (/partly, /not-received, /other) follow the state order; (2) what /c/\<token>/\<unknown step> returns; (3) whether the Other page re-shows the typed note after a 400; (4) whether the gas safety note appears on any page besides the main and thank-you pages. **Settled (the docs already said so):** (1) /partly, /not-received and /other follow the state order: PENDING shows the form, other states their page. (2) Any other path or method under /c/ (an unknown step, a POST to a step, an empty token) gets the HTML 404 page with no database lookup. (3) After a 400 the Other page keeps the cleaned text in the box (escaped). (4) The gas safety note is on every page, state and error pages included, as the last block before the footer line. CUSTOMER_PAGE §4, §5 and §6 already say this; no doc edit is left.

### Refills

- **G08-01.** Refill create idempotency: API_CONTRACT §7.11 and §4.2 give POST /filling-orders an Idempotency-Key stored as client_request_id, but DATA_MODEL §5.2 only adds filling_orders.client_request_id (and refill_no) in the inc3 migration. Inc 1 refill creates therefore can't be idempotent. **Settled:** Inc 1 has no filling_orders.client_request_id (DATA_MODEL §5.2 adds it in inc3, and the built inc1a has none), so the Inc 1 POST /filling-orders doesn't read the Idempotency-Key: a doubled request makes two PENDING refills, which moves no money, and the owner can cancel either before pickup (UX_MOBILE §6 promises no-double only for orders and top-ups). From Inc 3 the key is stored as client_request_id, unique per distributor: a retry returns the first refill with 200 and Idempotent-Replay: true, and the same key with a different fillingStationId, cylinderTypeId or requestedCount gives 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (the G15-02 key fields).
- **G08-02.** Refill count lower bound (API_CONTRACT §7.11): 1 ≤ requestedCount is required, but only REFILL_TOO_MANY (the upper bound) is named. The code for 0 or a negative count (VALIDATION_FAILED or REFILL_INVALID_COUNT) isn't stated, and no stock check at request time is described. **Settled:** requestedCount must be a whole number from 1 to refill.maxCylinders: 0, a negative number or a fraction gives 400 REFILL_INVALID_COUNT ("Check the number of cylinders."), as the built createFillingOrderSchema does (a promoted code, so a body with other problems too answers VALIDATION_FAILED); a missing or non-numeric count gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, and more than the setting 400 REFILL_TOO_MANY {max}. The rules run in this order after the body: serviceType DIY (410 REFILL_DIY_RETIRED), the maximum, then the station (404 NOT_FOUND {field: 'fillingStationId'}, 409 REFILL_STATION_INACTIVE); the pickup store is always the home store. No stock check is made at request time: the request is a plan, and from Inc 3 the pickup scans decide what goes.
- **G08-03.** Refill assign and audit: §7.11 PATCH /filling-orders/:id/assign names no error codes (driver not ACTIVE, no van, wrong status). Appendix B has no refill.create, refill.assign or Inc 1 office 'Mark complete' action; refill.complete exists only as the Inc 3 SYSTEM action. **Settled:** PATCH /filling-orders/:id/assign (office) takes { driverId } and checks, in order: 404 NOT_FOUND for an unknown refill or driver (details.field 'driverId'); status PENDING, or 200 X-Already-Applied when it is already ASSIGNED to this same driver, else 409 REFILL_WRONG_STEP {currentStatus}; the driver's user ACTIVE and availability AVAILABLE (409 ASSIGN_DRIVER_NOT_AVAILABLE {driver}); a van (409 ASSIGN_DRIVER_NO_VEHICLE {driver}), saved as the refill's assigned van. The office's Inc 1 "Mark complete" (RETURNED → COMPLETED) repeats with 200 X-Already-Applied and from any other status gives 409 REFILL_WRONG_STEP {currentStatus}. Appendix B adds refill.create (the distributor's request) and refill.assign (office), and refill.complete covers both the Inc 1 office complete (actor the office user) and the Inc 3 last receive (SYSTEM), each written in the same transaction as its change.
- **G08-04.** Refill status words: API_CONTRACT §1.4 defines no derived refill stage. UX_MOBILE §8.1 (WAITING_FOR_DRIVER, PICKED_UP, FILLING, COMING_BACK…) and UX_ADMIN §4.1 (NEEDS_DRIVER, PICKING_UP, AT_STATION, FILLED, RETURNING…) use two different stage sets, with no rule mapping FillingOrderStatus plus line counts to either. **Settled:** There is one derived RefillStage, computed by deriveRefillStage(refill) in shared-utils and sent as stage on every refill DTO from Inc 1, with counts { requested, picked, filled, received }. It is evaluated top-down: CANCELLED (status CANCELLED, or legacy FAILED), DONE (COMPLETED), BACK_AT_STORE (Inc 1: RETURNED; Inc 3: received ≥ 1), COMING_BACK (FILLED), AT_STATION, PICKED_UP (EMPTIES_PICKED), PICKING_UP (ASSIGNED with picked ≥ 1), DRIVER_ASSIGNED (ASSIGNED), NEEDS_DRIVER (PENDING); Inc 1 takes the counts from the legacy count columns (received = picked once RETURNED or COMPLETED). The shop app and the website map the same values to their own words — the shop's §8.1 table already does — and the office tabs are Needs a driver = NEEDS_DRIVER, In progress = DRIVER_ASSIGNED to BACK_AT_STORE, Done = DONE, Cancelled = CANCELLED; the Inc 1 screens show the stage words without counts instead of raw statuses.
- **G08-05.** API_CONTRACT §10.1 PICKUP: the 'distributor's own' rule has no listed error code (SCAN_WRONG_OWNER?), and there is no check order when several rules fail. REFILL_CYLINDER_ON_OTHER_REFILL looks unreachable: a cylinder on another open refill is on a van, so SCAN_NOT_AT_STORE fires first, unless a RETURNED line of a still-open refill counts. **Settled:** A refill PICKUP runs the §9.2 common steps (assigned driver 404, body 400, status ASSIGNED else 409 REFILL_WRONG_STEP, typed switch, resolve within the refill's distributor, lock, scanId resend or SCAN_ID_REUSED, owner = the refill's distributor 409 SCAN_WRONG_OWNER, the same pickup again 200 ALREADY_RECORDED, FAULTY or LOST 409 SCAN_CYLINDER_BLOCKED), then its own rules in this order: not on another open refill — a PICKED_UP or FILLED line of another refill that isn't COMPLETED or CANCELLED (409 REFILL_CYLINDER_ON_OTHER_REFILL); in the home store (409 SCAN_NOT_AT_STORE); the refill's size (409 REFILL_CYLINDER_WRONG_SIZE); EMPTY or PART_FILLED (409 REFILL_CYLINDER_NOT_EMPTY); picked lines below requested (409 REFILL_COUNT_REACHED). Checking the other refill before the store makes that code reachable and gives the clearer message, and a RETURNED line never blocks, because that cylinder is back in the store. A FILL needs status EMPTIES_PICKED or AT_STATION (REFILL_WRONG_STEP), treats an already filled line as the same move, and otherwise needs a PICKED_UP line of this refill still on the van (REFILL_CYLINDER_NOT_ON_THIS_REFILL).
- **G08-06.** API_CONTRACT §10.1 advance: 'Leave store needs at least one picked line' has no error code. A second FILL of an already-filled cylinder with a new scanId has no stated result. **Settled:** POST /filling-orders/:id/advance { to: 'EMPTIES_PICKED' } ("Leave store") needs status ASSIGNED with at least one picked line, and { to: 'FILLED' } ("Leave station") needs status AT_STATION; otherwise 409 REFILL_WRONG_STEP {currentStatus}, with no new code. Asking for the status the refill already has returns 200 with X-Already-Applied. The driver app keeps "Done picking up" disabled until a cylinder is picked and "Done filling" until one is filled; a second FILL of an already filled cylinder with a new scanId returns 200 ALREADY_RECORDED with X-Already-Applied and never raises filled (G05-05).
- **G08-07.** API_CONTRACT §10.1 'Any of these → COMPLETED: the last store receive' lets a refill complete with some or all cylinders never filled, even from ASSIGNED. Whether that's intended, and how the shop and office should show it, isn't stated. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** This is intended, as ADR-16 now reads (a refill tracks cylinders, not results): a refill becomes COMPLETED on the store receive that leaves no picked line un-received, from any open status (ASSIGNED included) and whether or not every cylinder was filled; unfilled cylinders come back with their state unchanged (EMPTY or PART_FILLED). A refill with no picked line never completes; it stays open until the owner cancels it. Both apps show the shortfall: the website's DONE reads "Done · {{filled}} of {{picked}} filled" when filled \< picked, and the shop's timeline ends "Done · {{filled}} of {{picked}} filled. The others came back as they were." (already in UX_MOBILE S18).
- **G08-08.** Responsible driver (API_CONTRACT §9.2, ADR-13) is defined only by LOAD or TAKE_BACK. The Inc 3 REFILL_PICKUP also moves a cylinder onto a van, so responsibility for refill cylinders isn't defined. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** A refill PICKUP moves the cylinder onto the refill's assigned van, so the refill's assigned driver becomes its responsible driver under the G06-02 rule; a FILL (van to van) doesn't change that, and the store's receive scan ends it. This keeps the owner's "whoever last scanned it IN" for refill cylinders, which stay with the driver throughout (there is no filling-station holder).
- **G08-09.** Refill cylinders and delivery trips can share a van. §9.2/§9.3 don't say whether refill cylinders count for TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY or VEHICLE_HAS_CYLINDERS. §5.5 and DATA_MODEL §3.6 don't say a refill pickup (event SCAN_OUT) must not stamp load_started_at, the refund cut-off, on the same driver's assigned orders. **Settled:** Cylinders on an open refill line (a PICKED_UP or FILLED line of a refill that isn't COMPLETED or CANCELLED) don't count for a delivery trip's TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY or for the 03:00 day-cutoff-van-check, but they do count for VEHICLE_HAS_CYLINDERS, because a van holding any cylinder can't change driver. Only a LOAD (an event with trip_id at the trip's STORE_PICKUP stop) stamps load_started_at; a refill pickup (SCAN_OUT with filling_order_id and no trip_id) never touches an order, so it is never the refund cut-off and never keeps a trip from being aborted. A refill cylinder can't be handed over on a delivery trip (SCAN_NOT_ON_YOUR_VAN), and GET /store/incoming lists it with came 'REFILL' and refill { shortCode }.
- **G08-10.** API_CONTRACT §10.1: GET /filling-stations 'drops price fields from new DTOs (old apps still get 0)', but how the server tells new callers from old ones (X-App-Version?) isn't stated. **Settled:** The server doesn't tell old callers from new ones: GET /filling-stations, and the station inside refill DTOs, keep sending pricePerCylinderPaisa: "0" to every caller in every increment, and writes keep ignoring it. New apps simply don't read the field, which is dropped only with the post-pilot contract migration (DATA_MODEL §9), so no X-App-Version check is needed.

### Day-end

- **G09-01.** Day-end row errors (API_CONTRACT §10.2): 422 DAY_SHEET_ROW_ERRORS is listed as an upload error, yet the upload response also returns errors[] and 'Row errors block' the submit. Which route returns the code, and whether an upload with row errors bumps the version, is ambiguous. **Settled:** Row problems refuse the upload; they are never stored. POST /day-end/:date/upload answers 422 DAY_SHEET_ROW_ERRORS {rows: [{sheet: 'CYLINDERS' | 'EXTRA', row, code, message}], total} when any row can't be read: row is the Excel row number (the header is row 1), each row gets the code of the first rule it breaks, at most 100 rows are listed in sheet then row order, and total counts them all. A refused upload stores nothing: the version, the lines and the stage stay as they were. A successful upload answers 200 {version, differences, summary} with no errors array, so a submit can never meet row errors and the catalogue text ('Some rows couldn't be read. Fix them and upload again.') reads right. Row codes and English (shared-types DAY_END_ROW_ERROR_EN, shop key dayEnd.rowError.\<code>): PLACE_UNKNOWN, STATE_UNKNOWN, REASON_REQUIRED, NOT_ON_LIST, DUPLICATE_NUMBER, NUMBER_INVALID, OTHER_SHOP_NUMBER, ON_LIST, SIZE_UNKNOWN, with the texts in the §10.2 replacement. That replacement (this gap's edit) also carries the decisions of G09-02 to G09-13.
- **G09-02.** DAY_ALREADY_SUBMITTED (API_CONTRACT §2.3) is tied to no route in §10.2, e.g. an upload while SUBMITTED. If uploads are refused while SUBMITTED, DAY_VERSION_CHANGED can only happen after a send-back and resubmit by someone else. **Settled:** While a day is SUBMITTED the shop can't change it: the sheet download and the upload answer 409 DAY_ALREADY_SUBMITTED (on an APPROVED day, 409 DAY_LOCKED). Submit {version, note? (at most 300)} checks, in order: a bad or future date 404 DAY_NOT_FOUND; APPROVED 409 DAY_LOCKED; SUBMITTED with this version 200 with X-Already-Applied and nothing written, with another version 409 DAY_ALREADY_SUBMITTED; stage not READY (no upload from the newest sheet since the last send-back or reopen) 409 DAY_SHEET_NOT_UPLOADED, a new code (HTTP 409, English 'Upload the filled sheet first.', no params); version different from upload_version 409 DAY_VERSION_CHANGED. Then one transaction: OPEN -> SUBMITTED with submitted_at, alert DAY_END_SUBMITTED (resource the day, deduplicated; approve and send-back resolve it), and audit day.submit with the note as its reason; it answers 200 with the day. So DAY_VERSION_CHANGED arises at approval only when the office's page is stale (a send-back and a new upload happened since it was loaded).
- **G09-03.** Approved fixes per place (API_CONTRACT §10.2; DATA_MODEL §5.3–5.4): 'On driver's van' and 'With customer' name no van or customer (DayCloseLine has no reported holder), and 'Missing' (NOT_FOUND) has no defined result (state LOST? which holder?).
