What 'approve all fixes' does to such rows is undefined. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** Approval applies every fix the sheet can name (ADR-17, Default; the owner may change it). Each differing line's fix (DayCloseFix, derived from the stored line, not a column) is: MARK_LOST when the sheet says Missing and the app doesn't have it LOST (state LOST, holder unchanged); MOVE_TO_STORE when the sheet says In my store and the app has it on a van, with a customer or LOST (holder the home store; state the sheet's state if given, which a LOST cylinder must give); NOTE_ONLY when the sheet says On driver's van or With customer and the app has it elsewhere (nothing changes: the sheet names no van or customer, so the office checks it by hand); SET_STATE when the place agrees and the state differs (Full FULL, Empty EMPTY, Part-filled PART_FILLED, Damaged FAULTY); REGISTER for an extra number (G09-04). For comparing, a LOST cylinder's app place is Missing (NOT_FOUND). Approval skips NOTE_ONLY lines and lines whose cylinder moved since the sheet, writes one ADJUSTED event (source DAY_END_FIX, the line's reason, actor the approver) or REGISTERED event per applied line in one transaction, and answers {day, registered: [{id, code, shortNo, shortCode, sizeLabel}]} so the new labels can be printed. 'Approve {{n}} fixes' counts fixesToApply. 'App says: where' adds ' · \<plate>' or ' · \<customer name>'.
- **G09-04.** Extra cylinders (DATA_MODEL §5.4): an unknown cylinder 'with a size' is REGISTERED, but the docs don't say whether it keeps the sheet's number or gets the next short_no, what happens to a row without a size, or how a number owned by another distributor is reported without leaking it. **Settled:** Numbers on both sheets are read like typed entry (parseCylinderNo, G05-08 and G16-02): '42', '0042', 'C0042' and 'AG-C0042' in any letter case are the caller's cylinder 42, and lines store the normal form AG-C0042 as sheet_key. A number with another shop's code ('BG-C0001') is the row error OTHER_SHOP_NUMBER, decided from the code alone: other shops' cylinders are never looked up, so nothing about them leaks. Cylinders sheet: not one of the caller's cylinders NOT_ON_LIST; listed twice DUPLICATE_NUMBER; not a number NUMBER_INVALID; a deleted row counts as matching. Extra sheet: one of the caller's cylinders ON_LIST; listed twice DUPLICATE_NUMBER; an unknown number needs a size from the list (SIZE_UNKNOWN) and a state (STATE_UNKNOWN) and becomes an UNKNOWN_CYLINDER line with fix REGISTER. On approval it is registered in the home store with the row's size and state and the next short number (for example AG-C0036), not the sheet's number, so the counter stays the only source of numbers; its label must be printed (the approval answer lists it). Like any row error, an OTHER_SHOP_NUMBER row refuses the upload (G09-01): the shop removes the row and calls the office.
- **G09-05.** Day-end reasons: API_CONTRACT §1.5 has no reason-code list for 'Why different', while DAY_END_FIX events need a reason (DATA_MODEL §5.1 and the §4.4 CHECK). Whether a blank reason on a differing row is a row error isn't stated. **Settled:** 'Why different' is free text; there is no reason-code list in the pilot (day_close_lines.reason_code stays NULL, reserved). A differing row on the Cylinders sheet needs a reason of at least 3 characters after cleaning (line breaks and tabs become spaces, other control characters are removed, spaces collapse, trimmed), else the row error REASON_REQUIRED; a longer reason is cut to 200 characters. It is stored in day_close_lines.note and becomes the ADJUSTED event's reason, which meets cylinder_events_reason_chk. A reason on a matching row is ignored; extra rows need none.
- **G09-06.** Sheet identity (API_CONTRACT §10.2, 'No HMAC'): the server checks the distributor and date, but the docs don't say where the sheet records them. DAY_SHEET_WRONG_DATE params are raw YYYY-MM-DD, and §2.1 formats only \*Paisa params. **Settled:** The sheet carries its identity in a hidden worksheet 'About' (exceljs state veryHidden; column A key, column B value): format 'smart-fleet-day-end/1', distributorId, distributorCode, businessDate and sheetFileId. Each download makes a new sheet (a DAY_END_SHEET stored file whose id is chosen before the file is written) and points day_closes.sheet_file_id and sheet_snapshot_at (the sheet time) at it; only that newest sheet can be uploaded, so the sheet time of any upload is known. Upload identity checks, after the file-type checks: no About sheet or another format 422 DAY_SHEET_UNREADABLE; another distributorId 422 DAY_SHEET_WRONG_DISTRIBUTOR; another businessDate 422 DAY_SHEET_WRONG_DATE {sheetDate, date}; a sheetFileId that isn't the day's newest sheet 422 DAY_SHEET_OUTDATED, a new code (HTTP 422, English 'This is an old copy. Download a new sheet and use that.', no params). A line's movedSinceSheet, and the approval skip, mean the cylinder's last event is newer than sheet_snapshot_at. For messages, a details key named date or ending in Date that holds a YYYY-MM-DD value is shown with formatIsoDay ('Tue 20 Oct') under the same name, as Paisa keys are shown with formatRs, so DAY_SHEET_WRONG_DATE reads 'This sheet is for Tue 20 Oct. Upload the sheet for Wed 21 Oct.' while details keep the ISO dates. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G09-07.** Upload limits (API_CONTRACT §10.2): ≤ 2 MB and a magic-byte check, but no codes are named. FILE_TOO_LARGE and FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED (§2.3 Files) speak of pictures ('Use a JPG, PNG or WebP picture'). **Settled:** The upload takes one multipart field, file, of at most 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes, the same binary megabyte as the 5 MB picture limit); a bigger file answers 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE {maxMb: 2}. The file must start with the ZIP signature PK\\x03\\x04, else 422 DAY_SHEET_UNREADABLE (never FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED, whose words are about pictures); a ZIP that isn't a workbook, unzips to more than 20 MB or has more than 20,000 rows on a sheet is also DAY_SHEET_UNREADABLE. An accepted file is stored as a DAY_END_UPLOAD file (upload_file_id); a refused one isn't stored.
- **G09-08.** Lock vs cut-off (API_CONTRACT §10.2): the docs don't say whether a day can be submitted or approved before its 03:00 cut-off, or what happens to scans between the approval and the cut-off (they belong to a locked date). 'Corrections dated in a locked day give 409 DAY_LOCKED' names no routes, e.g. send-back on an APPROVED day. **Settled:** Submit and approve are allowed any time after an upload, before the day's cut-off too. A lock never refuses a scan or anything outside day-end: later moves are recorded, holders stay live and the next sheet shows them, while the locked day's lines and summary are frozen at approval (day_closes.totals). DAY_LOCKED is answered only by the day-end routes of an APPROVED day: sheet download, upload, submit, send-back, and approve with another version (the same version is a 200 X-Already-Applied repeat). The sentence 'Corrections dated in a locked day give 409 DAY_LOCKED' goes, because nothing else is dated in a day-end. Approve on an OPEN day 409 DAY_NOT_SUBMITTED. Send-back {reason 5-300}: SUBMITTED -> OPEN with sent_back_reason and sent_back_at; a repeat right after it (no upload since) 200 X-Already-Applied with the first reason kept; another OPEN day 409 DAY_NOT_SUBMITTED; APPROVED 409 DAY_LOCKED. Reopen {reason 5-300}: APPROVED -> OPEN with reopen_reason and reopened_at, locked_at cleared and applied fixes kept; a repeat right after it 200 X-Already-Applied; any other state 409 CONFLICT_STALE_STATE {currentStatus}.
- **G09-09.** dayEnd.enabled (API_CONTRACT §6) isn't a features.\* key, so the §3.4 FEATURE_DISABLED guard doesn't clearly apply when it is off. UX_MOBILE §8.3 calls the flag features.dayEnd. **Settled:** Keep the built key dayEnd.enabled; apps read it as appConfig.features.dayEnd (as built). API_CONTRACT §3.4 gains setting switches: @SettingSwitch(key, name) guards a module behind a boolean setting outside features.\*, runs right after sign-in (before role and ownership checks), and while the setting is false answers every method, reads included, with 403 FEATURE_DISABLED and X-Feature-Disabled: \<name>, never [] (no installed app calls these routes). It is used for dayEnd.enabled (name dayEnd: every /day-end and /admin/day-end route) and confirmation.enabled (name confirmations: the confirmation view, share and new-link). UX_MOBILE §8.3 already names the setting.
- **G09-10.** DayClose is 'created OPEN … by the cut-off job' (API_CONTRACT §10.2), but no Inc 3 job is listed. §9.9 has only day-cutoff-van-check. **Settled:** No job creates day rows: the 'cut-off job' is dropped (no new scope). A day_closes row is created OPEN by the first sheet download for that date (two at once still make one row, by day_closes_distributor_id_business_date_key), and a read never creates one. GET /day-end/:date for a date with no row answers status OPEN, stage NOT_STARTED, lastUpload null and allowedActions ['DOWNLOAD']; GET /day-end lists only days with a row. :date must be a real YYYY-MM-DD no later than the current business date, else 404 DAY_NOT_FOUND; an unknown office :id is 404 DAY_NOT_FOUND. The office sees a day once the shop has downloaded its sheet (stage NOT_STARTED, 'Waiting for sheet', until an upload from the newest sheet).
- **G09-11.** The office links 'Download the uploaded sheet' and 'Download the app's sheet' (UX_ADMIN §4.3) have no route in API_CONTRACT §10.2, where the sheet route is DISTRIBUTOR exact. **Settled:** No new routes. GET /admin/day-end/:id carries files {sheetFileId, uploadFileId}, and the website's 'Download the uploaded sheet' and 'Download the app's sheet' open GET /files/:id/url (§7.10; the office may read any stored file, as built in FilesService.signedUrl). sheet_file_id is the newest sheet, which is the one the current upload was filled from; upload_file_id is the latest accepted upload. Each link is hidden while its id is null. The shop's GET /day-end/:date/sheet.xlsx stays DISTRIBUTOR exact.
- **G09-12.** Day-end status words: the shop chips (UX_MOBILE §8.3: NOT_STARTED, READY, WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL, APPROVED, SENT_BACK) and the office statuses (UX_ADMIN §4.3) don't map 1:1 to DayCloseStatus (OPEN/SUBMITTED/APPROVED), and §1.4 has no derived day-end stage. The mobile dayEnd.diff.\* words are undefined (only UX_ADMIN §4.3 gives them). **Settled:** One derived DayEndStage, computed by deriveDayEndStage(day) in shared-utils and sent as stage on every day-end DTO, top-down: APPROVED (status APPROVED); WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL (SUBMITTED); SENT_BACK (OPEN, with a send-back or reopen and no upload since it); READY (OPEN, and the latest upload is newer than the newest sheet); NOT_STARTED (otherwise, or no row). The shop maps it to its chips, already in UX_MOBILE §8.3. The office words: NOT_STARTED 'Waiting for sheet', READY 'Sheet uploaded', SENT_BACK 'Sent back', WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL 'To approve', APPROVED 'Approved · day closed'; the tabs are To approve = SUBMITTED, Open = OPEN, Approved = APPROVED. Difference words, the same in both apps: PLACE_DIFFERS 'In a different place', STATE_DIFFERS 'State differs', PLACE_AND_STATE_DIFFER 'Place and state differ', UNKNOWN_CYLINDER 'Number not in the app'. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G09-13.** The distributor GET /day-end/:date DTO (API_CONTRACT §10.2) carries no send-back note or reopen reason, yet UX_MOBILE S19 shows 'Sent back · see note'. **Settled:** GET /day-end/:date adds officeNote: {kind: 'SENT_BACK' | 'REOPENED', text, at} | null, set while stage is SENT_BACK, from the later of (sent_back_reason, sent_back_at) and (reopen_reason, reopened_at); day_closes gains sent_back_at and reopened_at. The DTO also carries stage and allowedActions ('DOWNLOAD' | 'UPLOAD' | 'SUBMIT')[]. The shop's S19 danger card, in UX_MOBILE §8.3, reads 'Office note: “{{note}}”' or 'Office reopened this day: “{{note}}”', then 'Fix it and upload again.' (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)

### Setup, reset, rehearsal and test data

- **G10-01.** Pilot setup file (API_CONTRACT §10.3) lists no customers and no opening balances, though the standard test data needs C1–C3 and Ahmed Gas's Rs 5,000 (ADR-11 covers only the migration). It also doesn't say whether setup is all-or-nothing on a bad zone, whether zones that only share a border count as overlapping, or what 'prints passwords once' means on a re-run. **Settled:** The setup file gains optional customers [{distributorCode, name, phone, address {label, lat, lng}, notes?}], checked with the normal customer rules (a Pakistani mobile, unique per distributor, a pin in an active zone where that distributor has a price), and optional openingBalances [{distributorCode, amountPaisa, note}], allowed only with --test (a file with them and no --test is refused). Each opening balance is written once as a correction ADD with reason OPENING_BALANCE (shown 'Opening balance'), actor SYSTEM cli:pilot-setup and request key pilot-setup:opening:\<distributorId>; a re-run never changes a balance, and live balances come only from top-ups and office corrections (ADR-11). Setup is all-or-nothing: it checks the whole file first (zod, shapes, overlaps among the file's zones and with stored active zones, store and customer pins, codes, phones, prices, settings, stock), then writes everything in one transaction through the services; a refused run writes nothing and exits 1 naming the first bad entry (its JSON path) with its error code and English text. Zones overlap when their interiors share more than 1 m² (ST_Area(ST_Intersection(a, b)::geography) > 1); a shared border or point is fine. Passwords: each login the run creates gets a random 12-character password, printed once at the end of a successful run (name, role, phone, password) to the terminal only, never logged, stored in clear or written to a file; re-runs create none and never reset one. --test marks distributors, their users, drivers' users and vans is_test, never office users. Stock is topped up to the file's count per distributor and size. The §10.3 replacement (this gap's edit) also carries G10-02 and G10-04.
- **G10-02.** Pilot reset (API_CONTRACT §10.3): it's unclear whether office users created with --test are is_test (the reset would remove the only super admins; see USER_LAST_SUPER_ADMIN), how audit_logs rows whose actor is a test user are handled (RESTRICT FK on an append-only log), and how a run without --yes behaves. **Settled:** Office users are never test rows and are never deleted, so the office can always sign in after a reset (USER_LAST_SUPER_ADMIN can't arise). The reset plans the deletion of every is_test distributor, user and van and what hangs off them (the rows they own and the rows under those), plus the audit_logs rows whose actor, distributor_id or resource_id is a deleted row: the one documented exception to the append-only log, needed because audit_logs.actor_user_id has a RESTRICT foreign key. Actor columns that point at office users don't keep a row. It refuses (exit 1, nothing deleted) when a row it would keep points at a row it would delete, naming the first (table, id, short number). Without --yes it prints the plan, deletes nothing and exits 1 with 'Nothing deleted. Run again with --yes to delete.'; --dry-run prints the plan and exits 0. With --yes it deletes in foreign-key order in one transaction and writes one pilot.reset audit row (actor SYSTEM cli:pilot-reset, diff: rows deleted per table); storage objects stay in the bucket. Production (APP_ENV or NODE_ENV is production, the stricter reading for a destructive command) needs --allow-production and --confirm-db equal to current_database().
- **G10-03.** Rehearsal bank list: the test server uses the dummy account PK00TEST…, so the go/no-go rule 'every top-up matched to one bank payment' needs a stand-in bank list the docs don't describe (the rehearsal cases use a printed list). **Settled (the docs already said so):** On the test server the company account is the dummy PK00TEST…, so the rehearsal lead brings a printed stand-in bank list: one line per payment the team makes (bank reference, amount, time). The office approves a top-up only against a line, typing its reference, amount and time, and ticks it; each line is used once. Go/no-go rule 1 holds when every approved top-up matches exactly one ticked line and every ticked line one approved top-up. Live approvals use only the real company bank app. README's Increment 3 exit already says this and the rehearsal cases already use the list, so no doc edit is left.
- **G10-04.** Standard test data gaps: it names no refill station (the cases assume 'Lahore Filling Station'), and gives no sign-in phone numbers for DA, DB, DR1, DR2, SA1 (Owner) and SA2 (Ops), and no phone for Usman (the rehearsal uses team test numbers). So cases can't assert exact USER_PHONE_IN_USE collisions, or that the shop's number on the customer page differs from Sana's. CNF-011 fixes DA's as +923211234567; the shared test-data sheet should set all of them. **Settled:** The standard test data (TEST_CASES.md) and pilot/test.json fix every phone and the station. Sign-in phones: SA1 Owner +923331000001 (0333 1000001), SA2 Ops +923331000002 (0333 1000002), DA Ahmed Gas +923211234567 (0321 1234567), DB Bilal Gas +923227654321 (0322 7654321), DR1 Kashif +923451000001 (0345 1000001), DR2 Imran +923451000002 (0345 1000002). Customers: C1 Sana +923001234567 (0300 1234567), C2 Usman +923217654321 (0321 7654321), C3 Hina +923009876543 (0300 9876543). The refill station is 'Lahore Filling Station', active, in Lahore. These numbers are reserved for the standard data; a case that needs a free number uses another one. The shop number on the customer page is DA's sign-in phone, never Sana's. pilot/rehearsal.json is the same data without Sana and Usman (the shop adds them in rehearsal step 4) and with the team's real test phones. The API_CONTRACT data-files paragraph is in the §10.3 replacement under G10-01.

### Sign-in, accounts, ownership and sessions

- **G11-01.** 404 code for ownership misses: API_CONTRACT §3.2 says policies return 404 NOT_FOUND, but §2.3 has CLIENT_NOT_FOUND / CLIENT_ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND and §7.6 rule 2 uses them; §7.4 ('own client only' on /clients/:id/addresses) names no code. **Settled:** Every ownership miss and every unknown id answers 404 and reveals nothing: the code is the resource's own not-found code where §2.3 has one, otherwise NOT_FOUND. Customers answer CLIENT_NOT_FOUND (a path id, GET/POST /clients/:id/addresses, PATCH /clients/:id, or a body clientId), addresses CLIENT_ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND, files FILE_NOT_FOUND, day-end days DAY_NOT_FOUND [Inc 3], and every other record NOT_FOUND. Status, code and message are identical for a record that doesn't exist, another owner's record and an id that isn't a UUID, as the built policies already do (canSeeClient answers CLIENT_NOT_FOUND, FilesService FILE_NOT_FOUND).
- **G11-02.** Callers not on the trip: API_CONTRACT §8.6 accepts '403 or 404' for a driver not on the trip, ADR-02 says ownership failures return 404, and §7.6 uses 403 ORDER_NOT_ON_YOUR_TRIP for PATCH /orders/:id/status. Not stated: the answer for another driver calling /orders/:id/fail; the PATCH status row for a DISTRIBUTOR caller (403 PERMISSION_DENIED, or 409 ORDER_INVALID_TRANSITION from the 'Anyone' row); and whether a DRIVER calling GET /cylinders/:code/history gets a role 403 or a policy 404 (§3.2). **Settled:** Every route checks in this order and the first failure answers: authentication (401), the roles guard (403 PERMISSION_DENIED, before any record is read), the ownership policy (404, §3.2), then the route's own rules; so a role a route never allows always gets 403, and an allowed role gets 404 for someone else's record. A DRIVER who isn't the driver of the order's current trip gets 404 NOT_FOUND on GET /orders/:id, PATCH /orders/:id/status and POST /orders/:id/fail (ADR-02 beats the 403 in §7.6); a DISTRIBUTOR calling PATCH /orders/:id/status or POST /orders/:id/fail gets 403 PERMISSION_DENIED; a DRIVER calling GET /cylinders/:code/history or GET /custody/cylinders/:id/history gets 403 PERMISSION_DENIED. ORDER_NOT_ON_YOUR_TRIP (403) stays only for the legacy POST /custody/scan, when the body's orderId isn't on the body's (own) trip, with the same answer for any id; the confirmation routes keep their explicit 404 for a DRIVER (§9.7).
- **G11-03.** Wrong-app sign-in: API_CONTRACT §7.1 refuses a wrong-app login with 403 AUTH_WRONG_APP (for example a distributor or driver signing in with X-App-Variant admin-web), while UX_MOBILE S1 (the WrongApp screen) and UX_ADMIN §2.10 (a full-page office-only gate) expect the sign-in to succeed first. UX_ADMIN §2.10 also lists only AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS, RATE_LIMITED and AUTH_ROLE_LOCKED. The UX docs need aligning with §7.1. **Settled:** API_CONTRACT §7.1 wins: a sign-in whose X-App-Variant names another app than the role's is refused with 403 AUTH_WRONG_APP {role, app} and no tokens. The role's app is DISTRIBUTOR → distributor, DRIVER → driver, every other role → admin-web (whose own gate then admits only SUPER_ADMIN); with no X-App-Variant or an unknown value there is no app check, because installed 0.1.0 apps send none. Both apps and the website show AUTH_WRONG_APP inline on the sign-in form (for example 'This account is for the Smart Fleet Driver app.') with no session started; the mobile WrongApp screen and the website's office-only page stay only as a fallback gate for a saved session whose role doesn't fit (UX_MOBILE S1 and §3.6 already say so; the built SignInScreen does this).
- **G11-04.** API_CONTRACT §7.1: the order of login checks (wrong password, inactive, locked role, wrong app) is not specified. **Settled:** POST /auth/login checks in this order and the first failure answers: (1) 429 RATE_LIMITED; (2) 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (phone 1–32 characters, password 1–128, as the built loginSchema); (3) 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS when the phone isn't a Pakistani mobile, no user has it, the user has no password or the password is wrong (with no user a dummy hash is still verified); (4) 403 AUTH_ROLE_LOCKED; (5) 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE (PENDING or SUSPENDED); (6) 403 AUTH_WRONG_APP; then 200 with tokens. So nothing about an account shows without its password, and a locked role wins over a wrong app. Every attempt counts toward the §3.6 limits, successful or not, and a success never resets a count; the per-phone limit counts by the normalised phone, so input that isn't a Pakistani mobile counts only toward the per-IP limit (as the built RateLimitGuard does).
- **G11-05.** API_CONTRACT §7.1: refresh refusal codes for a suspended user, a locked role or a tv mismatch are not named (AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED vs AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID vs AUTH_ROLE_LOCKED). The code for a request with no token is not named. **Settled:** On protected routes a missing, malformed, forged or expired access token gives 401 AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID (as the built JwtAuthGuard does), and a valid token whose user isn't ACTIVE, whose role is locked or whose tv differs from users.token_version gives 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED (the 60-second cached check). POST /auth/refresh gives 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID for a malformed, forged, expired, unknown or already-used refresh token (a reused one also revokes every live refresh token of that user), and 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED for a valid one whose user isn't ACTIVE, whose role is locked or whose tv differs, revoking that token; the apps treat any 401 from refresh as signed out. The /drivers socket emits error {code} and disconnects with AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID (no, bad or expired token), AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED (the same session check) or PERMISSION_DENIED (any role but DRIVER and SUPER_ADMIN).
- **G11-06.** A suspend (API_CONTRACT §7.3) bumps tv but doesn't say whether the user becomes non-ACTIVE. A suspended shop that signs in again may get AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE at login, or only DISTRIBUTOR_NOT_ACTIVE when it orders. **Settled:** PATCH /distributors/:id/suspend {reason 5–300} sets distributors.status and users.status to SUSPENDED and bumps tv in one transaction with the distributor.suspend audit row: the shop's sessions end within 60 seconds (401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED) and a new sign-in gets 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE. Orders already placed continue and the balance is unchanged; DISTRIBUTOR_NOT_ACTIVE stays as the guard on placing orders, top-up requests and refills (it covers the ≤ 60-second cache window). A distributor's two status columns always change together, whichever route changes them (PATCH /users/:id/status on its user included), and suspending an already SUSPENDED distributor answers 200 with X-Already-Applied and no new audit row (UX_ADMIN §2.4 already words the dialog this way).
- **G11-07.** UX_ADMIN §2.4 offers 'Reactivate…' on the distributor page, but API_CONTRACT §7.3 has only approve and suspend routes. **Settled:** 'Reactivate…' calls PATCH /distributors/:id/approve, which activates from PENDING (body optional) and reactivates from SUSPENDED (body {reason 5–300} required, else 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on reason). It sets distributors.status and users.status to ACTIVE in one transaction, writes distributor.activate with diff {from: 'PENDING' | 'SUSPENDED'} and the reason, and answers 200 with DistributorDto; approving an ACTIVE distributor answers 200 with X-Already-Applied and no audit row. UX_ADMIN §2.4 already names the route; Activity says 'Reactivated {{distributor}}'.
- **G11-08.** POST /users/:id/password (API_CONTRACT §7.2): no request body, no success shape, and no refusal codes for another super admin's password or a CLIENT target. UX_ADMIN §2.4 'Set app password' doesn't say who chooses the password or whether it is shown once. **Settled:** POST /users/:id/password (office) takes {password (8–128, not trimmed)} typed by the super admin (the built resetUserPasswordSchema), hashes it, bumps the target's tv (its sessions end within 60 seconds) and answers 200 {ok: true}, with the audit row user.password_reset; the password and its hash never appear in a response, log or audit row. Only DISTRIBUTOR and DRIVER users, whatever their status, may be targets: the caller's own account gives 403 USER_SELF_CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED (use POST /auth/change-password), any other target (another super admin, a CLIENT or a staff role) 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, and an unknown id 404 NOT_FOUND. On the website 'Set app password' is a dialog where the office types the password and tells the person by phone or in person; it is never stored or shown again (UX_ADMIN §2.4 already says so).
- **G11-09.** Driver admin routes (API_CONTRACT §7.2): the POST /drivers and PATCH /drivers/:id/profile bodies aren't given; there is no code for a field a driver may not change on their own profile; it isn't stated whether archiving (DELETE /drivers/:id) makes the user non-ACTIVE, so that login gives AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE; Appendix B has no action for reactivating a driver. **Settled:** POST /drivers (office) takes {name 1–80, phone, licenceNo 1–40, email?, cnic?, profilePictureUrl? ≤ 500}: the phone is normalised (else 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, field phone, code INVALID_PHONE, which also applies to POST and PATCH /distributors) and must not belong to any user (409 USER_PHONE_IN_USE {existingRole}, never an upsert), a licence number already used gives 409 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE, the CNIC follows §7.3 rule 4, and it creates an ACTIVE DRIVER user with no password plus an AVAILABLE driver, answering 201 with audit driver.create. PATCH /drivers/:id/profile takes {name?, email?, cnic?, licenceNo?, profilePictureUrl?} from the office, while a driver on himself may send only name and profilePictureUrl (any other field: 403 USER_FIELD_OFFICE_ONLY and nothing changes; another driver's id: 404 NOT_FOUND); audit driver.update {before, after}. DELETE /drivers/:id {reason 5–300} archives (users.status SUSPENDED, the van released, isOnline false, tv bumped, so sign-in gives 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE and assignment ASSIGN_DRIVER_NOT_AVAILABLE), PATCH /drivers/:id/reactivate {reason 5–300} sets the user ACTIVE without giving the van back, and both answer 200 (a repeat 200 with X-Already-Applied) with audit driver.archive\* or the new driver.reactivate\*.
- **G11-10.** PATCH /users/me (API_CONTRACT §7.2) doesn't say whether a body that mixes allowed and office-only fields is refused whole or partly applied, or whether a driver changes their name here or only through PATCH /drivers/:id/profile. **Settled:** PATCH /users/me (any signed-in role) changes only name (1–80) and email (blank or null clears it; an email used by another account gives 409 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE). A body that contains phone, cnic or businessName at all (any value, even unchanged) is refused whole with 403 USER_FIELD_OFFICE_ONLY and nothing changes; other unknown keys are ignored; success is 200 with the safe profile (the built updateMeSchema keeps those three keys so the service can refuse them). A driver can change his name here or through PATCH /drivers/:id/profile, which also takes the photo; both write users.name.
- **G11-11.** USER_CNIC_IN_USE (API_CONTRACT §7.3 rule 4): it isn't stated whether the blind index normalises the CNIC first, so that a CNIC typed with and without dashes counts as the same. **Settled:** Before it is encrypted or indexed, a CNIC is reduced to its 13 digits (spaces and dashes removed; anything else, or not 13 digits, gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on cnic with code INVALID_CNIC, as the built cnicSchema does), and cnic_index = HMAC-SHA256(BLIND_INDEX_KEY, those 13 digits). So '35202-7654321-3' and '3520276543213' are the same CNIC and the second gets 409 USER_CNIC_IN_USE; the check runs on the server, across all users, and the legacy plain users.cnic column is never written. In production and staging the boot guards require ENCRYPTION_KEY and BLIND_INDEX_KEY, each 64 hex characters, because without them the built CryptoService stores the CNIC in clear and indexes it with a bare SHA-256.
- **G11-12.** API_CONTRACT §3.5 strips cnic from every response, office views included. There is no rule for a masked CNIC on office forms. **Settled:** Office views of a person with a CNIC (DistributorDto, and the office driver view of GET /drivers, GET /drivers/:id, POST /drivers and PATCH /drivers/:id/profile) carry cnicMasked: string | null, the last four digits only, written '\*\*\*\*\*-\*\*\*\*567-1', never the CNIC itself; no other response carries it (not GET /distributors/me, not a driver reading himself). The website shows the mask read-only after saving: a distributor's CNIC can't be changed in the pilot (UX_ADMIN §2.4 already says so), and a driver's is replaced only by sending a full new cnic in PATCH /drivers/:id/profile. The key name cnicMasked passes the built SecretStripInterceptor, which strips exact keys only.
- **G11-13.** Seeded logins: ADR-02 and API_CONTRACT §8.5 lock only the seeded ADMIN. prisma/seed.ts also seeds a SUPER_ADMIN 'LPG Super Admin', a test distributor and a test driver with default passwords, and no doc says to disable them on live. **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** Only the two named super admins sign in on live (ADR-02): at the switch-over, after users:create-office has made them, ops suspends the seeded SUPER_ADMIN 'LPG Super Admin' (+923000000000) with PATCH /users/:id/status, and on live also suspends 'Test Distributor' (+923001111111, PATCH /distributors/:id/suspend) and archives 'Test Driver' (+923002222222, DELETE /drivers/:id), each with a reason; the seeded ADMIN stays refused by auth.lockedRoles. prisma/seed.ts refuses to run when the deployment is production (APP_ENV=production, or NODE_ENV=production without APP_ENV), because its upserts would re-activate those users (ADR-02 and DATA_MODEL §2.5 already say so). On the test server the test distributor and driver may stay as test logins; the seeded super admin is suspended there too.
- **G11-14.** API_CONTRACT §6: auth.lockedRoles accepts any UserRole[], with no rule against locking SUPER_ADMIN (one setting change would lock the office out). **Settled:** auth.lockedRoles is a list of distinct roles that never contains SUPER_ADMIN: a list with SUPER_ADMIN or a repeated role gives 400 SETTING_INVALID_VALUE and the value is unchanged, as the built registry already enforces (LOCKABLE_ROLES and uniqueList). DISTRIBUTOR and DRIVER may be locked as an emergency stop, with a reason and an audit row; the setting isn't on the website's Settings page and is changed only over the API by engineering.
- **G11-15.** API_CONTRACT §6/§7.1: auth.otpLogin.enabled=true is unspecified (which roles may use codes, and the answer for an unknown phone). **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** Code (OTP) sign-in is not built in the pilot: auth.otpLogin.enabled stays false and becomes a reserved setting that can't be changed over the API (403 SETTING_NOT_EDITABLE), and both OTP routes always answer 403 AUTH_OTP_DISABLED, send no code and never create a user (ADR-03). The rule recorded for later, if it is ever built: codes sign in only existing DISTRIBUTOR and DRIVER accounts, send answers 200 {ok: true} for any well-formed phone and texts a code only when such a user exists, and verify then applies the password sign-in checks from step (3) on. This replaces building an unused on-path (the pilot has no live SMS provider anyway).
- **G11-16.** API_CONTRACT §2.3/§7.2: with the self-change rule, USER_LAST_SUPER_ADMIN is reachable only by two super admins racing. The 60 s session cache (§3.3) means the check needs a row lock, which the docs don't require. **Settled:** When PATCH /users/:id/status or /role targets a SUPER_ADMIN, the transaction first locks every ACTIVE SUPER_ADMIN row (SELECT … FOR UPDATE, ordered by id, so two such requests can't deadlock) and re-reads the caller from the database instead of the 60-second cache. A caller who is no longer ACTIVE then gets 401 AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED; next, a change that would leave no ACTIVE SUPER_ADMIN gets 409 USER_LAST_SUPER_ADMIN; only then come the update, the tv bump and the audit row. Two super admins suspending each other at once therefore end with exactly one 200 and one 401, and USER_LAST_SUPER_ADMIN stays as the safety net.
- **G11-17.** Website session: the idle sign-out (UX_ADMIN §2.10) is client-only, and the access and refresh token lifetimes (expiresIn, API_CONTRACT §7.1) are undocumented. **Settled:** expiresIn is the access token's lifetime in seconds: env JWT_ACCESS_TTL, default 43200 (12 hours); a refresh token lasts JWT_REFRESH_TTL, default 2592000 (30 days), and is replaced on every refresh with reuse detection, as the built configuration has it. On the server a session ends only by token expiry, a tv bump (suspend, archive, role change, phone change, password change or reset) or a locked role, each enforced within 60 seconds; the website's 30-minute idle sign-out runs in the browser only (it deletes the tokens and returns to sign-in), which is accepted for the pilot.
- **G11-18.** Push tokens: DELETE /push-tokens (API_CONTRACT §7.2) gives no body and no answer for someone else's token. Nothing says the apps remove the token at sign-out, so a signed-out driver phone may still get 'New job' pushes (UX_MOBILE §7.2 R8). **Settled:** POST /push-tokens {token (1–200), platform?} upserts by token, so a token held by another user moves to the caller (one phone, one signed-in user), and answers 200 {ok: true}. DELETE /push-tokens {token} deletes the row only when it belongs to the caller and always answers 200 {removed: 0 or 1}, so someone else's or an unknown token is left alone and nothing is revealed. The driver app calls DELETE /push-tokens before clearing the session on Sign out (best effort; a failure never blocks signing out), and the next sign-in on that phone moves the token anyway (UX_MOBILE R8 already says so).

### Settings, switches and jobs

- **G12-01.** Settings cache: API_CONTRACT §5.2 caches SettingsService.get for 30 s, but UX_ADMIN §2.8 says changes 'apply right away', and the docs don't say whether set() clears the cache. The catalogue is split: WAL-004, ORD-002, ORD-011, DRV-033 and DRV-039 wait 30 s, while FND-002, FEE-022, TOP-003, TOP-005, TOP-006 and TOP-018 assume set() clears it. Decide and state it. **Settled:** SettingsService.get keeps its 30-second in-process cache, and set() — as built — clears that process's cache when its transaction commits. Because the pilot runs one API instance (ADR-23), a change saved over PATCH /settings applies to the very next request; a change made by the settings CLI, which runs as another process, reaches the API within 30 seconds. Phones re-read GET /app/config at most every 5 minutes (UX_MOBILE §3.6), so what a phone shows can lag by up to 5 minutes while the server's own checks don't; tests never wait for the cache after a PATCH /settings.
- **G12-02.** Training flag: API_CONTRACT §6 doesn't say which APP_ENV values make PublicAppConfig.training and topup-info.training true. FND-001 and TOP-001 expect false on APP_ENV=test, while MIG-013 and RHS-002 expect the shop app's 'TRAINING · test money only' strip on the test server. UX_MOBILE §2.2 drives EnvBanner from appConfig.environment, while S4 ties the banner to training=true. **Settled:** As built, PublicAppConfig.environment is APP_ENV, and training — in GET /app/config and in GET /payments/topup-info — is true only when APP_ENV is training. Neither app's environment strip reads training: the shop and driver EnvBanner follows appConfig.environment, falling back to EXPO_PUBLIC_ENV until the config loads (training → "Training · test money only"; development, test and staging → "Test server · test money only"; production → none), as UX_MOBILE §2.2 already says, and the website's EnvBadge keeps UX_ADMIN §2.10. S4 shows whatever account topup.account holds on each server. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G12-03.** Business date in SQL: DATA_MODEL §5.4 hard-codes 'Asia/Karachi' and '3 hours', while day.timezone and day.cutoffLocalTime are editable (API_CONTRACT §6; UX_ADMIN §4.4 offers 00:00–06:00). The database and the apps would disagree after a change, and the setting's value is typed only as 'string'. **Settled:** Business-date SQL never writes the zone or the cut-off as literals: a query for one business day filters ts >= start AND ts \< end with the bounds from businessDayRange(date, { timezone, cutoffLocalTime }) (shared-utils, as built; start inclusive, end exclusive), and a query that groups by business date uses ((ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE \$tz - \$cutoff::interval)::date, with \$tz = day.timezone and \$cutoff = day.cutoffLocalTime read from SettingsService. The settings are typed as built: day.timezone is an IANA zone name that Intl accepts (at most 64 characters) and day.cutoffLocalTime a local "HH:mm" from 00:00 to 23:59 (the website offers whole hours 00:00–06:00). As ADR-21 says, change them only between business days with no day-end OPEN or SUBMITTED — an ops rule the API doesn't enforce — because stored dates never move while "today" counts and reports regroup at once.
- **G12-04.** ADR-21 says every cron passes timeZone 'Asia/Karachi'. API_CONTRACT §8.5 gives no schedule for housekeeping, and §9.9 lists confirmation-expiry with no time zone (harmless for \*/15, but unstated). **Settled:** Every @Cron passes { timeZone: 'Asia/Karachi' } literally, including the \*/15 confirmation-expiry, where it changes nothing. The schedules are wallet-nightly-check '30 3 \* \* \*', housekeeping '0 3 \* \* \*' (03:00 Karachi; HOUSEKEEPING_CRON may change the expression, never the zone), day-cutoff-van-check '0 3 \* \* \*' and confirmation-expiry '\*/15 \* \* \* \*' (both Inc 2), plus G09-10's day-close-open (Inc 3). Job times are fixed in code and don't follow day.timezone or day.cutoffLocalTime, as ADR-21 now says.
- **G12-05.** The nightly wallet check (API_CONTRACT §8.5; ADR-23, no job-run table) leaves no visible record of a clean run, so 'clean' can't be told apart from 'didn't run' without the server log. **Settled:** Every run of wallet-nightly-check, clean or not, writes one audit row wallet.check: actor SYSTEM with label job:wallet-check, resourceType 'job', resourceId null, and diff { checked, mismatches, distributorIds } (the ids of the mismatching wallets), in the same run after any WALLET_CHECK_MISMATCH alerts. It is the visible record that the job ran, shown in Activity as "Nightly wallet check: {{checked}} wallets checked, all match" or "Nightly wallet check: {{mismatches}} of {{checked}} wallets don't match their history". It is an audit row, not the job-run table ADR-23 rules out (ADR-23 and README already say so), and the live integrity check on the wallet page writes nothing.

### Expenses and fuel logs

- **G13-01.** 'Today' for expenses: API_CONTRACT §7.12 says 'at most today in Asia/Karachi', while the business day has a 03:00 cut-off (§1.1, ADR-21). Fuel-log months use 'an Asia/Karachi date' (§7.12), but DATA_MODEL §5 gives a business-date SQL formula. Between 00:00 and 03:00 these differ. **Settled:** Expense dates are calendar dates, not business dates (already written in ADR-21): EXPENSE_DATE_IN_FUTURE when expenseDate is after today's calendar date in Asia/Karachi (shared-utils localDate(now), with no 03:00 cut-off), on POST and PATCH alike, so at 01:00 on 22 Oct an expense dated 22 Oct is accepted and 23 Oct is refused. Fuel-log months use the Asia/Karachi calendar date of refill_at, also with no cut-off, and the expense list's default range is the current calendar month in Asia/Karachi. In SQL the zone comes from day.timezone, like business dates (G12-03), only without the cut-off. The 03:00 business day applies only to operational 'today' figures (orders, top-ups approved today, the Today page, day-end).
- **G13-02.** The inc1a backfill (DATA_MODEL §3.4 (11)) creates archived legacy expense types with name_key = lower(category), e.g. 'food'. Adding a type called 'Food' later is then refused with EXPENSE_TYPE_NAME_TAKEN; is that intended? **Settled:** Intended. Type names are unique across active and archived types, ignoring case and spaces (name_key), the archived LEGACY\_\* types included: adding 'Food' while the archived legacy 'Food' exists gives 409 EXPENSE_TYPE_NAME_TAKEN {name: 'Food'}, where name is the existing type's stored name. The same holds for a rename. The office restores the archived type instead (its old expenses come back with it), or renames it first to free the name. On the website, when the clash is an archived type in the drawer's own list (same toExpenseTypeNameKey), the error reads "There's already an archived type called {{name}}. Restore it instead." with a Restore button on that row (already in UX_ADMIN §2.7).
- **G13-03.** features.fuelRefills (API_CONTRACT §6, §7.2): only the two office read routes are named. The driver's write and list routes, and what turning the switch on does, are undocumented, although UX_ADMIN §2.7 counts fuel logs in totals. **Settled:** Driver fuel logging is not used in the pilot (ADR-04, ADR-14). features.fuelRefills gates only the driver's own routes: while off, POST /fuel-refills gives 403 FEATURE_DISABLED and GET /fuel-refills/mine gives 200 [], both with X-Feature-Disabled: fuelRefills (the built @Feature guard and interceptor, on those two handlers only). Switched on, they work as today for DRIVER (exact), with today's body { vehicleId, litres, costPaisa, odometerKm, fuelStation?, notes? } and the driver taken from the token (a body driverId is ignored). The pilot driver app has no fuel-log screen (its menu item is removed in Inc 1, UX_MOBILE §5), so the switch stays off. The office reads GET /fuel-refills, /fuel-refills/vehicle/:id and /fuel-refills/driver/:id are office only with safe selects and answer whatever the switch, as do GET /reports/fuel-consumption and ExpenseSummary.fuelLogs, so older logs stay visible and, if the switch is ever turned on, new logs appear beside Petrol (left out of totals unless the office's include switch is on).

### Office Today page, wallets list and reports

- **G14-01.** GET /admin/summary (API_CONTRACT §7.13): is prices.missing.zones a count or a list? Does placedToday include orders cancelled later? Do not-yet-active distributors appear in prices.missing? **Settled:** GET /admin/summary: prices.missing has one row per ACTIVE distributor with at least one active zone without its price, sorted by name, and zones is how many such zones (a count, as built in shared-types); distributors waiting to start or suspended are left out (a waiting one shows in distributors.waitingToStart, whose checklist covers prices). orders.placedToday counts the orders created in the current business day whatever their status now (later cancels included). The other figures: needsDriver = PENDING or CONFIRMED (oldestNeedsDriverAt = the oldest createdAt); inProgress = ASSIGNED or IN_TRANSIT; deliveredToday = DELIVERED with deliveredAt in the business day; topups.toCheck = PENDING requests (oldestWaitingAt = the oldest createdAt); approvedToday as in G14-02.
- **G14-02.** GET /admin/wallets lastTopupAt could mean the last approved or the last requested top-up (API_CONTRACT §7.8). approvedToday's day boundary (business day or calendar day) is stated only for costTakenTodayPaisa (§7.9, §7.13). **Settled:** GET /admin/wallets lastTopupAt = when the distributor's latest approved top-up was approved (completed_at of its newest SUCCESS payment), null if none; requests being checked or rejected don't count. approvedToday, in GET /admin/topups and GET /admin/summary alike, = SUCCESS requests whose approval time (completed_at) falls in the current business day (Asia/Karachi, 03:00 cut-off, businessDayRange), with the count and the sum of the credited amounts; the same boundary as costTakenTodayPaisa.
- **G14-03.** UX_ADMIN §1.2/§1.3: reports are 'hidden', but the docs don't say what the /reports address shows. **Settled:** As built by the admin-web foundation (app/router.tsx reportsRoute, NotFoundPage): /reports keeps the legacy Reports screen inside the new shell, office only, reachable only by typing its address: it is in no menu and has no module switch (there is no features.reports). Its figures come from the /reports/\* API, which stays office only and reads the ledger (ADR-04, API_CONTRACT §7.13). Any unknown path shows the built not-found page: "We couldn't find this page" / "The link may be old or mistyped." with "Go to Today". UX_ADMIN §1.2, §1.3 and ADR-04 already say this; the legacy-cleanup list and the API contract follow.

### API conventions, errors, files and idempotency

- **G15-01.** Idempotency storage gap: API_CONTRACT §7.4 (POST /clients) and §7.3 (POST /distributors) take an Idempotency-Key, and §4 (2) promises a 200 Idempotent-Replay, but DATA_MODEL §3.2 gives clients and distributors no client_request_id (§4 and §7 cover only orders, payments, refills and expenses). A retried 'Save customer' would probably come back as 409 CLIENT_PHONE_EXISTS (or USER_PHONE_IN_USE for a distributor) instead of a replay. **Settled:** Customers and distributors store the Idempotency-Key like orders and payments: POST /clients in clients.client_request_id (unique per distributor) and POST /distributors in distributors.client_request_id (unique), both nullable UUID columns added to inc1a. A retry with the same key is looked up before the phone rules run and answers 200 with Idempotent-Replay: true and the first resource (for a customer: the customer, its first address and today's price for it); the same key with different key fields (§4.2) gives 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A request without a key behaves as before (a repeat gets 409 CLIENT_PHONE_EXISTS or USER_PHONE_IN_USE), and the other office creates (drivers, vans, zones, stores, cities, cylinder types) store no key in the pilot.
- **G15-02.** API_CONTRACT §4: IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT compares 'the stored resource's key fields' without listing them per resource. Behaviour for a non-UUID key isn't stated (client_request_id is @db.Uuid). **Settled:** The Idempotency-Key must be a UUID, compared lower-cased; anything else gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with details.fields[0] {path 'Idempotency-Key', code INVALID_ID} (the built @IdempotencyKey decorator). It is stored only when the create commits, so a refused request leaves it free, and it is looked up right after authentication and body validation, before the route's other rules, so a retry gets the first resource even if the request would now be refused. A conflict is a stored key whose key fields differ from the request after the same normalisation as saving (null and absent equal, paisa by value, phones normalised, line sets order-free): POST /orders compares clientId, the delivery point (the address's pin or deliveryLocation, to 6 decimals) and lines {cylinderTypeId, fullCount, expectedReturnCount}; POST /payments/topup-requests amountPaisa, payerName, payerChannel; POST /filling-orders [Inc 3] fillingStationId, cylinderTypeId, requestedCount; POST /expenses expenseDate, amountPaisa, typeId, vehicleId, driverId; POST /clients name, phone; POST /distributors phone, businessName. Other fields are not compared, and corrections keep their own key adjust:\<Idempotency-Key> (§7.8).
- **G15-03.** Files (API_CONTRACT §5.8, §7.10): '5 MB' isn't defined (5,000,000 or 5,242,880 bytes). Not stated: the upload success status; the error a DISTRIBUTOR gets for purpose EXPENSE_RECEIPT ('office only'); the refusal code for GET /files/:id/url by someone who is neither the uploader nor the office (NOT_FOUND or FILE_NOT_FOUND); and whether the storage-key date is UTC or Karachi. **Settled:** 5 MB means 5,242,880 bytes (5 × 1024 × 1024, the built UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES): exactly that size is accepted and one byte more gives 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE {maxMb: 5}; checks run authentication (401) → roles (403) → rate limit (429) → size while the file streams in (413) → purpose value (400) → file missing (400 VALIDATION_FAILED on file) → purpose rule (403 PERMISSION_DENIED for EXPENSE_RECEIPT by a non-office caller, 400 VALIDATION_FAILED INVALID_CHOICE for DAY_END\_\*) → type by magic bytes (415 FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED, an empty file included), and a storage failure gives 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, all as built. POST /files/upload answers 201 {fileId, key, url, mimeType, size}, also when the same uploader re-sends the same bytes for the same purpose and the existing row comes back; GET /files/:id/url for anyone but the uploader or the office, or for an unknown or non-UUID id, gives 404 FILE_NOT_FOUND with the same body; storage keys use the UTC date, uploads/\<UTC yyyy-mm-dd>/\<uuid>.\<ext>. Across the API a POST that creates the record it returns answers 201 (its replay 200 with Idempotent-Replay), every other success answers 200 (actions sent as POST included), the public form POST /c/:token answers 303, and no route answers 204.
- **G15-04.** API_CONTRACT §2.3: several {{param}} templates have no documented details key: RATE_LIMITED {{minutes}}, ORDER_TOO_MANY_CYLINDERS {{max}}, ASSIGN_DRIVER_NOT_AVAILABLE/NO_VEHICLE {{driver}}, DISTRIBUTOR_CODE_IN_USE {{code}}, EXPENSE_TYPE_ARCHIVED {{name}}, SCAN_NOT_AT_STORE {{store}}, CASE_ALREADY_RESOLVED {{by}}. No machine-readable params list exists for the completeness test. **Settled:** The details keys of every code are defined in packages/shared-types/src/errors.ts: ErrorDetailsMap (types) and ERROR_DETAIL_KEYS (the runtime list the completeness test reads), with the built compile-time check that every {{param}} of ERROR_MESSAGE_EN is a documented key once Paisa is dropped. API_CONTRACT §2.3 gains a details table copied from it, naming the keys the gap lists: RATE_LIMITED minutes (whole minutes until the window resets, rounded up, at least 1, plus a Retry-After header in seconds), ORDER_TOO_MANY_CYLINDERS max, ASSIGN_DRIVER_NOT_AVAILABLE and ASSIGN_DRIVER_NO_VEHICLE driver (the driver's name), DISTRIBUTOR_CODE_IN_USE code, EXPENSE_TYPE\_\* name, SCAN_NOT_AT_STORE store (the store's name) and CASE_ALREADY_RESOLVED by (the closer's name). Any code may also carry currentStatus (§4.3) and scan refusals carry progress (§9.3); a key added anywhere in this contract is added to errors.ts in the same pull request.
- **G15-05.** SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (503, API_CONTRACT §2.3) has no documented trigger on any route. **Settled:** 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE means a dependency the request needs is down: the database can't be reached or times out (Prisma P1001, P1002, P1008, P1017, P2024, P2028, a client initialisation error, or SQLSTATE 57014), object storage refuses an upload, or an upstream answers 503; the raw cause goes only to the logs and Sentry, as the built error mapping does. It is retryable: apps retry GETs and the user repeats a mutation with the same Idempotency-Key. As built, a deadlock or serialization failure (P2034, SQLSTATE 40001 or 40P01) is 409 CONFLICT_STALE_STATE, a malformed id (P2023, SQLSTATE 22P02) is 404 like an unknown record, and Redis being down never fails a request.
- **G15-06.** 'Money is a string of digits' (API_CONTRACT §1.1) doesn't say how negative amounts are written (StatementItem.amountPaisa); '-48000' is assumed. **Settled:** A signed money field (StatementItem.amountPaisa, ledger amounts, any field documented as signed) is a digit string with a leading ASCII hyphen-minus for money out and no sign for money in or zero: '-48000', '500000', '0', as the built Paisa type and toPaisa accept; only formatRs turns it into '−Rs 480'. Request amounts are never negative: a negative or non-integer value gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (INVALID_AMOUNT or AMOUNT_TOO_SMALL, as the built paisaSchema does).
- **G15-07.** API_CONTRACT §1.3: behaviour for ?limit above 100 (refuse or clamp) is not stated. **Settled:** ?limit must be a whole number from 1 to 100 (default 30) and is never clamped: above 100 gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on limit with code TOO_LARGE {max: 100}, below 1 TOO_SMALL {min: 1}, and a non-number INVALID_TYPE or NOT_INTEGER, as the built pageQuerySchema does. A cursor this list didn't make gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on cursor (INVALID_VALUE), the cursor is base64url, and the legacy bare-array lists ignore both parameters.
- **G15-08.** API_CONTRACT §6 426 gate: the docs don't say which minVersion applies when X-App-Variant is missing (the installed 0.1.0 APK sends none), or whether /app/config and /health are exempt. **Settled:** The 426 gate takes the variant from X-App-Variant when it is driver or distributor; with no header or an unknown value the signed-in role decides (DRIVER → driver, DISTRIBUTOR → distributor), and admin-web, other roles and anonymous calls without the header are never gated, as the built AppVersionInterceptor does. A missing or unreadable X-App-Version counts as '0.1.0', versions compare as three numbers (0.10.0 > 0.9.3) with any -pre or +build suffix ignored, and GET /app/config, GET /health and GET /health/live are exempt.
- **G15-09.** API_CONTRACT §7.2 GET /health: the body shape and the status when the database is down are undocumented. Today's controller returns the raw DB error text. **Settled:** GET /health/live answers 200 {status: 'ok'} whenever the process runs (the deploy health check already uses it). GET /health runs SELECT 1 with a 2-second timeout and answers 200 {status: 'ok', environment, version, uptimeSeconds, checks: {database: {ok: true, latencyMs}}}, or 503 with the same shape, status 'degraded' and database.ok false. Neither body ever contains error text, connection details or NODE_ENV (environment is the APP_ENV value of /app/config); both are public and exempt from the 426 gate, and this 503 body is the one JSON error body that isn't the §2.1 envelope.

### Words, numbers and formats on screen

- **G16-01.** Money signs: API_CONTRACT §1.1 writes '−Rs 330', UX_MOBILE §2.2/§3.7 write '− Rs 330' and '+ Rs 5,000', and UX_ADMIN §1.6 writes '+Rs 5,000'. One formatRs can't produce both. FND-024 follows API_CONTRACT. **Settled:** formatRs writes the sign directly before 'Rs' with no space: '−Rs 330' (U+2212, money out) and, with sign 'always', '+Rs 5,000' (money in); zero is never signed. That is the API_CONTRACT §1.1 form and what the built shared-utils formatRs prints (UX_MOBILE §2.2/§3.7 and UX_ADMIN §1.6 already say so). Copy that writes its own '+ ' before an unsigned amount, such as the price panel's '+ Rs 40 per 11.8 kg cylinder', is copy, not a signed amount, and stays.
- **G16-02.** Order and cylinder numbers share one format: ADR-22, API_CONTRACT §1.1 and the README format orders (AG-0142) and cylinders (AG-0042) the same way from separate counters, so on a fresh setup order AG-0001 and cylinder AG-0001 look identical. 'Handed to Sana (AG-0001)' is ambiguous, the customer page's 'no cylinder numbers' rule (CUSTOMER_PAGE §3, §12) can't be tested with a pattern, and customers, testers and support calls can confuse the two (the blueprint's open question about AG-C0042). **Settled (a default; the owner may change it):** Cylinder numbers get their own form AG-C0042: formatNo(code, 'CYLINDER', n) = code + '-C' + n zero-padded to 4 digits (printed in full past 9999), while orders stay AG-0142, top-ups AG-T031 and refills AG-R007 (README and ADR-22 already say so). Typed cylinder numbers everywhere (driver and store scans, the office's manual delivery, Find cylinder, GET /cylinders/:code/history, the day-end sheet) go through one parseCylinderNo(text, distributorCode?) in shared-utils, which accepts '42', '0042', 'C0042' and 'AG-C0042' in any letter case, spaces ignored, Arabic-Indic or Urdu digits allowed, 1–6 digits with a value of at least 1, and returns { code, shortNo } or null. A written code must be the distributor in context (the run's for a driver scan, the caller's for the shop, the order's for the office's manual delivery); with no distributor in context (the office's Find cylinder and cylinder history) only the full AG-C0042 form or the QR value resolves, and anything else, including the order-style AG-0042 or another distributor's code, is SCAN_CYLINDER_UNKNOWN for a scan or 404 NOT_FOUND for a lookup. The owner can veto the form before labels are printed.
- **G16-03.** formatNo (ADR-22, API_CONTRACT §1.1): the kind names and the result past 9999 (AG-10000?) are not stated. **Settled:** formatNo(code, kind, n) has four kinds: ORDER (4 digits), TOPUP ('T' + 3), REFILL ('R' + 3) and CYLINDER ('C' + 4, G16-02). n must be a whole number ≥ 0 (else RangeError); it is zero-padded to the width and printed in full when longer (AG-10000, AG-T1000, AG-C10000) so numbers stay unique, and with no code only the part after the dash is returned, all as built apart from the C (ADR-22 already says so). Past 9999 the SMS still fits: order numbers up to ABCDEF-99999 are 12 characters, worst case 151 of 160 (CUSTOMER_PAGE §9 already says so).
- **G16-04.** Copy has no singular forms, although UX_MOBILE §3.3 says plurals use \_plural: UX_ADMIN §2.2 'Approved today: … · 3 top-ups', §2.3 '2 of 10 zones have no price', §2.1 '2 zones have no delivery price' and §4.3 'Approve {{n}} fixes and lock the day'; UX_MOBILE S20 '{{n}} differences' and 'Send for approval ({{n}} differences)', and §7.3 S15 '{{n}} customer problems'; and the driver strings TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY, VEHICLE_HAS_CYLINDERS, '{{count}} scans are not saved' and 'Trip · {{count}} customers'. **Settled:** Every UI string that shows a count has a singular and a plural form and takes the count as 'count': the apps use i18next v3 keys key / key_plural (compatibilityJSON 'v3', as built) and the website i18next 23 keys key_one / key_other (UX_MOBILE §3.3 and UX_ADMIN §1.6 already say so, with the driver, shop, Today, top-up, prices and expenses strings). Error texts stay one English string per code (ERROR_MESSAGE_EN), so every counted one is reworded to read right for any count: RATE_LIMITED 'Too many tries. Please wait {{minutes}} min and try again.', ORDER_TOO_MANY_CYLINDERS 'Too many cylinders. An order can have at most {{max}}.', LOAD_INCOMPLETE 'Load every cylinder first: {{done}} of {{total}} loaded so far.', VEHICLE_HAS_CYLINDERS 'This van still has cylinders on it ({{count}}). Unload at the store first.', TOPUP_TOO_MANY_PENDING 'Top-ups being checked: {{count}}. Wait for them before sending another.', REFILL_TOO_MANY 'Too many cylinders. A refill can have at most {{max}}.', REFILL_COUNT_REACHED 'All picked up: {{requested}} of {{requested}}.' (TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY in G16-05); params are unchanged. The website strings still missing a singular get one: the unsaved-settings bar, the vans message and the day-end approve button and dialog. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G16-05.** TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY wording differs: ERROR_MESSAGE_EN (API_CONTRACT §2.3) says 'The store still needs to scan in {{count}} cylinders from your van.', while UX_MOBILE §7.2 R3 says 'The shop still needs to receive {{count}} cylinders from your van.' **Settled:** API_CONTRACT wins: the driver app shows TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY as errors.TRIP_VAN_NOT_EMPTY, the one catalogue text, worded for any count (G16-04) as 'The store must scan in {{count}} more from your van.', which UX_MOBILE §5 and §7.2 R3 quote instead of their own wording. (Words updated by the simple-UX pass, 2026-10-23.)
- **G16-06.** Correction reason labels differ: UX_ADMIN §2.6 'Charged by a system error' vs UX_MOBILE §3.4 wallet.correction.SYSTEM_ERROR 'System error'. **Settled:** The office keeps one set of reason words on the website (Top-up approved by mistake · System error · Bank reversed a top-up · Opening balance · Other), so its reason select and history say 'System error', never 'Charged by a system error'. Since the simple-UX pass (2026-10-23) the shop app shows its own words for two of them, 'Top-up added by mistake' and 'Mistake fixed', and no label for Other (UX_MOBILE §3.4, UX_ADMIN §2.6); the stored reason codes are the same in both apps.
- **G16-07.** Phone formats: UX_MOBILE S1 shows '0300 1234567', while UX_ADMIN §1.5 PhoneInput shows '+92 300 1234567'. No shared-utils formatter (formatPkPhone or similar) is named in any doc for the display form or the SMS form '03001234567'; the API_CONTRACT intro lists only normalizePkPhone. **Settled:** formatPkPhone(phone, style) in shared-utils is the one phone formatter: 'local' (the default) '0300 1234567' in the shop and driver apps and on the customer page, 'international' '+92 300 1234567' everywhere on the website (both built), and a new 'compact' '03001234567' for SMS text; a number that isn't a Pakistani mobile prints as stored. tel: links use the E.164 value (tel:+923001234567) and wa.me links its digits without the plus (923001234567). UX_MOBILE S1, UX_ADMIN §1.5 and CUSTOMER_PAGE §6 and §9 already say so.
- **G16-08.** normalizePkPhone's accepted input forms are not documented (00 92 prefix, spaces, dashes, '3001234567'). Today's phone.ts returns null for '00923001234567'. **Settled:** normalizePkPhone (built) returns '+923XXXXXXXXX' for a Pakistani mobile written as 0300 1234567, 300 1234567, +92 300 1234567, 92 300 1234567 or 0092 300 1234567, with spaces, dashes, dots or brackets, in ASCII, Arabic-Indic or Urdu digits, and drops a stray 0 after the country code (+92 0300 1234567); landlines, other countries, letters and wrong lengths give null. The inc1a SQL backfill (built) accepts the same ASCII forms except the stray-zero form and non-ASCII digits, which it leaves as typed and flags with client.phone_needs_fix like any other unfixable number.
- **G16-09.** UX_MOBILE §3.3: formatWhen doesn't say whether 'Today/Yesterday' uses the calendar day or the 03:00 business day, or how other years are shown. **Settled:** formatWhen (built) uses the Asia/Karachi calendar day, not the 03:00 business day: 'Today, 4:12 pm' and 'Yesterday, 9:05 am' by calendar date, otherwise 'Mon 19 Oct, 4:12 pm', with the year added when it differs from now's year ('Sun 19 Oct 2025, 4:12 pm'); a later time today still reads 'Today'. Day headings (formatDayLabel) follow the same rule, while business-day screens (day-end, 'done today') use businessDate; UX_MOBILE §3.3 already says so, so no doc changes.

### Data model, migrations and environments

- **G17-01.** Opening entries: ADR-11 says 'no ledger history behind it'; DATA_MODEL §3.4 backfill 7 says 'cached balance differs from the ledger sum'. They give different results for partial history and for negative gaps. **Settled:** The DATA_MODEL rule, as built in inc1a, is the rule (ADR-11 already says so): each distributor whose cached balance differs from its ledger sum (no history, or only part of it) gets one ADJUSTMENT row with reason OPENING_BALANCE, amount = balance − ledger sum (negative when the old history adds up to more, never 0), balance_after_paisa = the cached balance and key opening:\<distributorId>, plus one wallet.opening_entry audit row; a distributor whose history already adds up gets none. Afterwards the ledger sum equals the balance; a negative cached balance is left to the inc1b pre-check, which asks for an office correction.
- **G17-02.** Post-migration invariants: DATA_MODEL §7 is the constraint-to-API mapping table. The invariants the migration cases check (codes and counters, ledger sum = balance, expense type_id, E.164 phones or flagged, the six expense types, backfills safe to re-run, the pre-check) are spread over §2.4, §3.4 and §3.5. No single invariants list exists to test against. **Settled:** DATA_MODEL gets a §3.8 'Post-migration invariants', a numbered list (inc1a items 1–16, inc1b items 17–20) that the MIG cases assert by number and ops re-checks on a restored copy of live before the prod deploy (the §2.4 checklist already points to it); §7 stays the constraint-to-API table. The list only writes down rules already in §2.4, §3.4 and §3.5 (plus backfill 12 from G17-03), with the built pre-check prefix 'MIGRATION_BLOCKED inc1a:'; the inc1b pre-checks run in a fixed order and the first failure stops the file.
- **G17-03.** Alert rules: API_CONTRACT §7.2 says existing DISTRIBUTOR_CREDIT_OVER rules are deactivated, but no migration or release step in DATA_MODEL §3.4 does it. **Settled:** inc1a deactivates existing DISTRIBUTOR_CREDIT_OVER rules with backfill 12, UPDATE alert_rules SET is_active = false, updated_at = now() WHERE rule_kind = 'DISTRIBUTOR_CREDIT_OVER' AND is_active (safe to re-run); if inc1a has already reached a shared database, the same statement ships in inc1b step 2 instead. The alert evaluator never runs that kind, creating such a rule or setting one active gives 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, and the enum value stays until the post-pilot contract migration.
- **G17-04.** API_CONTRACT §3.6/§3.7: only BULLMQ_PREFIX must carry the environment name. Rate-limit keys on the shared staging/prod Redis have no required prefix. 'Environment name' doesn't say NODE_ENV or APP_ENV. **Settled:** The environment name is the deployment name the built boot guard uses: APP_ENV when set, else derived from NODE_ENV (production, staging or test, else development), and BULLMQ_PREFIX must contain it or a listed alias (production/prod, staging/stage/stg, training/train, development/dev, test), for example sf-prod and sf-staging. Every Redis key the API writes starts with BULLMQ_PREFIX: the BullMQ queues and the rate-limit counters (\<BULLMQ_PREFIX>:rl:\<rule>:\<first 32 hex of sha256(identity)>:\<window start>, as built), so staging and production on the shared Redis never share counters and no phone number or IP is stored in clear.
- **G17-05.** DATA_MODEL §2.6 names snapshot restore as the rollback, but no drill, schedule, RPO/RTO or storage-bucket backup is documented. **Settled:** Pilot backup targets (DATA_MODEL §2.6 already states them): the production database uses the provider's automated daily backups with point-in-time recovery, kept 7 days, plus the snapshot before every migration deploy; data loss is at most 5 minutes with point-in-time recovery (24 hours if only daily snapshots exist), the API is back on a restored database within 4 hours, and staging keeps 3 days. The uploads bucket has versioning on, with old versions kept 30 days. A restore drill (restore into a scratch database on the test server, run prisma migrate status and the nightly wallet check, compare counts, open a stored picture, record the restore time and the data-loss window) runs before the Inc 1 switch-over and before the first production deploy of each later increment's migration, and a failed drill blocks that deploy.
